title: Bug: app terminated for excessive memory around shared-Margin podcast → native-text playback
body:
## Summary

Spoken Margins was terminated for excessive memory during a listening session that transitioned from a podcast with shared Margins to a native-text item. The native-text item then triggered another termination a few minutes into playback after relaunch. A third attempt appears to be working.

This is a repeated real-device memory-pressure/termination report. The transition from shared-Margin podcast playback to native text is part of the observed sequence, but the root cause is not yet established.

## Observed sequence

1. Listen to a podcast with shared Margins active/present.
2. While in that session, tap/open a native-text item.
3. Spoken Margins is terminated for using too much memory.
4. Relaunch the app.
5. Start playing the same native-text item.
6. A few minutes into native-text playback, the app is again terminated for excessive memory.
7. Relaunch a third time and play the item again.
8. Third attempt currently appears to work.

## Affected native-text item

**Title:** Spoken Margins AI Handoff: The Astra+Sol Thread Workflow for Coding  
**Source:** https://x.com/kevinkern/status/2099247371309678940?s=20

Session state supplied with the report:

- Status: `in_progress`
- Completion: 51%
- Listening Map chapters:
  - The Astra+Sol Thread Workflow for Coding — 0%
  - Prompt — 17%
  - Tips — 49%
  - Code Output — 77%
  - Conclusion — 93%

## Expected behavior

- Moving from a podcast with shared Margins to a native-text item must not cause unbounded retained memory or a jetsam/excess-memory termination.
- Native-text playback should remain memory-bounded over time, including while preparation/rendering, Listening Map state, imported/shared Margin state, and prior-item playback state coexist.
- Leaving the previous podcast/session should release resources that are no longer required.
- Relaunching and replaying the same native-text item should not repeatedly approach the process memory limit.

## Investigation / hypotheses to falsify

These are investigation targets, not established causes:

1. Shared-Margin/imported-commentary state or media resources from the previous podcast remain retained after switching items.
2. Native-text rendering/preparation retains model/runtime, audio chunks, decoded buffers, or task graphs longer than intended.
3. Item transition temporarily holds both the podcast/shared-Margin playback graph and native-text playback/render graph at full size.
4. Listening Map / chapter / summary presentation state is retained or duplicated during playback updates.
5. Repeated SwiftUI/model projections or caches grow monotonically during native-text playback.
6. A failed/terminated first attempt leaves durable state that changes memory behavior on subsequent launches.

## Required diagnostics

On a physical device, reproduce the transition and capture:

- process resident/physical footprint over time;
- allocation growth grouped by major subsystem/type;
- retain cycles / objects whose counts grow across item transition and playback;
- native-text renderer/model load and unload events;
- prepared-audio/chunk cache ownership and in-memory buffer sizes;
- imported/shared-Margin player and model teardown when leaving the podcast;
- Listening Map/resource cache sizes before and after the transition;
- iOS termination/jetsam evidence if available;
- memory warnings and app response before termination.

Prefer IDs/counts/sizes/timing in diagnostics rather than logging private source or Margin text.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The reported podcast-with-shared-Margins → native-text transition is exercised on a physical device with memory instrumentation.
- [ ] The dominant source(s) of memory growth/retention are identified from evidence rather than inferred from the termination alone.
- [ ] Leaving the podcast/shared-Margin item releases playback and presentation resources that are no longer needed.
- [ ] Native-text playback and preparation reach a bounded steady-state footprint for this item rather than growing continuously.
- [ ] Repeating the transition and then playing the native-text item for a representative period does not produce an excessive-memory termination.
- [ ] Repeated open/play/leave cycles do not show monotonic retained-memory growth.
- [ ] Regression coverage or a repeatable profiling procedure is recorded for this specific cross-item transition.
- [ ] Product-owner real-device validation confirms the original workflow no longer terminates the app.

## Related

- #93 — loaded Item/Timeline performance and shared-Margin presentation under realistic app load.
- #64 — durable prepared native-text audio, renderer lifecycle, termination/relaunch, and physical-resource evidence.
- #18 — imported/shared Margin listening layer lifecycle and playback behavior.

## Priority

High reliability issue: repeated OS termination during ordinary listening/playback.

title: Feature: hands-free Watch gestures for starting and ending a Margin
body:
User testing requests hands-free or minimal-interaction Margin capture while listening: a supported finger double-tap gesture, or a wrist-raise interaction if feasible, without taking out or unlocking the phone.

This is a gesture/interaction feasibility follow-up to #96 (Watch-owned capture) and #75 (untethered Watch sync), not a request to remotely start the locked iPhone microphone. Prefer local Watch recording with durable queued transfer to the phone later. Implementation is deferred.

Investigate supported watchOS APIs and hardware/OS restrictions before promising any gesture. Distinguish system double-tap, accessibility gestures, and wrist raise; do not assume third-party background gesture access. Provide a large on-screen/complication fallback on unsupported hardware. Establish explicit start/stop feedback, accidental activation protection, and cancellation.

Acceptance evidence should include supported and unsupported Watch models, locked/pocketed phone, AirPods and Watch microphone routing, disconnected capture and eventual duplicate-safe transfer, preserved source anchor, retry/relaunch recovery, and false-positive gesture testing while walking. Report unavailable triggers honestly. Capture remains private and local; no AI subscription or paid offering required.

title: Process: Generate onboarding screen recordings as a beta-release QA gate
body:
## Goal

For beta releases, generate a small set of polished screen-recorded walkthroughs that serve two purposes:

1. Give users concise onboarding material for common Spoken Margins workflows.
2. Act as a final QA pass that verifies those workflows still match the current UI/UX.

## Proposed process

Before a beta is considered ready, record end-to-end walkthroughs of key user journeys using the current build. Add narrated audio, potentially rendered with a voice such as Chatterbox, and publish or bundle the resulting videos wherever onboarding/help content lives.

The important constraint is that these should be regenerated or explicitly revalidated for each beta rather than treated as static marketing assets. If a walkthrough can no longer be recorded cleanly because the UI changed, that is useful release feedback.

## Initial walkthrough set

- Add/follow a podcast from Spotify.
- Add/follow a podcast from Apple Podcasts.
- Add an article to Spoken Margins.
- Create a margin/interjection during playback.
- Share a margin.
- Any other core workflow we consider essential for a first-time beta user.

## QA value

Treat recording each walkthrough as a lightweight release acceptance test:

- The documented path is still available.
- Labels, controls, and navigation match the narration/onboarding copy.
- The flow can be completed without unexplained dead ends or workarounds.
- Permission prompts and external-app handoffs behave as expected.
- The final recording reflects the UI shipping in that beta.

If a workflow has materially changed, update both the recording and any associated onboarding/help copy before release.

## Automation opportunities

Longer term, make this as reproducible as practical:

- Maintain a canonical checklist/script for each walkthrough.
- Use stable demo content/accounts where possible.
- Render narration from version-controlled scripts (for example with Chatterbox or another TTS voice).
- Stamp recordings with the app/build version so stale assets are identifiable.
- Consider storing scripts and/or recording metadata in the repo so UI changes can trigger a documentation review.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A canonical list of beta onboarding walkthroughs exists.
- [ ] Each required walkthrough has a current screen recording for the beta build.
- [ ] Narration/captions describe the actual UI shown in the recording.
- [ ] Core external-source flows (including Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and article import) are represented.
- [ ] Sharing a margin is represented.
- [ ] Recording the walkthroughs is included in the beta release checklist / QA process.
- [ ] Any mismatch found while producing the recordings is resolved or explicitly tracked before release.
- [ ] Assets are versioned or otherwise identifiable as belonging to a specific release/build.

title: Feature: opt-in headphone remote shortcut for bookmarks
body:
## Goal

Let a listener create a Spoken Margins bookmark from headphones without taking the phone out, using an **explicitly opt-in remapping of a supported remote media command** while Spoken Margins owns Now Playing.

This builds on #117's lightweight Bookmark capture path. It must not introduce a second bookmark model or require the app to detect raw AirPods touch gestures that iOS does not expose to media apps.

## Platform boundary

Headphones and other external accessories deliver media commands through the system remote-command path. Spoken Margins can register handlers through `MPRemoteCommandCenter`, but it should reason about the resulting media command (play/pause, skip forward, next track, etc.), not assume it can observe a particular physical tap/press sequence on every headset.

Apple also exposes a dedicated `bookmarkCommand`; support that canonical command wherever the system/accessory presents it. For common headphones that do not emit a bookmark command, this feature may optionally reinterpret one user-selected supported transport command as Bookmark while Spoken Margins is the active Now Playing app.

## Product behavior

- Default: **Off**. Existing headphone transport behavior remains unchanged.
- Settings exposes an explicit option such as **Headphone Bookmark Shortcut**.
- The user chooses from only commands the app can reliably receive and distinguish on the current playback stack.
- A candidate initial mapping is **Skip Forward → Bookmark** or another low-risk command selected through product testing. Do not silently steal Play/Pause or another command by default.
- If the user chooses a command that normally performs another action, clearly state that this command will create a bookmark instead while the option is enabled and Spoken Margins is Now Playing.
- Executing the shortcut creates the same canonical bookmark as #117 and leaves source playback uninterrupted unless the remapped command itself must be consumed to prevent its ordinary transport action.
- Disabling the setting immediately restores ordinary media-command behavior.

The UI may explain how a user can configure their headset's own gesture settings to emit the chosen media command, but Spoken Margins should not claim control over AirPods gesture configuration it does not own.

## Command handling

- Register the remapped command only while the feature is enabled and Spoken Margins is an eligible active Now Playing session.
- Route the event to #117's single Bookmark capture service.
- Return the appropriate remote-command result so the system does not also perform the original skip/track action after a successful bookmark.
- Do not change playback position, rate, selected source, voice/runtime, or session identity as a side effect of bookmark capture.
- When Spoken Margins is not the active Now Playing app, do not intercept another app's headset behavior.
- Treat duplicate delivery/retry of one command event idempotently according to #117 while preserving two deliberate successive bookmark gestures.

## Settings / discoverability

The setting should communicate behavior in terms the system actually exposes, for example:

- Off
- Use Skip Forward as Bookmark
- Use Next Track as Bookmark

Only expose mappings that are genuinely supported by the app's current remote-command implementation. If hardware-specific behavior varies, state that the headset must be configured to send the selected media command rather than listing unsupported gesture guarantees.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The shortcut is disabled by default and ordinary headphone controls are unchanged until the user opts in.
- [ ] On a supported physical headset, a user-selected remote command creates a #117 bookmark without taking the phone out or opening Spoken Margins.
- [ ] A successful bookmark shortcut does not also perform the original skip/next action.
- [ ] Bookmark capture does not pause, restart, seek, change rate, switch voice/runtime, or replace the active source.
- [ ] Disabling the feature restores the original remote-command behavior immediately.
- [ ] Spoken Margins does not intercept the selected command while another app owns Now Playing.
- [ ] The UI describes the remapped **media command**, not an unsupported guarantee about raw AirPods tap counts.
- [ ] `MPRemoteCommandCenter.bookmarkCommand`, when delivered by the system/accessory, routes through the same canonical bookmark service without requiring a remap.
- [ ] Physical-device validation covers at least AirPods plus one other supported remote-control path (Lock Screen/Control Center or another headset) and records which media command each device actually emits.
- [ ] Repeated intentional shortcut uses create distinct bookmarks while duplicate event delivery does not.

## Related

- #117 — canonical lightweight Bookmark model, Lock Screen/Live Activity capture, deferred context enrichment.
- Existing remote transport correctness issues remain authoritative for Now Playing state; this feature must not regress play/pause/skip synchronization.

## Non-goals

- Detecting arbitrary raw AirPods taps/presses independently of the system media command they generate.
- Changing the user's AirPods settings from Spoken Margins.
- Enabling the remap without explicit user consent.
- Reserving a global hardware gesture when Spoken Margins is not the active media app.

title: Feature: lightweight bookmarks with Lock Screen / Live Activity capture
body:
## Goal

Add a lightweight **Bookmark** action that records the listener's current source position without interrupting playback, then retains or derives enough surrounding context to make the bookmark useful later.

A bookmark is intentionally cheaper than an interjection: it captures **“remember this point”** rather than taking over the audio session for recording or conversation.

## Desired experience

- Provide a simple bookmark icon during active playback, including the Live Activity / Lock Screen experience where supported.
- Tapping Bookmark must not pause, seek, restart, duck, or otherwise take over source playback.
- The immediate operation should be fast enough to use while walking or with the phone locked.
- Repeated bookmarks are allowed; they should remain distinct unless they are exact duplicate command deliveries that need idempotent suppression.
- Bookmarks should later be visible in an appropriate item/session/Margins context with a route back to the anchored source position.

Current ActivityKit supports Live Activity actions through `LiveActivityIntent`; use a system-supported interaction rather than requiring the user to unlock and foreground Spoken Margins solely to capture the bookmark.

## Capture contract

Persist the smallest durable record first:

- stable bookmark ID;
- item/source revision ID;
- canonical playback/source position available at command time;
- media timestamp where meaningful;
- chapter/section identity where available;
- creation time;
- capture provenance (in-app, Live Activity, remote command, etc.);
- enrichment state.

The bookmark must be considered saved once this minimal record is durably committed. Context enrichment is secondary and must not be able to erase the captured position.

## Context enrichment

Reuse the same durable source-anchor/context machinery used by interjections where practical, without pretending a bookmark is an interjection.

When immediately available, retain a bounded amount of source context around the bookmark position sufficient for recognition and later anchor repair. Do not copy excessive source text merely because it is locally available.

If the device is locked, the extension/action execution context cannot safely or reliably perform full enrichment, or required source context is temporarily unavailable:

1. save the canonical position/timestamp immediately;
2. mark the bookmark as needing enrichment;
3. later derive the surrounding source anchors/context from the retained item/source revision;
4. preserve the original capture time and position separately from any later enrichment time.

A failed enrichment attempt must leave a usable timestamp/source-position bookmark rather than deleting or hiding it.

## Remote/system integration

Apple's MediaPlayer framework exposes `MPRemoteCommandCenter.bookmarkCommand` specifically for remembering the current media item. Where appropriate, register a handler that routes the system bookmark command into this same canonical Bookmark capture path rather than implementing a second bookmark model.

The Live Activity action, in-app action, and any remote-command action must converge on the same idempotent bookmark service and anchor semantics.

## Playback and concurrency requirements

- Capturing a bookmark does not change `isPlaying`, current position, playback rate, selected voice/runtime, or active source.
- Capture during partially rendered native text must anchor to the canonical source position, not merely an unstable temporary chunk offset.
- A bookmark command arriving near a seek/interjection boundary must use a clearly defined snapshot of canonical playback state.
- Duplicate delivery/retry of the same action identifier must not create accidental duplicate bookmarks.
- Bookmark persistence must not wait for transcription, AI, network access, or full context extraction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] While audio is playing, tapping Bookmark creates a durable bookmark without audible interruption or playback-state change.
- [ ] The Live Activity / Lock Screen presentation exposes a clear bookmark action on supported OS versions and can save a bookmark without requiring the user to navigate through the app UI.
- [ ] A saved bookmark records the correct item/source revision and canonical position even if contextual enrichment is deferred.
- [ ] Deferred enrichment later attaches bounded before/after context and durable anchor evidence without changing the original capture position/time.
- [ ] Failed or unavailable enrichment leaves the timestamp/source-position bookmark intact and visibly usable.
- [ ] Native audio, podcast, prepared native text, and partially prepared native text use the correct canonical coordinate space.
- [ ] In-app, Live Activity, and `MPRemoteCommandCenter.bookmarkCommand` capture paths create equivalent canonical Bookmark records.
- [ ] Duplicate command delivery is idempotent while two deliberate nearby bookmarks remain distinct.
- [ ] Relaunch preserves bookmark identity, position, enrichment state, and context.
- [ ] Opening a bookmark returns to the intended source position within the existing seek/anchor tolerances.
- [ ] Product-owner validates bookmark capture while the phone is unlocked, locked, and actively playing through headphones.

## Related

- Existing interjection/source-anchor machinery should be reused for context and position evidence, but Bookmark remains a separate lightweight capture type.
- #64 — native-text durable source/media mapping.
- #112 — coordinate-space correctness for assistant/source targets; bookmarks must retain the actual target being heard.

## Non-goals

- Recording audio or opening an interjection flow.
- Requiring AI processing before a bookmark is saved.
- Copying large copyrighted excerpts as bookmark context.
- Treating a timestamp alone as sufficient when stronger local source anchors are available later.

title: Feature: show native-text render frontier on the playback scrubber
body:
## Goal

Show how much of a native-text item has actually been rendered/prepared directly on the playback timeline, using a subtle buffer-style indicator similar to the loaded/buffered region on a media scrubber.

The purpose is to let the listener understand at a glance how far ahead prepared audio exists without adding another status label or forcing them into a preparation screen.

## Desired experience

For native-text/PDF/other synthesized-text playback that is still being prepared:

- keep the ordinary playback scrubber as the primary position control;
- add a thin secondary line/track immediately above, below, or visually integrated with the scrubber;
- the secondary track represents the contiguous portion of the item for which compatible audio has been successfully rendered and committed;
- do not require percentage text, labels, or a separate progress card;
- update the indicator as preparation advances;
- once the entire item is prepared, the indicator may simply span the whole track or visually collapse into the completed state if that is clearer.

The listener must be able to distinguish **current playback position** from **rendered/prepared frontier**. The UI must not make a partially rendered item look fully buffered.

## Data authority

The indicator should be derived from the same durable prepared-audio state owned by #64, not from transient task/spinner state.

- Count only compatible, successfully committed audio/chunks as rendered.
- Do not advance the visible frontier merely because a chunk has been queued or synthesis has started.
- If reliable fractional progress within an in-flight chunk is unavailable, stop the indicator at the last committed boundary rather than inventing precision.
- Voice/source/model invalidation must immediately recompute or reset the frontier from the currently valid render manifest.
- Relaunch should reconstruct the same visible frontier from durable state.

For items whose canonical duration is not yet safely known, map committed preparation onto the stable source/chunk coordinate space rather than fabricating a playable media duration. This feature must not weaken #64's rule against advertising unsupported whole-item media seeking.

## Interaction behavior

- The render indicator is informational; it must not steal touch handling from the scrubber.
- Scrubbing inside already prepared media should behave normally.
- Scrubbing or jumping beyond the prepared frontier should follow the canonical preparation/buffering behavior from #64/#73; this issue does not authorize silent voice/runtime switching.
- The visual should remain legible with Dynamic Type, accessibility contrast settings, and both light/dark appearance without making the timeline visually noisy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A partially prepared multi-chunk native-text item displays a distinct rendered/prepared region on or adjacent to the playback scrubber.
- [ ] The current playback position and the rendered frontier are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] The frontier advances only when compatible audio becomes durably committed; queued/in-flight work does not falsely appear ready.
- [ ] Preparation progress survives relaunch and matches the #64 durable manifest.
- [ ] Changing source text, voice, or render signature cannot leave stale rendered progress visible.
- [ ] A fully prepared item shows a complete prepared region without requiring explanatory text.
- [ ] The indicator does not interfere with scrub gestures or worsen the scrubber regressions tracked elsewhere.
- [ ] Seeking beyond the rendered frontier uses the existing explicit preparation/buffering behavior and never silently changes voice/runtime.
- [ ] Product-owner validation confirms the indicator is understandable without a label on representative short and long native-text items.

## Related

- #64 — durable prepared native-text audio and authoritative render manifest.
- #73 — preparation horizon and reprioritization policy.
- #98 — preparation-stall/recovery seam.
- #84 — scrubber interaction/synchronization work; this visual must not take touch ownership.

## Non-goals

- Adding another textual percentage/status row.
- Fabricating whole-item media duration for an incomplete representation.
- Changing preparation scheduling policy.
- Making unrendered audio seekable by pretending it has already been prepared.

title: UI/UX: show Skim destination before skipping
body:
## Goal

When Skim is available, show the user **where Skim will take them before they activate it** so they can judge how much content they are about to skip.

The current affordance communicates that Skim advances playback, but not the magnitude of the jump. The user needs a concrete destination such as a timestamp and/or source-relative percentage before committing.

## Desired behavior

Wherever a Skim action is exposed, present enough destination information to answer: **“How far forward will this move me?”**

Useful representations include:

- destination timestamp, e.g. `Skim to 18:42`;
- destination percentage, e.g. `Skim to 37%`;
- optionally the delta when useful, e.g. `+6:15` or `+12%`;
- for native text or other non-time-native sources, the canonical source-relative percentage/position when a stable media timestamp is unavailable.

Prefer a compact presentation that does not make Skim look like the ordinary fixed-time skip controls.

## Product contract

- The displayed destination must be computed from the **same canonical Skim target** that activation will use.
- The preview must update if the current playhead or Listening Map changes enough to change the target.
- Do not estimate from a generic fixed interval if Skim actually uses semantic/chapter/map boundaries.
- If no valid forward Skim target exists, do not display a misleading destination.
- If only an approximate mapping is available, label/present it as approximate rather than implying exactness.

## Surfaces

Apply this consistently anywhere Skim can be triggered, including at minimum:

- the in-app playback surface;
- Live Activity / compact external playback surfaces where platform space permits.

Accessibility text should expose the destination as part of the control meaning, e.g. “Skim forward to 18 minutes 42 seconds, 37 percent.”

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Before activating Skim, the user can see the destination timestamp and/or source-relative percentage.
- [ ] The shown destination matches the position actually reached after activation within the precision of the source/media mapping.
- [ ] The preview changes when a different Skim target becomes active.
- [ ] Semantic Skim remains visually and behaviorally distinct from ordinary fixed-time skip controls.
- [ ] Sources without a stable time mapping still expose a meaningful canonical position such as percentage.
- [ ] Invalid/unavailable Skim targets do not show stale or fabricated destination values.
- [ ] VoiceOver announces the destination clearly before activation.
- [ ] Regression coverage verifies preview/activation agreement at multiple playhead positions and after Listening Map changes.
- [ ] Product-owner validation confirms that the UI makes it obvious how much content will be skipped before tapping Skim.

## Related

- #90 — Skim semantics, state, accessibility meaning, and capability rules.
- #100 — visual integration/polish of Skim controls on playback and Live Activity.

## Non-goal

This issue does not redefine how the Skim target itself is selected. It makes the already-selected target legible to the user before they commit to the jump.

title: Feature/App Request: Spoken Margins Unplugged — verifiably local-only edition
body:
## Summary

Create a separate **Spoken Margins Unplugged** app/target: a one-time-purchase, local-first edition of Spoken Margins that makes **no requests to Spoken Margins servers or third-party analytics/AI/telemetry services** and keeps listening history, interjections, transcripts, Listening Maps, summaries, and generated audio on-device.

The goal is not merely an "offline mode" toggle inside the connected app. The trust proposition depends on shipping a **separate binary with a separate Bundle ID and App Store listing** so users can independently verify that the Unplugged edition has minimal permissions, minimal data collection, and no developer-controlled data plane.

## Product promise

> Spoken Margins Unplugged works without a Spoken Margins account or backend. It may contact only source locations needed to retrieve content explicitly requested by the user (for example RSS feeds, podcast media/CDN URLs, chapter/transcript resources referenced by those feeds, and webpages the user imports). It does not contact Spoken Margins servers, analytics providers, ad networks, remote AI providers, or telemetry services.

The app should remain useful even if Spoken Margins as a company/service disappears.

## Why a separate app instead of a setting

A server-capable binary can promise that a mode is offline, but users still have to trust that dormant networking paths stay dormant. For the privacy-first product, the absence of those capabilities should be externally observable:

- separate App Store SKU / Bundle ID
- App Store privacy label consistent with **Data Not Collected**, if the final implementation legitimately qualifies under Apple's definitions
- no account system
- no analytics SDK
- no crash/telemetry SDK that sends data off-device
- no ad SDK
- no remote AI SDK/client
- no Spoken Margins service endpoints linked into the target
- no Connected-only package in the target's dependency/link graph

This should be a thin app target over the same shared local engine, **not a forked codebase**.

## Core capabilities

Unplugged should preserve the core Spoken Margins value proposition locally:

- RSS/public podcast intake and native audio playback
- article/web intake where the user explicitly requests the source
- pasted text / Markdown / Obsidian / supported local files
- text-based PDF intake
- listener interjections anchored to source position/context
- local/on-device interjection transcription
- installed/on-device TTS
- publisher chapters / deterministic Listening Maps
- on-device transcript/map generation where supported and practical
- on-device summaries where supported
- local search/indexing where supported
- session export / AI handoff to a chatbot chosen by the user
- pasted assistant-response import, playback, and further interjection

No Connected-only features should silently degrade into remote calls.

## Explicit non-goals for Unplugged

These belong in the connected Spoken Margins product, not Unplugged:

- Spoken Margins account or cloud sync
- book clubs / shared margins
- server-generated TTS
- server-side transcription
- server Listening Map generation
- server summaries
- in-app remote AI conversation
- compute-credit marketplace / cooperative processing
- analytics / telemetry
- advertising

## Verifiability requirements

The privacy claim should be **falsifiable by the user**, not just stated in a privacy policy.

### 1. Apple App Privacy Report

Document a supported verification flow:

1. Enable iOS App Privacy Report.
2. Use Spoken Margins Unplugged normally.
3. Inspect its network activity.
4. Expected domains should correspond only to sources the user requested or resources referenced by those sources.
5. There should never be Spoken Margins backend domains, analytics, ad, telemetry, or remote AI providers.

The product should explicitly tell users that Apple's report is the independent source of truth.

### 2. Local Privacy Ledger

Provide an optional on-device network/activity ledger that explains each outbound source request, e.g.:

- `feeds.example.com` — RSS feed requested by user
- `cdn.example.com` — episode audio referenced by that feed
- `publisher.example.org` — article imported by user

It should also show:

- Spoken Margins services: **None**
- Analytics: **None**
- Account: **None**
- Cloud AI: **None**

The UI must state that this local ledger is informative, not independent proof, and point users to Apple's App Privacy Report for verification.

### 3. Build-time privacy boundary

Add automated checks for the Unplugged target that fail the build/release if prohibited dependencies or endpoints appear.

Examples:

- reject known Connected-only package/module imports
- reject fixed Spoken Margins service hostnames
- reject analytics/telemetry SDKs
- inspect target entitlements/privacy manifests
- enumerate linked frameworks

Prefer a composition root where Unplugged has no implementation of a remote service client at all, rather than a runtime `connectedMode = false` flag.

### 4. Public verification tooling without open-sourcing the product

Investigate publishing a small public privacy-verification repository containing only the trust boundary, such as:

- Unplugged network-origin policy
- allowed-source rules
- target entitlements / privacy manifest expectations
- static-analysis scripts that scan an exported app/archive for prohibited frameworks/domains
- reproducible instructions for inspecting network behavior
- release-by-release audit reports

Do **not** require open-sourcing the main Spoken Margins implementation to satisfy this feature.

### 5. Independent audit

Before broad release, consider a third-party mobile security/privacy review of the Unplugged target. Publish a concise report covering:

- outbound networking paths
- embedded SDKs
- permissions / entitlements
- developer-controlled endpoints
- observed runtime traffic

Repeat after material networking/dependency changes.

## Network policy nuance

"Offline" must not be represented as literally zero network access, because podcast/RSS/article retrieval inherently uses the Internet.

The precise claim should be closer to:

> **No developer-controlled data plane.** Spoken Margins Unplugged contacts only content sources selected by the user or referenced by those sources. Personal listening/interjection data is not sent to Spoken Margins or third-party service providers.

Downloaded/local sources should continue to function with no network available.

## Packaging / business model

Initial direction:

- separate App Store listing
- one-time purchase
- no subscription required for core functionality
- no account required
- no server dependency

The connected Spoken Margins app can separately support IAP/subscription/compute credits, shared margins/book clubs, premium server processing, cloud TTS, and integrated remote AI.

## Architecture direction

Keep shared behavior in local packages/modules and make the app targets thin:

```text
Shared Local Engine
  ├─ playback
  ├─ interjections
  ├─ local ASR
  ├─ local TTS
  ├─ maps
  ├─ summaries
  ├─ persistence
  └─ export/import

Spoken Margins Unplugged target
  └─ local engine + source fetcher only

Spoken Margins Connected target
  └─ local engine + service client + sync/social/server features
```

Avoid two product forks.

## Acceptance criteria / investigation gates

- [ ] Decide whether to ship Unplugged as a separate App Store product and Bundle ID.
- [ ] Define an exact, reviewable outbound-network policy.
- [ ] Produce an Unplugged target that cannot link Connected service modules.
- [ ] Add build/release checks for prohibited endpoints and SDKs.
- [ ] Verify normal RSS/article/media retrieval still works under the constrained policy.
- [ ] Verify downloaded/local items remain fully usable with networking unavailable.
- [ ] Verify all core interjection, playback, map, local-AI, export, and pasted-response workflows without backend traffic.
- [ ] Validate App Store privacy disclosures for the actual shipped implementation.
- [ ] Document Apple App Privacy Report verification for end users.
- [ ] Prototype the local Privacy Ledger.
- [ ] Evaluate publication of privacy-boundary verification tooling.
- [ ] Evaluate an independent security/privacy audit before release.

## Related future product split

This issue intentionally focuses on **Spoken Margins Unplugged**. A separate future issue can define the connected edition's cooperative-compute / Compute Credits system, server-generated TTS/maps/summaries, book clubs/shared margins, and integrated AI conversation.

## Product principle

**The app works without us. The networked product may make it better, but Unplugged should remain independently useful and independently inspectable.**

title: Post-App-Store launch: email margin.fm founder about independent convergence and book-club cooperation
body:
## Outcome

After **Spoken Margins is publicly available through the external App Store release** (not merely internal/external TestFlight), email the founder of **margin.fm** to introduce Spoken Margins and open a cooperative conversation.

This is intentionally gated on public release so the note can point to a real, independently developed product rather than sounding like a pre-launch claim about overlapping ideas.

## Release dependency

**Do not send before the public App Store release is live.**

Current related release work:

- #41 — App Store submission/product-page screenshot readiness.
- #30 — external TestFlight release work; completion of this issue alone is **not** sufficient to trigger outreach.

If/when a dedicated public App Store release tracker is created, link this issue to it and treat that tracker as the authoritative blocker.

## Intent of the email

The email should communicate four things clearly and without sounding territorial:

1. **Independent convergence**
   - I independently arrived at a closely related idea while building Spoken Margins.
   - I discovered margin.fm after developing the core concept/workflow rather than setting out to clone it.
   - The overlap is interesting enough that I wanted to reach out directly rather than silently develop in parallel.

2. **Spotify-native single-click mechanism**
   - I do **not** intend to scoop or race them on their Spotify-native single-click mechanism.
   - Keep this statement narrowly scoped to that mechanism; do not accidentally imply a broad non-compete, ownership concession, or restriction on unrelated Spoken Margins functionality.

3. **Book-club direction**
   - I had been planning a book-club / shared-reading-listening feature for Spoken Margins.
   - Ask whether margin.fm is also planning to pursue a book-club/social-reading direction.
   - The question is exploratory rather than a demand for roadmap disclosure.

4. **Potential cooperation**
   - If both products are heading toward a similar book-club use case, suggest that there may be a useful way to cooperate rather than independently duplicate every part of that feature.
   - Keep possible cooperation deliberately open-ended: interoperability, shared formats/anchors, complementary product boundaries, experiments, or simply comparing notes.

## Suggested structure

- Brief personal introduction and link to the now-public Spoken Margins app/product page.
- Explain the independent path that led to Spoken Margins and acknowledge the conceptual overlap with margin.fm.
- Explicitly mention respect for their Spotify-native one-click mechanism and the intention not to race them on that specific interaction.
- Mention the planned book-club direction and ask whether they are thinking about the same space.
- Offer a short conversation to compare notes and see whether cooperation makes sense.

## Tone / guardrails

- Collegial and candid, not legalistic.
- Do not imply that either side owns the broad idea of annotating/listening/reacting to media.
- Do not claim knowledge of margin.fm's private roadmap.
- Do not make commitments about exclusivity, markets, features, IP, or future competition beyond the specific Spotify-native mechanism stated above.
- Do not frame the contact as asking permission to continue developing Spoken Margins.
- Preserve the possibility that the products remain independent even if no cooperation emerges.

## Done when

- [ ] Spoken Margins is publicly available through the App Store.
- [ ] The correct founder/contact channel for margin.fm is verified.
- [ ] A concise email is drafted using the points above and reviewed by the product owner.
- [ ] The email includes a public Spoken Margins link that the recipient can actually open/use.
- [ ] The product owner sends the email.
- [ ] Any substantive reply or proposed cooperation is captured in a follow-up issue rather than silently changing the roadmap.

## Non-goal

This issue does not authorize changing Spoken Margins' roadmap, entering a partnership, making IP commitments, or committing to interoperability. It only tracks the post-launch introduction and exploratory conversation.

title: Bug: interjections on AI responses are placed by source-relative percentage instead of AI-turn position

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
## Build 27 owner validation — September 12, 2026

AI-response Margins retain their assistant-turn identity and coordinate space in the accepted response-note flow. This is distinct from the remaining scene/chapter/own/shared visual distinction in #68.

The product owner reported using **Build 27** on September 11, accepted all checklist flows except six named problems, and explicitly requested this issue reconciliation on September 12, 2026. Status here is **human_validated by owner report**, not inferred from tests. The report is aggregate acceptance; no separate device/OS matrix or exact installed commit is invented. Subsequent local repairs are not covered by that acceptance.

Evidence: `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md` and the second-edition/current owner checklists in the local workspace. No upload, external approval, or source-baseline promotion is claimed. Original issue text/checklists are preserved below as history; unchecked historical boxes are not a claim that accepted behavior is still failing.

---

## Summary

When the listener interjects while an **AI response** is playing, the resulting Margin is placed in the main timeline using the AI response's fractional progress as though it were fractional progress through the **original source**.

Example: if the listener interjects at roughly **25% through an AI response**, that Margin appears beside the original source Margins around the source's **25% position**. The Margin should instead remain attached to the AI response / assistant turn in which it was created.

This is a timeline/anchor ownership bug: progress within a derivative AI turn is not the same coordinate space as progress within the source item.

## Observed behavior

1. Play an AI response attached to a source item/session.
2. Interject partway through the AI response (for example, around 25%).
3. Finish/save the interjection.
4. Inspect the timeline.
5. The new Margin is positioned near the source Margins at approximately 25% of the original item rather than in relation to the AI response that was actually playing.

## Expected behavior

- An interjection created during an AI response retains the identity of that AI/assistant turn as its immediate playback context.
- Its position within that turn is represented in the AI-turn coordinate space, not converted into a percentage of the parent source timeline.
- The timeline should make the parent-child relationship intelligible: source item -> AI response -> Margin created while listening to that response.
- Source-relative anchors used to explain *why the AI response exists* may still be retained as provenance, but they must not overwrite the Margin's actual playback target/position.
- Interjections created on the original source continue to use the ordinary source coordinate system.

## Investigation hypotheses to falsify

1. A generic `completionPercentage` or normalized progress value is being reused for both source playback and AI-turn playback without target identity.
2. Timeline placement accepts a percentage but not the coordinate-space / target ID that the percentage belongs to.
3. AI-turn interjections persist the parent source item ID while dropping the active assistant-turn ID.
4. The interjection is persisted correctly but presentation flattens all positions onto the source timeline.
5. Restoration/relaunch reconstructs the Margin from source-relative progress even if richer AI-turn anchor data existed initially.

## Required state model

Keep these concepts distinct:

- **Source anchor:** canonical location in the original article/podcast/text that prompted the conversation.
- **AI-turn identity:** stable ID of the assistant response being played.
- **AI-turn playback position:** logical/media position within that response.
- **Margin-on-AI-turn anchor:** the listener's interjection target inside the AI turn.
- **Timeline presentation:** a view that may nest or sequence derivative turns without projecting their fractional progress onto the source coordinate space.

A normalized percentage is meaningful only together with the target/coordinate space it measures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Interjecting at ~25% of an AI response does **not** place the new Margin at ~25% of the original source timeline.
- [ ] The saved Margin retains the stable AI-turn identity and a position within that turn.
- [ ] Multiple interjections at different positions in the same AI response preserve their order within that response.
- [ ] Interjections on two different AI responses cannot collide merely because they were made at the same fractional progress.
- [ ] Original-source Margins continue to use source-relative placement unchanged.
- [ ] Relaunch/reload preserves the same AI-turn association and presentation.
- [ ] Export / AI handoff can distinguish a Margin made on source content from one made while listening to an AI response.
- [ ] Regression coverage includes 0%, ~25%, ~50%, and near-end positions in an AI response plus ordinary source interjections in the same session.

## Related

- #95 — pasted AI-response import/listening workflow and AI-turn interjection discoverability.
- #59 — historical playback-session state ownership issues around AI responses; closed, but relevant architectural context.
- #71 — native-text interjection position/state ownership precedent.

## Priority

Core conversation-history correctness. The current behavior visually attributes the listener's response to the wrong place in the source and can make later review of the conversation misleading.

title: Bug: Native-text narration mangles domain lists into unintelligible speech
body:
## Summary

While listening to **Countering misuse of AI: September 2026**, the user encountered a domain-heavy passage that text-to-speech mangled badly enough that they could not understand what was being read. They recorded an interjection at **6%** specifically to identify the unintelligible material.

This blocks comprehension of the affected passage, rather than being merely an undesirable voice or cosmetic pronunciation preference. The extent beyond this item is not yet established.

## Reported item and evidence

- Item: https://www.anthropic.com/threat-intelligence-report-september-2026
- Session status: `in_progress`
- Completion / interjection anchor: **6%**
- Evidence: user-provided Spoken Margins AI handoff. No audio recording, exact app build, OS version, selected voice, synthesis engine, or preparation state was supplied. Do not infer these from other reports or the latest release.

### Source context before the interjection — verbatim handoff excerpt

```text
]org
[.]org
itechx[.]tel
[.]net
```

### Listener interjection at 6%

> All right, I need to figure out what the heck this is because I can't hear it. The text speech completely mangled it.

### Source continues — verbatim handoff excerpt

```text
meridian-protocol[.]org
meridiangroup-corp[.]com
projectnightcrawler[.]dev
metricwave[.
```

**Evidence boundary:** the reported audible mangling is the observed symptom. The partial strings at the edges of the handoff may simply reflect bounded context extraction; they do **not**, by themselves, prove that ingestion or speech chunking truncated the source. No independent audio reproduction has been performed, and a regression from a previously working build is not established.

## Reproduction target

1. Open the affected item, or import the linked report through the corresponding text intake path.
2. Start text narration and locate the domain-list passage shown above; the reported session reached it around 6%, but the strings are a more reliable locator than assuming identical progress after reimport.
3. Listen through the list and the surrounding prose, including entry boundaries and any render-chunk transitions.
4. Compare the audible output with the retained source text and identify exactly which names, separators, or entries become unintelligible.

## Expected behavior

The listener should be able to recognize that a domain list is being read and distinguish its entries. Bracketed separators such as `[.]`, hyphens, and line breaks must not result in unintelligible output or silently lose meaningful parts of the identifiers.

Any speech-specific normalization should preserve the original source text and its position mapping. Do not solve the problem by silently deleting the list, substituting a summary, or turning its strings into active links. A clearer spoken form, explicit spelling, or another bounded reading strategy can be evaluated, but the fix should follow the reproduced failure rather than assume one particular cause.

## Investigation — hypotheses to test, not established causes

Compare the original passage, imported text, speech-normalized text, synthesis chunks, and resulting audio to locate the first stage where intelligibility or fidelity is lost:

- **Extraction / reading order:** are intact entries and relevant headings preserved, or are columns, lines, or unrelated fragments being merged or reordered?
- **Normalization / segmentation:** is punctuation stripped or treated as a sentence boundary in a way that splits `[.]` or breaks domain names? Are adjacent entries run together without usable separation?
- **Synthesis:** does an intact, correctly segmented input still produce unintelligible speech in the affected engine/voice? Compare supported neural and system-voice paths without assuming which one was active in this report.
- **Prepared audio:** does fresh rendering reproduce the same output, or is an older cached rendering being replayed? If normalization changes, verify that incompatible prepared output is not reused.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce and document the affected passage with build, voice/engine, playback rate, and prepared/live state recorded.
- [ ] Before/after listening evidence demonstrates intelligible, distinguishable entries and coherent surrounding prose; a text-only snapshot is insufficient to establish an audio fix.
- [ ] Add focused fixtures for the complete domain strings above, `[.]`, hyphens, line-separated entries, and boundaries near domain tokens. Keep truncated handoff excerpts distinct from complete-source fixtures.
- [ ] No meaningful identifier content is silently dropped, concatenated with another entry, or invented.
- [ ] Original source text, interjection anchoring, and source-to-audio mapping remain correct after any speech-only transformation.
- [ ] Verify the relevant supported playback paths and fresh versus previously prepared output; document any engine-specific limitation rather than claiming all voices were tested.
- [ ] Product-owner listening validation confirms that the formerly unintelligible passage is understandable.

## Related boundaries

- #34 — render identity includes normalization/chunking revisions that affect output.
- #64 — durable prepared audio and source-to-media mapping.

This issue tracks content intelligibility, not the separate preparation-stall or playback-control failures.

title: Imported Margin play/pause controls target source playback and leave the Margin card active
body:
## Build 27 owner validation — September 12, 2026

Imported-Margin pause/resume, source pause ownership, Return to Source, completion and remote transport are accepted. The new two-Margin sender failure (#17), Timeline provenance (#68), and scrolling (#93) remain open.

The product owner reported using **Build 27** on September 11, accepted all checklist flows except six named problems, and explicitly requested this issue reconciliation on September 12, 2026. Status here is **human_validated by owner report**, not inferred from tests. The report is aggregate acceptance; no separate device/OS matrix or exact installed commit is invented. Subsequent local repairs are not covered by that acceptance.

Evidence: `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md` and the second-edition/current owner checklists in the local workspace. No upload, external approval, or source-baseline promotion is claimed. Original issue text/checklists are preserved below as history; unchecked historical boxes are not a claim that accepted behavior is still failing.

---

## Report
The product owner reports that pressing pause during an imported Margin seems to break out of the Margin while leaving it dismissible.

## Reproduced
A focused app-hosted XCTest reproduced a transport ownership mismatch on iPhone 17 Pro Simulator, iOS 26.5, September 9, 2026. This is developer verification, not human validation.

Starting a playable imported Margin pauses the canonical source session and starts a separate AVPlayer. The primary play/pause toggle then resumes the canonical source session instead of pausing the Margin. The Margin player remains running and playingImportedCommentary remains populated, so the UI continues to show its playing card and Return to Source.

Calling pause() explicitly also leaves the Margin AVPlayer running.

### Exact observed state
```
before toggle: source=paused, marginTime=0.20986925, marginRate=1.0
after toggle: source=playing, marginRate=1.0, card=true
after explicit pause: source=paused, marginRate=1.0, card=true
Executed 1 test, with 0 failures; TEST SUCCEEDED
```

The reproduction test asserts the current faulty behavior. It uses a real 30-second synthetic CAF and real AVPlayer for the imported Margin, with NoopAudioPlaybackClient for source playback. Thus source **state resumption** and continued Margin playback are verified; audible source overlap, the Margin actually stopping, and the owner's exact device/package are not established. The active card exposes **Return to Source**; literal **Dismiss** belongs to the pending prompt.

## Reproduction steps
1. Start a source session with an imported voiced Margin.
2. Navigate to its verified anchor and choose Listen.
3. Confirm the Margin audio starts.
4. Tap the primary play/pause control.
5. Observe canonical source state returning to playing while the Margin remains playing and its card remains present.
6. Issue explicit Pause: source state becomes paused, but the Margin player still has rate 1.0.

## Code evidence
At base commit fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704:
- [Gate1AppModel.playPause / pause](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/App/SpokenMarginsApp/Sources/SpokenMarginsApp/Gate1AppModel.swift): dispatch checks Skim and canonical snapshot status, but does not route imported-Margin transport to interjectionAudioPlayer.
- The same file's listenToImportedCommentary pauses the source, starts the separate AVPlayer and sets playingImportedCommentary. resumePlayback resumes the engine. stopImportedCommentaryPlayback clears the Margin state only on explicit return/completion.
- [Gate1RootView imported commentary card](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/App/SpokenMarginsApp/Sources/SpokenMarginsApp/Gate1RootView.swift): playingImportedCommentary controls the Playing / Return to Source card.

Tested current codex/provisional-next worktree based on that SHA, with existing uncommitted local-audio integration changes (build number remains 26). This is not a reproduction against the exact distributed TestFlight binary. No runtime fix or release-plan change was made.

Local evidence: artifacts/reviews/2026-09-09-imported-margin-pause/{reproduction-test.swift,xcodebuild.log,reproduction.xcresult}. The temporary test was injected into Gate2CompactControlTests for the run, then removed; the reproduction source is retained in the evidence directory.

## Expected behavior / acceptance
- [ ] Primary pause during an imported Margin pauses that Margin at its current position and keeps source playback paused.
- [ ] Play resumes the same Margin from its paused position; it does not resume source prematurely.
- [ ] Card text, transport state and actual active player agree while playing and paused.
- [ ] Return to Source / completion clears the active Margin state and applies the existing source-resume policy exactly once.
- [ ] Focused regression coverage exercises both primary toggle and explicit pause, actual Margin position advancement/freeze/resume, and source advancement with a real adapter.
- [ ] Check manual Listen and autoplay, native text and native media, and separately verify remote controls.
- [ ] Product owner rechecks the original device flow.

Related: #59 tracks broader playback/session-state drift; this issue isolates received-Margin transport.

title: UI/UX: turn Margins into an actionable scoped workspace
body:
## Build 27 owner reconciliation — September 12, 2026

**Margins workspace use is accepted except detail-action feedback and context recovery; keep open.** Copy with Context, Play Recording and related actions lacked visible feedback; Retry Context failed despite source audio being on device. Diagnostics showed a missing source-audio file path. Local repair displays feedback within the presented detail, exposes retry progress/results, and resolves the current app-owned audio location. Relocated-file and in-sheet UI checks pass. Owner must retry copy, recording playback/stop and context recovery on the affected Margin. Search is accepted and #94 closes; sharing remains #17.

The product owner reported using **Build 27** on September 11, accepted all checklist flows except six named problems, and explicitly requested this issue reconciliation on September 12, 2026. Only accepted portions above are **human_validated by owner report**; listed exceptions remain pending. The report is aggregate acceptance; no separate device/OS matrix or exact installed commit is invented. Subsequent local repairs are not covered by that acceptance.

Evidence: `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md` and the second-edition/current owner checklists in the local workspace. No upload, external approval, or source-baseline promotion is claimed. Original issue text/checklists are preserved below as history; unchecked historical boxes are not a claim that accepted behavior is still failing.

---

## Goal

Make the **Margins** screen useful as the primary workspace for reviewing and acting on accumulated listener thinking, rather than a passive list with unclear scope and non-actionable status.

The product-owner audit summarizes the current state as **“Margins is useless right now.”** This issue owns the broader screen/workflow redesign while preserving the narrower features already tracked in #92 and #94.

## Requested changes

### Add explicit scope

The screen should make its scope obvious and switchable, including at minimum:

- **All** margins;
- **Item Margins** for the currently selected/source item context.

Do not make the user infer whether they are seeing global or item-scoped results.

Scope changes should preserve stable margin identity and make it straightforward to navigate back to the associated source position.

### Make Need Attention actionable or remove it

The current **Need Attention** treatment should not remain as a passive warning bucket.

Either:

1. each attention state has a meaningful fix and the section provides an appropriate **Fix All** action for safe/idempotent repairs; or
2. remove the aggregate Need Attention section if the app cannot offer useful remediation.

`Fix All` must not blindly retry destructive, ambiguous, expensive, privacy-sensitive, or user-choice-dependent operations. It should only batch operations whose semantics are safe and explicit; other cases should route to individual review.

### Move session export to Margins

Make Margins the destination for **Export Sessions** / engagement export rather than keeping that workflow on Library.

The export surface should use the existing export contracts rather than inventing a second serialization path. #16 remains authoritative for portable Markdown/JSON behavior and file/share semantics.

### Integrate existing Margins improvements coherently

This broader screen must compose with:

- #92 — summarized interjections as the primary scannable callout;
- #94 — text search across margins;
- existing navigation back to the source/timeline.

Do not implement scope, search, summaries, and export as four disconnected headers that recreate the current clutter problem.

## Information architecture principle

A useful Margins screen should answer three questions quickly:

1. **What did I think?** — concise summarized/cleaned margin content.
2. **Where did I think it?** — source/item and anchor context.
3. **What can I do with it?** — open, search/filter, resolve a real problem, or export.

Anything that does not help answer one of those questions should justify its screen space.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Margins has an explicit, understandable scope control including All and Item Margins.
- [ ] Switching scope returns the correct canonical margins without duplicating or losing records.
- [ ] Need Attention either maps each surfaced state to useful remediation and offers a safe Fix All where applicable, or is removed.
- [ ] Fix All never performs ambiguous/destructive/user-consent-dependent actions silently.
- [ ] Session export is available from Margins and removed from Library once the replacement workflow is complete.
- [ ] Export reuses the existing #16 contract/path rather than creating a Margins-only format.
- [ ] #92 summary callouts and #94 search fit naturally into the same screen hierarchy.
- [ ] Every margin result retains clear source identity and a route back to its anchored source/timeline position.
- [ ] Empty, failed, pending, and no-attention states are clear without consuming disproportionate vertical space.
- [ ] Dynamic Type and VoiceOver expose scope, status, source identity, and actions unambiguously.
- [ ] Product-owner validation demonstrates that the screen is useful for locating, reviewing, and exporting real accumulated margins without returning to Library for the core workflow.

## Related

- #92 — summarized interjections as primary Margins callout.
- #94 — search margins by text.
- #16 — canonical Markdown/JSON export and share/file behavior.
- #108 — Library redesign; removes Export Sessions once this destination exists.

## Non-goals

- Redefining the underlying margin/interjection persistence model solely for presentation.
- Treating every recoverable backend state as something the user needs to see in Need Attention.

Internal Margins distribution is confirmed; Build 21 remains external. #14 and later-release authorization are unchanged.

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Goal

Make the **Library** screen substantially denser and more useful by reducing oversized chrome, surfacing relevant preparation state, and adding the organization controls called out in the product-owner audit.

This issue intentionally owns the Library-screen portion of that audit; Item Detail and Margins are tracked separately.

## Requested changes

### Reduce the massive header / wasted vertical space

The current Library composition spends too much vertical space on header/chrome before the user reaches library content. Tighten the top hierarchy without shrinking important tap targets or making the screen visually cramped.

### Move Offline Rendering higher

Move **Offline Rendering** near the top of the Library, immediately after the primary header area, so preparation state/action is discoverable without scrolling through less actionable content first.

This is presentation only; preparation policy and correctness remain owned by #64/#73/#98.

### Default to unplayed + in-progress; hide played/completed items

The Library should default to the items that are still candidates for listening: **unplayed** and **in-progress**. Items whose canonical source state is **Played/Complete** should be hidden from the default Library view so a large long-lived library does not overwhelm the user with already-consumed material.

Implement this as a reversible presentation/filter rule, not deletion:

- the default scope includes unplayed and in-progress items;
- played/completed items remain available through an obvious **All**, **Played**, or equivalent scope/filter;
- completion must use the canonical item/session semantics from #102 rather than arbitrary historical sessions or AI-turn completion;
- changing the filter must not alter completion state;
- the user should never have to remember that completed items exist behind a hidden state: the reveal-all/played control must be discoverable;
- if a user deliberately chooses another Library scope, preserve that explicit choice according to the Library filter persistence contract rather than repeatedly forcing the default.

Validate this behavior with a realistically large library before closure because the default materially changes what appears on launch.

### Sort by number of margins

Add a Library sort option for **number of margins**, enabling items with more user engagement to be surfaced together.

- define deterministic tie-breaking;
- derive the count from canonical margins/interjections rather than transient UI state;
- sorting must remain performant on a realistically large library and should be included in #93 profiling if necessary.

### Move session export out of Library

Remove **Export Sessions** from Library once the replacement Margins workflow is available. Export is an action on accumulated engagement, so its destination is tracked in the Margins workspace issue rather than duplicated here.

### Compact Library Now Playing

The Library's Now Playing treatment is currently approximately 1.5 inches tall and mostly empty space. Make it compact:

- remove the low-value/redundant icon called out in the audit;
- retain only the information/actions required to identify and return to active playback;
- avoid reproducing the full playback card inside Library.

This is separate from #100, which owns the full playback surface itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Library reaches actual item content materially sooner on a representative iPhone size.
- [ ] Offline Rendering is positioned near the top after the primary header area.
- [ ] On a fresh/default Library scope, unplayed and in-progress items are visible while canonically played/completed items are hidden.
- [ ] An obvious All/Played/equivalent control reveals completed items without changing their completion state.
- [ ] Completion filtering uses #102's canonical item-level state; stale sessions and incomplete AI responses do not misclassify visibility.
- [ ] An explicit non-default filter choice is preserved according to the Library query/filter persistence contract.
- [ ] Library offers sort by margin count with deterministic tie-breaking.
- [ ] Margin-count sorting remains responsive on a realistic loaded library.
- [ ] Export Sessions is absent from Library once the Margins replacement is available.
- [ ] Library Now Playing is substantially shorter, removes the redundant icon, and still provides a clear route back to playback.
- [ ] Dynamic Type and VoiceOver preserve discoverability of filtering, sorting, Offline Rendering, and Now Playing.
- [ ] Product-owner validates the revised Library with played, unplayed, in-progress, stale-session, and margin-heavy items.

## Related

- #86 — Library search, filters, and sorting; this issue defines the requested default listening-state scope.
- #102 — canonical Played/in-progress semantics and Mark Complete.
- #93 — loaded-library scrolling/performance profiling.
- #64 / #73 / #98 — rendering/preparation semantics; Library only presents their state.
- #100 — full playback-card polish, not the Library Now Playing strip.
- Margins workspace follow-up owns the destination for session export.

## Non-goals

- Deleting hidden items or rewriting historical sessions to enforce the default filter.
- Duplicating the full player inside Library.

## Goal

This issue is based on the product-owner screen audit and intentionally groups the Item Detail notes into one information-architecture pass.

### Listening Sessions before Chapters

Move the **Listening Sessions** section above **Chapters** so the user's actual engagement/history is surfaced before secondary source structure.

### Overview must earn its space

The current **Overview** should either:

- provide an actual concise overview that helps the user understand the item; or
- disappear when there is no useful overview to show.

Do not reserve a prominent section for placeholder or duplicative content.

### Listening Readiness must be actionable or disappear

**Listening Readiness** should either provide meaningful, specific state plus actions, or be removed.

Useful readiness presentation should answer questions such as:

- what is ready now;
- what is missing or blocked;
- what action can resolve it;
- whether the item can still be played through a fallback.

A generic status with no actionable consequence is not useful enough to justify a section.

Rename **Continue Listening** to **Continue**. The context already establishes that the action resumes the item.

## Canonical item overflow menu

The Item Detail `…` menu should be the home for secondary item actions, capability-gated by source type/state:

- **Prepare Listening Map**
- **Mark Complete**
- **Download**
- **Render**

These actions should use existing domain semantics rather than implementing screen-specific state:

- Render/preparation uses the durable preparation rules in #64/#73 and current regression work in #98;
- Download is shown only where the source/representation supports a meaningful download;

Do not show enabled actions that can only respond with “next time” or otherwise fail to perform the promised current-item operation.

Build 26 includes an edge-confined back gesture to protect scrubber touch ownership. That correction is not implementation or acceptance of a continuously finger-tracked navigation transition. This broader interaction change remains deferred and must not regress the accepted scrubber (#84).

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Summary

Horizontal swipe navigation in the current UI feels delayed: the user swipes, then the destination navigates after the gesture rather than moving continuously with the finger.

The product-owner audit describes the desired behavior as effectively **navigate as I swipe**, not **swipe, release, then navigate**.

## Expected interaction

- The destination/source view should track horizontal drag progress continuously where the navigation pattern supports it.
- Reversing the gesture before the commit threshold should naturally cancel and return to the origin.
- Crossing the commit threshold should complete from the current interactive position rather than starting a second delayed animation.
- Gesture velocity/distance should produce predictable completion behavior.
- A partial gesture must not accidentally change selected item/session state before the transition commits.

## Investigation

Determine whether the current implementation uses a discrete swipe recognizer or state change followed by a separate navigation animation rather than an interactive transition.

Also verify that attempts to make the transition interactive do not expose the broader performance regression tracked in #93. The transition should remain directly coupled to touch under realistic loaded-library conditions.

## Accessibility / platform behavior

- Preserve ordinary button/navigation alternatives; swipe must not become the only route.
- Respect Reduce Motion with an appropriate system-consistent transition while preserving prompt input response.
- VoiceOver focus must end on the correct destination after commit and remain on the origin after cancellation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] During a supported horizontal navigation swipe, visible transition progress tracks finger movement rather than waiting until gesture completion.
- [ ] Reversing/cancelling a partial swipe returns smoothly to the original screen without changing the selected target.
- [ ] Committing the swipe completes from the current gesture progress without a perceptible pause/restart.
- [ ] Slow drags, fast flicks, aborted gestures, repeated swipes, and edge-of-screen interactions behave deterministically.
- [ ] Interaction remains responsive on a physical device with a realistic loaded library.
- [ ] VoiceOver and Reduce Motion behavior remains correct.
- [ ] Product-owner validates the gesture against the current delayed behavior.

## Related

- #93 — UI/UX revamp scrolling and frame-hitch performance; interactive navigation should be profiled under the same realistic workload.

## Non-goals

- Replacing the app's navigation architecture wholesale if the affected transition can be made genuinely interactive within the existing structure.

title: Feature: narrate meaningful figures during PDF playback
body:
## Goal

Make PDF listening preserve meaningful information that currently exists only in figures, diagrams, charts, or other non-text visual content.

The product-owner audit explicitly calls out **PDF — Narration of Figures**. This is distinct from ordinary PDF text extraction and should be treated as an accessibility/content-understanding feature with provenance and grounding requirements.

## Desired experience

During PDF playback, when the reading order reaches a meaningful figure:

- narrate an available authored caption/alt description when it adequately conveys the figure;
- when no adequate authored description exists, optionally generate a concise figure description only through an explicitly supported image-understanding path;
- place the narration at the figure's logical position in document reading order;
- clearly distinguish authored text from AI-generated description when provenance matters;
- allow a listener to skip or disable figure narration without losing the surrounding text position.

## Evidence hierarchy

Prefer stronger document evidence before generated interpretation:

1. tagged-PDF alt/actual text associated with the figure;
2. authored figure caption and nearby labels;
3. deterministic extraction of obvious labels/table structure where reliable;
4. bounded AI-generated visual description when enabled and adequately grounded;
5. explicit unavailable/omitted state when the figure cannot be described reliably.

Do not silently invent conclusions from a chart or diagram. A generated description should distinguish directly observable content from interpretation.

## Figure eligibility

Not every image deserves interruption. The implementation should distinguish meaningful figures from decorative images, logos, repeated headers/footers, tiny icons, and artifacts of PDF rendering.

When confidence is insufficient, omit the narration rather than flooding playback with low-value descriptions.

## Anchoring and playback

- Preserve the figure's page/source location as a durable anchor.
- Figure narration must not corrupt canonical text position, progress, interjection anchoring, or session restoration.
- An interjection made during figure narration should retain provenance showing that the listener was hearing a figure description and the source figure/page it describes.
- Generated-description duration must not be confused with canonical PDF source extent.

## Accessibility and controls

- Expose a setting or per-item control for figure narration if generation is materially different from ordinary source narration.
- VoiceOver/read-aloud semantics must not duplicate the same caption twice.
- Provide concise disclosure for AI-generated figure descriptions without making ordinary listening cumbersome.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A tagged PDF with useful figure alt text narrates that authored description at the correct source position.
- [ ] A captioned figure is not redundantly described when its authored caption already provides the useful information.
- [ ] Decorative/repeated images do not produce narration.
- [ ] An eligible figure without adequate authored text can use the supported generated-description path when enabled.
- [ ] Generated descriptions are identified as derived content and never presented as source quotation.
- [ ] Unclear or unsupported figures fail closed rather than producing confident invented interpretation.
- [ ] Skipping/disabling figure narration preserves the underlying PDF source position.
- [ ] Interjections and resume behavior remain anchored to the correct PDF location before, during, and after a figure description.
- [ ] Fixtures cover text-heavy figures, charts, diagrams, photographs, decorative graphics, missing alt text, malformed tags, and repeated page furniture.
- [ ] Product-owner validates the feature on representative academic/technical PDFs where figures materially affect understanding.

## Related

- Existing PDF/native-text playback should remain the canonical source/text spine.
- #14 applies to generated derivative material that might later be exported or shared.

## Non-goals

- General-purpose OCR of every rasterized PDF page.
- Claiming semantic certainty about ambiguous scientific/technical figures.
- Replacing the original figure or caption with generated text.
