body:
## Build 27 owner reconciliation — September 12, 2026

**Partially accepted; keep open for repeated-Skim exit.** In Build 27, pressing Skim while its summary plays restarts the summary. Expected: end the summary and move to the chapter boundary, preserving prior source play/pause intent. Local repair completes the active bridge; real-player regression verifies advancement after exit. Owner retry remains required, including the final available summary. Accepted imported-Margin transport is separately closed in #110.

The product owner reported using **Build 27** on September 11, accepted all checklist flows except six named problems, and explicitly requested this issue reconciliation on September 12, 2026. Only accepted portions above are **human_validated by owner report**; listed exceptions remain pending. The report is aggregate acceptance; no separate device/OS matrix or exact installed commit is invented. Subsequent local repairs are not covered by that acceptance.

Evidence: `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md` and the second-edition/current owner checklists in the local workspace. No upload, external approval, or source-baseline promotion is claimed. Original issue text/checklists are preserved below as history; unchecked historical boxes are not a claim that accepted behavior is still failing.

---

## Build 26 reconciliation — 2026-09-08

Bounded app/Live Activity Skim controls are included in the internal baseline. Build 25 explicitly leaves device Skim, bridge transport, cancellation, and resource/grounding acceptance pending; Build 26 does not supply individual results for them. Do not treat Skim as a new low-risk feature to introduce or as already human-validated.

Evidence: [scope-specific record](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-25/build-25-testflight-upload.md), [owner acceptance](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/gate-1/2026-09-08-build-26-acceptance.md), [Build 26 handoff](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-26/build-26-testflight-upload.md).

Build identity: **0.1 (26)**, exact source `9c967793e7a0e86c26a3030390818e87d830723b`; release manifest is **verified** (425 app/adapter/UI tests plus fast checks). The owner recorded **human_validated for the candidate**, without a separate device-by-device or individual-flow matrix. Internal Margins distribution is confirmed; Build 21 remains external. #14 and later-release authorization are unchanged.

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Outcome

Add **Skim Forward** and **Skim Backward** as semantic playback controls alongside the existing independently configurable time-skip controls.

- **Skim Forward:** speak a concise summary of the current scene, then begin the next scene.
- **Skim Backward:** speak a concise summary of the previous scene, then begin the current scene.

A scene is the product's neutral semantic navigation unit from #88. It may represent a claim, topic, narrative scene, procedural step, or conversational movement.

This issue owns player state, navigation semantics, UI and accessibility, compact-surface capability publication, bridge playback, cancellation/repetition behavior, and verification. It does not own scene generation or the portable map schema.

## Why Skim and time skip coexist

Time skip and Skim solve different jobs:

- **Time skip** provides literal, fine-grained movement by a user-configurable duration.
- **Skim** provides semantic movement across a scene boundary with compressed context.

Do not automatically replace, retune, or hide time-skip settings when Skim becomes available. A listener may choose shorter time jumps once scene navigation exists, but that remains the listener's decision.

If a listener is 90% through a scene and presses Skim Forward, the bridge summarizes the **whole current scene**. If they only want to move through the remaining seconds, they can use their configured time-skip control.

## Canonical interaction

For previous scene `S-1`, current scene `S0`, and next scene `S+1`:

```text
Skim Backward:  summary(S-1) -> start(S0)
Skim Forward:   summary(S0)  -> start(S+1)
```

Beginning the current scene after a backward skim is intentional. Resuming at the original halfway position would act like “remind me” rather than semantic backward navigation and could return mid-thought immediately after a context summary.

The generated summary is a temporary bridge. It is not a source quotation, not another scene, and cannot recursively participate in Skim.

## Typed playback state

Keep these layers distinct:

### Canonical source state

- active item/target;
- accepted source or media position;
- duration;
- current resolved scene;
- playback rate;
- active source representation and readiness.

Continue using the canonical playback and anchor spine established by #84, #64, and the existing SessionKit contracts. Skim must not create a competing source clock or anchor model.

### Skim command state

- direction;
- origin position and origin scene;
- summary scene;
- destination scene and resolved landing;
- command sequence/repetition identity;
- unavailable/fallback reason.

### Bridge state

- generated summary text/audio identity and provenance;
- playing, paused, cancelled, failed, or completed state;
- progress within the bridge;
- retained source origin and destination;
- optional interjection target/provenance if the listener interjects during the bridge.

Bridge duration is not added to canonical source duration or source media time.

### Landing state

After a completed bridge, perform one accepted transition to the resolved scene boundary and resume through the ordinary source player. Do not maintain a second hidden position that can drift from Now Playing, persisted session state, interjection anchoring, or the scrubber.

## Control behavior during a bridge

The listener retains control throughout:

- pause/resume pauses or resumes the bridge;
- direct seeking or a configured time skip cancels the bridge under an explicit deterministic rule and moves through ordinary source transport;
- repeated same-direction Skim traverses additional scenes rather than replaying the same bridge;
- opposite-direction Skim cancels/reverses under an explicit tested rule;
- back/cancel provides a recoverable path to the saved origin;
- interjection remains available only if its target can preserve both bridge provenance and the summarized scene anchor without pretending the listener was at the landing source position;
- route interruption, audio-session loss, backgrounding, and relaunch never strand the session between two source positions.

The product-owner must validate the audible feel of queuing, reversal, cancellation, and interjection behavior; automated state-machine checks establish only verification.

## Boundaries and unavailable states

- At the first scene, Skim Backward restarts or remains at the first scene without fabricating previous context.
- At the final scene, Skim Forward summarizes it and reaches the item's normal end behavior.
- A repeated backward command after landing must step farther backward rather than trapping the listener in the same previous-summary/current-start pair.
- Excluded or unknown spans from #88/#89 receive no bridge. Commands within them navigate predictably to neighboring valid scene boundaries without exposing a convenient user-visible ad label.
- If no valid scene map or summary is available, Skim is unavailable with an honest capability state; it must not silently degrade into a time skip.
- A malformed/unresolved destination leaves source playback at a recoverable accepted position and reports the failure.
- Publisher chapter navigation and ordinary mapless playback remain available independently.

## UI and accessibility

On the full playback surface, semantic and time transport must be distinguishable without relying only on icon shape or position.

Candidate accessible names:

- “Skim backward one scene”
- “Back 15 seconds” using the configured value
- “Forward 30 seconds” using the configured value
- “Skim forward one scene”

The exact visual arrangement requires product-owner validation and must work with Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, increased contrast, Reduce Motion, and one-handed use.

Compact surfaces may expose Skim only when their command vocabulary and active runtime capability can represent it honestly. Do not silently repurpose standard Lock Screen, headphone, car, or Watch time-skip commands as Skim. Any user-configurable remapping must be explicit and reversible.

If new command IDs, snapshot fields, or capability values are required, update schemas, validators, runtime, fixtures, traces, and tests together.

## Coverage and provenance

Align with #80:

- source audio actually played remains observed source presentation;
- source skipped by Skim remains skipped/unobserved;
- hearing a generated bridge does not count as hearing the underlying source scene;
- replay caused by Skim Backward may count only the source audio actually presented after landing;
- bridge playback retains AI/derivative provenance and is never labeled as source speech.

Diagnostics must record IDs, states, positions, evidence classes, and timing without logging private full transcripts or unrelated interjection content.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Skim Forward from any point in an eligible scene speaks that scene's whole summary and begins the next scene.
- [ ] Skim Backward from any point in an eligible scene speaks the previous scene's summary and begins the current scene.
- [ ] Separately configurable forward/back time skips remain available and unchanged.
- [ ] A 90%-complete scene still receives its whole-scene Skim summary; time skip remains the precise alternative.
- [ ] Pause, resume, cancel, time seek, same-direction repetition, opposite-direction reversal, interruption, backgrounding, and relaunch have deterministic state-machine coverage.
- [ ] Repeated Skim Backward commands move progressively backward and never loop on one scene pair.
- [ ] Bridge playback never changes canonical source duration, falsely advances source coverage, or shifts an interjection/source anchor.
- [ ] The source player, scrubber, persisted session, Now Playing state, and landing anchor agree after every completed or cancelled Skim.
- [ ] Excluded/unknown spans receive no summary and do not appear as convenient labeled ad nodes.
- [ ] Missing, malformed, ambiguous, or unresolved scene data produces an honest unavailable/recoverable state rather than a time-skip fallback.
- [ ] A listener can undo an accidental Skim and recover the saved origin.
- [ ] VoiceOver distinguishes Skim from configured time skips and announces the direction and scene-level effect.
- [ ] Capability-constrained surfaces never advertise Skim when they can only perform ordinary time transport.
- [ ] Contract validators, focused SessionKit tests, app-model tests, UI accessibility tests, interruption/restoration tests, and proportional builds pass.
- [ ] Automated evidence may mark the feature `verified`; only product-owner use may mark it `human_validated`.

## Evaluation and falsification

Compare four alternatives on the same listening corpus:

1. configurable time skips only;
2. chapter jumps with no bridge;
3. Skim Forward only;
4. symmetric Skim Forward/Backward plus time skips.

Test argument, interview, narrative, and procedural sources; very short/long scenes; 10%, 50%, and 90% scene positions; first/final scenes; mapless items; excluded ads; malformed summaries; route interruptions; and rapid repeated commands.

Record:

- landing accuracy and cumulative drift;
- time saved;
- immediate undo/reversal rate;
- comprehension of the skipped/current context;
- whether listeners predict the landing correctly;
- bridge start latency;
- control-response latency;
- summary/source confusion;
- unwanted repetition;
- accessibility comprehension.

Falsification checks include:

- forward landing in the wrong scene;
- backward resuming at the old halfway point;
- repeated back becoming stuck;
- a bridge being counted as source coverage;
- bridge duration shifting the scrubber;
- an interjection during a bridge anchoring to the future landing point;
- a time-skip command being silently interpreted as Skim;
- an excluded ad receiving a summary;
- failed/cancelled Skim stranding playback.

Stop or narrow the release if landings cannot remain exact, listeners regularly mistake generated bridges for source speech, controls become unavailable during bridges, or representative listeners cannot predict the forward/backward semantics.

## Dependencies and related work

- #88 is the hard contract dependency for scenes, summaries, provenance, eligibility, and resolution.
- #89 produces or imports Skim-ready scenes and bridge assets; hand-authored fixtures may unblock runtime development before model generation is available.
- #84 owns canonical podcast media time and scrubber synchronization.
- #64 owns durable prepared native-text audio and source-to-media mapping.
- #80 owns source-coverage semantics.
- #27 governs automatic cross-edition scene placement; exact-edition Skim may proceed independently.
- #46 supplies publisher podcast chapter navigation.
- #85 provides the guarded interjection-state precedent; Skim must not bypass recording protections.

## Non-goals

- No replacement of configurable time skips.
- No ad-labeling or ad-summary product.
- No demand-time scene generation.
- No public transcript reader.
- No claim that compact/system surfaces can expose controls their platforms do not support.
- No authorization to enter an active release lane; implementation requires a later product-owner release-plan update.

body:
## Build 27 owner reconciliation — September 12, 2026

**Portable map use is present and the owner's Build 27 report includes successful generation of 24 scenes with summaries.** Prior comments limiting this to inert proposal transport are historical. Keep the broader map contract issue open pending the affected downstream rechecks: chapter/scene provenance (#68), two-Margin export with map artifacts (#17), and Skim exit (#90). Generation evidence does not by itself validate the complete map/transport matrix.

The product owner reported using **Build 27** on September 11, accepted all checklist flows except six named problems, and explicitly requested this issue reconciliation on September 12, 2026. Only accepted portions above are **human_validated by owner report**; listed exceptions remain pending. The report is aggregate acceptance; no separate device/OS matrix or exact installed commit is invented. Subsequent local repairs are not covered by that acceptance.

Evidence: `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md` and the second-edition/current owner checklists in the local workspace. No upload, external approval, or source-baseline promotion is claimed. Original issue text/checklists are preserved below as history; unchecked historical boxes are not a claim that accepted behavior is still failing.

---

## Build 26 reconciliation — 2026-09-08

Portable private map/scene contracts are included in the Build 25 internal baseline and carried into Build 26. The bounded sharing/alignment acceptance does not establish scene-generation or Skim flow acceptance. Keep this contract's remaining compatibility/validation checklist distinct from generation (#89) and transport (#90).

Evidence: [scope-specific record](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-25/build-25-testflight-upload.md), [owner acceptance](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/gate-1/2026-09-08-build-26-acceptance.md), [Build 26 handoff](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-26/build-26-testflight-upload.md).

Build identity: **0.1 (26)**, exact source `9c967793e7a0e86c26a3030390818e87d830723b`; release manifest is **verified** (425 app/adapter/UI tests plus fast checks). The owner recorded **human_validated for the candidate**, without a separate device-by-device or individual-flow matrix. Internal Margins distribution is confirmed; Build 21 remains external. #14 and later-release authorization are unchanged.

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Outcome

Define a versioned portable Listening Map contract that can carry ordered **scenes** and concise, source-grounded scene summaries for Skim without treating recipient-local timestamps as portable truth.

A scene is the product's neutral semantic navigation unit. It may represent a claim, topic, narrative scene, procedural step, or conversational movement; the user should not need to classify which.

This issue owns the contract, schema evolution, validators, fixtures, compatibility, and transport boundary. It does not own scene generation or playback controls.

## Product behavior enabled

A valid scene map can support:

- **Skim Forward:** summarize the current scene, then begin the next scene.
- **Skim Backward:** summarize the previous scene, then begin the current scene.
- exact-edition transport of scene structure and summaries;
- later cross-edition resolution without rewriting portable evidence;
- text-backed, transcript-backed, publisher-chapter, and prepared-audio representations;
- excluded or unresolved source intervals that remain playable but are not summarized.

The summary is a derivative bridge, not source quotation, not a transcript replacement, and not another scene.

## Challenge model

Keep these typed layers distinct.

### Source identity

- stable item/source identity;
- edition or revision identity when known;
- canonical source attribution;
- optional exact-edition digest;
- source type and language.

### Portable scene semantics

- stable scene ID and ordering;
- concise scene summary;
- optional navigation title;
- summary provenance and generation/version metadata;
- summary eligibility state and reason;
- source evidence sufficient to audit what the scene and summary cover.

The contract must not require a cinematic or rhetorical subtype. “Scene” is the user-facing abstraction.

### Durable anchor evidence

- source locator or text range for text-backed items;
- transcript segment/span and surrounding human-inspectable context for transcript-backed media;
- publisher chapter evidence when used;
- sender/source media time only as a hint;
- no local chunk index, UI position, or model-provided percentage as the sole anchor.

### Recipient-local resolution

Keep resolved start/end positions, evidence class, confidence, ambiguity, resolver version, and unresolved/absent outcomes separate from the portable scene. Do not overload the existing local-playback `AnchorConfidence` vocabulary.

An exact-edition scene may resolve directly. Automatic cross-edition placement remains governed by #27; ambiguous or absent scenes must remain unresolved rather than attaching to a plausible passage.

### Rights and disclosure

- source attribution accompanies transported scene summaries;
- full generated native-audio transcripts and large source excerpts remain excluded;
- generated summaries retain clear AI/derivative provenance;
- transport and preview follow the policy produced by #14;
- if scene maps are embedded in a `.spokenmargins` package, they follow #17's deterministic package and recipient-preview conventions.

## Ads and other non-scene audio

The contract must support audio that exists in the playable track but is absent from the scene structure.

Do not require user-visible ad labels. Internally, a span that is excluded or not positively eligible for summarization may remain playable and locally anchorable without receiving a scene summary. Absence of ad evidence must not imply summary eligibility.

## Compatibility and versioning

- Preserve `listening-map.v1` decoding and behavior.
- Do not silently reinterpret v1 chapters as fully grounded v2 scenes.
- Define explicit upgrade/import behavior and failure diagnostics.
- Update schema, runtime models, validators, fixtures, exports, and tests in one intentional change.
- Existing publisher chapters remain authoritative source structure and are never silently replaced.
- Mapless playback remains valid when no scene contract can be resolved.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A versioned schema represents ordered scenes, concise summaries, eligibility, provenance, durable anchor evidence, and recipient-local resolution without mixing those layers.
- [ ] v1 maps continue to validate and play with unchanged semantics.
- [ ] A v2 map round-trips deterministically and rejects invalid structure according to the repository's compatibility policy.
- [ ] Fixtures cover native text, prepared text audio, an exact-edition podcast, publisher chapters, dynamically inserted unlabeled audio, excluded/unknown spans, an unresolved cross-edition scene, and an absent scene.
- [ ] Every valid scene resolves monotonically to source evidence on its producing edition.
- [ ] A transported summary remains traceable to its scene and source evidence without transporting a full native-audio transcript.
- [ ] Summary provenance distinguishes source text, publisher-supplied text, deterministic transformation, and model-generated derivatives.
- [ ] Invalid scene structure or unresolved anchors never destroy the prior valid map or block mapless playback.
- [ ] Exports and diagnostics have negative tests proving that internal transcripts, large excerpts, and private paths do not leak.
- [ ] Contract validators, focused SessionKit tests, migration tests, and relevant app builds pass.
- [ ] Product-owner validation remains distinct from automated verification.

## Audit and falsification

Compare:

1. current `listening-map.v1`;
2. a minimal scene extension that stores local timestamps;
3. the selected portable-evidence plus local-resolution design.

Use omission checks for attribution, negation, speaker identity, summary provenance, excluded audio, exact-edition identity, unresolved cross-edition placement, publisher chapters, and v1 compatibility.

Treat any of the following as a stopping failure:

- a local timestamp is presented as a portable cross-edition position;
- ambiguous evidence is automatically placed;
- a scene summary cannot be traced to its covered source;
- excluded/unknown audio is implicitly eligible for summarization;
- full generated native-audio transcript text leaks through a map or package;
- v1 maps change meaning after the migration.

## Dependencies and related work

- #14 owns rights, attribution, excerpt, AI-derived-material, and sharing policy.
- #17 owns deterministic `.spokenmargins` packaging and recipient preview when this map is shared inside that transport.
- #27 owns cross-edition podcast-anchor benchmarking and automatic-placement thresholds.
- #46 supplies publisher podcast chapters and mapless fallback.
- #51 owns server-hosted native-audio Listening Map feasibility and exact source-position requirements.
- #48 is advanced cross-item semantic research and is not required for scene maps.
- #80 owns source-coverage accounting; summaries and skipped source must remain distinct there.

## Non-goals

- No scene generation pipeline.
- No Skim controls or playback bridge state.
- No public transcript reader.
- No public content index or cross-item semantic graph.
- No claim that semantic compression alone establishes a right to redistribute.
- No authorization to enter an active release lane; implementation requires a later product-owner release-plan update.

title: [Post-MVP] Sleep timer with timed and end-of-chapter modes
body:
## Summary

Add a session-scoped sleep timer with timed and canonical end-of-chapter modes.

## Scope

- Timed choices: 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes.
- End of Chapter targets the current canonical source chapter and is unavailable for mapless items or the last chapter.
- Show a visible countdown with Extend 15 Minutes and Cancel.
- Expiry pauses playback without ending the session and preserves position.
- Timed modes use wall-clock time and remain armed through manual pause and backgrounding.
- Timers do not survive process termination or session or item replacement.
- Expiry during interjection recording is deferred until recording finishes or is cancelled.
- Derive presentation from typed SleepTimerState.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each timed choice expires against wall-clock time while foregrounded or backgrounded.
- [ ] Manual pause does not disarm a timed timer.
- [ ] Process restart and session or item replacement clear the timer.
- [ ] Expiry pauses playback without completing the session or changing the canonical position.
- [ ] Interjection recording defers expiry until its explicit terminal transition.
- [ ] End of Chapter pauses at the current canonical chapter boundary and is disabled when no valid boundary exists.
- [ ] Extend and Cancel update countdown and state deterministically.
- [ ] Regression fixtures cover backgrounding, clock advancement, interjection deferral, and chapter changes.

title: Prevent timeline/source navigation from cancelling an active interjection recording
body:
## Build 27 owner validation — September 12, 2026

Recording continuity and preservation of the captured source position are accepted under the second-edition capture/navigation flow.

The product owner reported using **Build 27** on September 11, accepted all checklist flows except six named problems, and explicitly requested this issue reconciliation on September 12, 2026. Status here is **human_validated by owner report**, not inferred from tests. The report is aggregate acceptance; no separate device/OS matrix or exact installed commit is invented. Subsequent local repairs are not covered by that acceptance.

Evidence: `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md` and the second-edition/current owner checklists in the local workspace. No upload, external approval, or source-baseline promotion is claimed. Original issue text/checklists are preserved below as history; unchecked historical boxes are not a claim that accepted behavior is still failing.

---

## Summary

While recording an interjection during podcast playback, tapping the **SRC/source headline item in the timeline** immediately stopped the interjection and reset podcast playback all the way to **0:00**.

An incidental timeline tap should not be able to destructively terminate an active recording or mutate the underlying podcast position. Interjection capture is a high-priority modal state: source/timeline navigation must either be disabled while recording or require an explicit, safe transition that preserves the recording and playback anchor.

## Reproduction

1. Start podcast/native-audio playback.
2. Begin recording an interjection.
3. While the interjection is actively recording, accidentally tap the **SRC/source headline** item in the timeline.
4. Observe the interjection stop.
5. Observe podcast playback/session position reset to the beginning of the episode.

## Observed behavior

- A normal timeline tap can terminate the active interjection without an explicit stop/cancel action.
- The source podcast position can be reset to 0:00 as a side effect.
- The user can therefore lose both recording continuity and their listening position from a single accidental tap.

## Expected behavior

While an interjection is being recorded:

- ordinary taps on SRC/source items or other timeline entries do **not** cancel/finish the recording;
- ordinary navigation cannot reset or seek the underlying source player;
- the source playback anchor captured at interjection start remains immutable until the interjection transition completes;
- only explicit recording controls such as Stop/Done/Cancel may end the recording;
- if product design eventually allows navigation during recording, it must be an explicit transition with deterministic recording and resume semantics rather than an incidental tap side effect.

For the MVP, the safest behavior is to make source/timeline navigation non-interactive while recording an interjection, except for controls deliberately designed for the recording state.

## Investigation targets

1. Check whether tapping SRC replaces the selected timeline item and triggers generic playback-selection logic before the recording state machine has completed.
2. Check whether source selection initializes a player with the default position of 0 before restoring the session position, and whether the recording transition prevents that restore.
3. Verify whether interjection cancellation is currently an implicit side effect of any timeline selection rather than an explicit state-machine event.
4. Confirm that the interjection resume anchor and active player position are preserved independently of timeline selection/UI focus.
5. Audit all tappable timeline rows/cards while `recordingInterjection == true` (or equivalent) for unintended navigation, seek, playback replacement, or recording cancellation actions.

## Required state-machine rule

Treat active interjection recording as an explicit state with guarded transitions:

`sourcePlaying -> recordingInterjection -> processing/saving -> sourceResume`

During `recordingInterjection`, generic timeline-selection events must not transition directly to `sourcePlaying`, replace the active player item, seek the source, or discard the recording. Ending/cancelling the recording must be represented by explicit events and tested as such.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] During an active interjection recording, tapping the SRC/source headline does not stop, cancel, or complete the recording.
- [ ] The same tap does not seek or reset the podcast position.
- [ ] The source resume anchor captured when recording begins remains unchanged throughout the recording.
- [ ] Only explicit recording controls can terminate/cancel the active interjection.
- [ ] Other timeline rows/cards are audited and cannot implicitly terminate recording or replace/reset the active source player.
- [ ] After an interjection is explicitly completed, the source resumes from the intended captured media time rather than 0:00.
- [ ] Repeated accidental taps during a recording do not alter recording duration, source media time, or session identity.
- [ ] Regression tests exercise `recordingInterjection + SRC tap` and prove both recording continuity and source-position continuity.

## Related

- #84 — podcast scrubber/progress desynchronization observed in the same session; both issues should preserve one canonical source media-time anchor across interjection transitions.
- #59 — existing playback-session/interjection state drift; relevant state-ownership precedent.

title: Regression: podcast scrubbing sticks and progress/remaining time desynchronizes from playback
body:
## Build 26 reconciliation — 2026-09-08

The accepted candidate includes the final single-touch playback slider and edge-confined back gesture. Actual Simulator drags to 70%, 22%, and 85% continued progressing after release; a paused drag to 40% preserved pause. Closing the bounded scrubber regression on the owner-accepted candidate; reopen with exact target/runtime and diagnostics if either sticky dragging or frozen post-seek progress recurs.

Evidence: [scope-specific record](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/reviews/2026-09-08-scrubber-C/evidence.md), [owner acceptance](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/gate-1/2026-09-08-build-26-acceptance.md), [Build 26 handoff](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-26/build-26-testflight-upload.md).

Build identity: **0.1 (26)**, exact source `9c967793e7a0e86c26a3030390818e87d830723b`; release manifest is **verified** (425 app/adapter/UI tests plus fast checks). The owner recorded **human_validated for the candidate**, without a separate device-by-device or individual-flow matrix. Internal Margins distribution is confirmed; Build 21 remains external. #14 and later-release authorization are unchanged.

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Summary

Podcast/native-audio scrubbing is again unreliable and can leave the visible timeline badly desynchronized from actual playback. This is not just a cosmetic defect: dragging the scrubber itself can repeatedly stick, and near the end of a podcast the UI can still claim that roughly **16 minutes remain** even though only about **2 minutes of audio actually remain**.

This needs to be treated as a recurring timeline/state-ownership regression rather than another isolated progress-bar patch. We have already tracked closely related synchronization failures in #59, #62, #65, and historical progress/state issues. The goal here is to identify and enforce one canonical media-time model for podcast playback so scrubbing, elapsed time, remaining time, interjection resume, and visible progress cannot drift independently.

## Observed behavior

### 1. Scrubber drag interaction repeatedly sticks

During podcast playback:

1. Press and hold the scrubber thumb.
2. Drag to seek through the episode.
3. The thumb repeatedly catches/sticks instead of tracking the drag continuously.
4. The user has to re-engage or fight the control multiple times to move through the timeline.

The experience is sufficiently unreliable that normal seeking becomes frustrating.

One possible explanation is that the requested target was outside the currently buffered/loaded range, but that is **not established**. If buffering is involved, silently making the scrubber stick is the wrong behavior: seeking intent should remain continuous and the player should either seek/buffer to the requested media time or expose an explicit unavailable/buffering state.

### 2. Remaining time / progress becomes wildly stale near completion

Later in the same podcast session:

- an interjection was made;
- podcast playback then continued for roughly **2 more minutes** before the episode ended;
- the visible scrubber/progress UI still indicated roughly **16 minutes remaining**.

This means the displayed timeline was no longer representing actual playback position and/or duration.

## Expected behavior

- The podcast scrubber tracks a continuous drag without repeatedly dropping/catching the gesture.
- A drag maps to one canonical requested media time.
- If the target is not yet buffered, preserve the requested target and enter a truthful buffering/seeking state rather than sticking the thumb or silently clamping to a stale loaded range.
- Audible playback position, scrubber position, elapsed time, remaining time, Now Playing position, persisted session position, and the interjection resume anchor derive from the same authoritative media-time state.
- After any seek or interjection transition, progress resumes advancing immediately from the canonical position.
- Near the end of an episode, remaining time is accurate within normal player timing tolerance; it cannot claim ~16 minutes remain when ~2 minutes remain.

## Investigation: hypotheses to falsify

These are investigation targets, not established root causes.

1. **Buffered-range incorrectly treated as seekable range** — the gesture or slider may be clamped/rejected based on `loadedTimeRanges` rather than allowing the player to seek and buffer to an arbitrary valid media time.
2. **Gesture state is being overwritten during drag** — periodic player progress updates may continue writing the slider value while the user is dragging, causing the thumb to fight/catch against playback-time updates.
3. **Multiple time authorities** — UI progress may observe a cached/session/interjection position while AVPlayer continues from a different `currentTime`.
4. **Interjection transition restores one position but leaves another progress store stale** — podcast playback may resume correctly while remaining-time UI keeps the pre-interjection or pre-seek position.
5. **Duration/position snapshot goes stale after seek or stream loading changes** — remaining time may be computed from cached duration/current position rather than the active player item.
6. **Observer lifecycle duplication/loss** — periodic time observers may be detached, duplicated, or rebound to an obsolete player/item after interjection or seek transitions.

## Required architecture outcome

Do not fix this by adding another UI-only timer or another special-case correction after an interjection.

Define and enforce one podcast timeline contract:

- **Canonical duration:** active media item's verified duration.
- **Canonical current position:** active player's accepted media time.
- **User seek intent:** temporary drag state that is not overwritten by periodic playback updates while the gesture is active.
- **Accepted seek:** exactly one transition from requested time to player time, followed by progress observation from that same player state.
- **Buffering:** orthogonal to timeline position; buffered ranges may affect readiness but must not masquerade as the episode's seekable duration unless the stream truly forbids arbitrary seeking.
- **Interjection anchor:** captured from the same canonical media time used by the scrubber immediately before interruption.

Any alternate caches/session snapshots should be derived data, not competing playback authorities.

## Diagnostics to capture

For seek/interjection transitions, capture structured diagnostics sufficient to compare:

- item/player-item identity;
- verified duration;
- `currentTime` before gesture/interjection;
- requested scrub target;
- seekable and loaded ranges;
- accepted seek target/completion time;
- player `timeControlStatus` / buffering state;
- UI-rendered elapsed/remaining time;
- captured interjection resume anchor;
- restored media time after interjection;
- observer attach/detach identity and player/item identity.

Do not log private interjection content when timestamps/IDs are sufficient.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a representative remote-stream podcast, the scrubber can be pressed, held, and dragged continuously across the episode without repeatedly sticking or losing the gesture.
- [ ] Periodic playback updates do not overwrite the slider while an active drag is in progress.
- [ ] Seeking beyond the currently buffered range either succeeds by buffering/seeking to the requested valid media time or presents an explicit truthful limitation; the scrubber does not simply catch/stick.
- [ ] After seek completion, audible playback, slider position, elapsed time, remaining time, and system Now Playing position agree within normal timing tolerance.
- [ ] Starting and finishing an interjection does not leave the podcast progress observer on a stale position or stale player item.
- [ ] In a podcast with ~2 minutes of actual media remaining, the UI reports approximately ~2 minutes remaining, not a stale value such as ~16 minutes.
- [ ] Ten repeated cycles of `drag seek -> play -> interject -> resume` do not accumulate position drift.
- [ ] Regression tests explicitly separate **user drag state**, **buffered state**, and **canonical player media time**.
- [ ] Tests cover partially buffered remote streams as well as fully local/offline podcast media.
- [ ] Instrumentation proves only the active player/item drives periodic podcast progress updates.

## Related

- #59 — playback-session state drift around interjections/AI response/Live Activity; already calls for a single playback source of truth.
- #62 — native-text lock-screen seek can freeze progress; relevant state-ownership precedent.
- #65 — native-text in-app scrub regression; relevant seek-capability precedent.

This issue is specifically for **podcast/native-audio media time and scrubber correctness**.

title: Native text can become unresumable after AirPod pause while Supersonic is still rendering

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
## Build 27 scope reconciliation — September 12, 2026

The accepted Build 27 checklist includes headphone/Lock Screen and playback controls; preserve that bounded acceptance. Keep this trigger-specific issue open because the aggregate report does not separately identify the partial-render AirPod removal/reinsertion plus Stop Generating recovery sequence described here. Do not present the historical failure as a newly reproduced Build 27 defect.

The owner accepted the checklist except six named failures and requested GitHub reconciliation on September 12. Acceptance is owner-reported Build 27, with no inferred exact installed SHA or device-by-device matrix. Original scope is preserved below; later feature expansions and explicit research measurements are not silently marked complete. Evidence: local `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md`.

---

## Summary

During **native-text playback while Supersonic rendering is still in progress**, pausing from the phone's locked state by removing an AirPod can leave the session unable to resume from **Lock Screen** or **Control Center**. Recovery then requires returning to the Spoken Margins app.

This is especially concerning because it appears to be another remote-transport/state-ownership failure in the same family as #62, but with a distinct trigger: an external route/pause event while the native-text representation is only partially rendered.

There is also a related recovery problem around **Stop Generating**: once the Supersonic generation path is stopped in this state, there is no reliable remote recovery path. The fallback Apple Accessibility/system voice also does not expose the expected speaking-rate control, so falling back changes both the voice/runtime and the user's ability to control playback speed.

## Reproduction

1. Open a native-text item.
2. Start playback using Supersonic while rendering/generation is still incomplete.
3. Lock the phone while playback continues.
4. Remove an AirPod, causing playback to pause from the locked state.
5. Attempt to resume using the Lock Screen Now Playing controls or Control Center.
6. Observe that playback cannot be resumed remotely.
7. Reopen Spoken Margins; recovery requires interaction inside the app.
8. In the affected state, try **Stop Generating** for Supersonic.
9. Observe that the session still does not have a reliable remote resume/recovery path; if playback falls back to the Apple Accessibility/system voice, the expected speaking-rate control is unavailable.

## Observed behavior

- AirPod-removal pause during incomplete Supersonic rendering can strand native-text playback in a state that Lock Screen / Control Center cannot resume.
- The user must reopen Spoken Margins to recover playback.
- Stopping Supersonic generation in the affected state does not provide a reliable remote recovery path.
- Fallback to the Apple Accessibility/system voice changes playback capabilities: speaking rate cannot be controlled as expected.

## Expected behavior

- Route-change / AirPod-removal pause must leave the native-text session in a valid, remotely resumable state, regardless of whether Supersonic rendering is complete.
- Lock Screen and Control Center play/pause commands must target the same authoritative native-text playback session as the in-app controls.
- A partially rendered item must not lose its remote-command registration or canonical `isPlaying`/paused state when an AirPod is removed.
- **Stop Generating** must have explicit, recoverable semantics. If active playback falls back to the system voice, transport and playback-rate controls should remain coherent and user-controllable.
- Switching from Supersonic to the Accessibility/system voice must not silently discard the user's selected playback speed or make the effective speaking rate uncontrollable.

## Suggested investigation

- Exercise `AVAudioSession` route-change / old-device-unavailable handling while native-text Supersonic generation is incomplete.
- Check whether removing an AirPod tears down or replaces the player/session that owns `MPRemoteCommandCenter` handlers.
- Verify remote-command registration survives the transition between partial Supersonic output, paused state, and any system-voice fallback.
- Confirm there is one canonical state owner for playback mode, `isPlaying`, source position, rendered position, selected voice/runtime, and playback rate.
- Inspect **Stop Generating** behavior while playback is active: it should cancel future rendering without leaving transport ownership orphaned.
- Verify that the fallback system-speech path receives and applies the current playback-rate setting, or expose an explicit limitation rather than silently losing rate control.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] During incomplete Supersonic rendering, removing either AirPod pauses playback and Lock Screen / Control Center can resume it on the first attempt.
- [ ] Repeated AirPod remove/reinsert cycles do not require foregrounding Spoken Margins to recover playback.
- [ ] Remote play/pause remains registered and synchronized before, during, and after partial rendering.
- [ ] `isPlaying`, audible playback, in-app state, Lock Screen state, and Control Center state agree after every route-change event.
- [ ] **Stop Generating** during active native-text playback leaves the session in a defined, resumable state.
- [ ] If playback falls back from Supersonic to the Apple Accessibility/system voice, the effective speaking rate remains controllable and consistent with the user's selected rate, or the UI explicitly communicates any unavoidable limitation.
- [ ] Regression coverage includes: start native text → partial render → lock phone → remove AirPod → remote resume → reinsert AirPod → Stop Generating → continue/resume playback.
- [ ] Regression coverage verifies both transport state and voice/runtime/playback-rate identity.

## Related

- #62 — previous Lock Screen native-text desynchronization / voice-switch bug (closed as completed; this may be a regression or uncovered route-change edge case).
- #64 — durable prepared native-text audio / Lock Screen behavior, including partial-render and Stop semantics.

title: [Post-MVP] Validate transport-neutral classroom assignment and return packets
body:
## Build 26 reconciliation — 2026-09-08

The underlying one-way sender/recipient package flow is integrated and bounded-human-validated; the historical unlanded-branch uncertainty in #81 no longer describes the internal baseline. Classroom assignment and return packet contracts are a distinct, still-open feature. Build 26 acceptance is not evidence of this classroom pilot or authorization to implement it.

Evidence: [scope-specific record](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/docs/release-lanes.md), [owner acceptance](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/gate-1/2026-09-08-build-26-acceptance.md), [Build 26 handoff](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-26/build-26-testflight-upload.md).

Build identity: **0.1 (26)**, exact source `9c967793e7a0e86c26a3030390818e87d830723b`; release manifest is **verified** (425 app/adapter/UI tests plus fast checks). The owner recorded **human_validated for the candidate**, without a separate device-by-device or individual-flow matrix. Internal Margins distribution is confirmed; Build 21 remains external. #14 and later-release authorization are unchanged.

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Outcome

Validate the smallest useful classroom workflow from #70 without first committing to accounts, a hosted roster, or a telemetry backend. An instructor creates an assignment manifest, students acquire the referenced source through ordinary Spoken Margins intake, work locally, preview a return packet, and explicitly share it back. The instructor imports one or more packets for source-aligned review.

This is a package-only product pilot and contract boundary, not the final classroom service.

## Actors and authority

- **Instructor/creator:** authors an assignment and one or more return destinations; may name co-instructors for display/review but package exchange alone does not grant server authority.
- **Participant/student:** imports the assignment, resolves the source, listens or reads, records interjections, reviews what will be returned, and explicitly exports it.
- **Reviewer:** imports returned packets and views each participant layer against the bound source.
- **Transport:** Files, share sheet, AirDrop, mail, learning-management upload, or another user-chosen carrier; transport is not identity, authorization, or durable delivery confirmation.

## Package boundaries

### Assignment package

- stable assignment ID, schema version, title, instructions, due date when supplied, and instructor display metadata;
- canonical public/source URL plus source identity/revision/digest expectations;
- acquisition guidance that routes through existing import flows;
- requested evidence policy, clearly distinguishing optional interjections from app-observed or self-attested participation;
- return destination hints without embedded credentials or executable routes.

The package must not redistribute copyrighted source content by default. Bundled content is permitted only when the exporting user has rights and the package contract explicitly supports it.

### Local work binding

- importing an assignment creates a durable binding between the assignment and a locally acquired item/source revision;
- assignment state must not overload or mutate the canonical `Session` playback model;
- mismatched, redirected, changed-edition, unavailable, or paywalled sources remain visible and recoverable rather than silently binding to the wrong item;
- ordinary unassigned library use remains unchanged.

### Return packet

- assignment and source binding;
- participant-chosen display identity appropriate to a package-only pilot;
- selected interjections with durable source anchors and required media assets;
- optional participation receipt from #80;
- package/schema versions, creation time, and integrity digest;
- no unrelated library history, raw event ledger, or unselected private interjections.

## Instructor review

- Import multiple participant packets without overwriting the instructor's own layer or another participant.
- Show source mismatch, unsupported version, missing media, duplicate packet, and integrity warnings before import.
- Provide per-participant and source-position views, with explicit observed/self-attested/unobserved evidence labels.
- Permit local export of a review summary while retaining links back to the underlying anchored interjections.
- Treat AI grouping/synthesis as later work under #26; the pilot must be useful without generated summaries.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An instructor can create and preview an assignment package containing a source link and instructions without redistributing the source itself.
- [ ] A participant can import the assignment, acquire/bind the correct source through existing intake, and recover from unavailable or mismatched editions.
- [ ] Listening, in-app reading, external/self-attested reading, and no-evidence states remain distinct.
- [ ] A participant can preview, include/exclude optional interjections and evidence, cancel, and explicitly share a return packet.
- [ ] An instructor can import at least two participant packets for the same assignment and review their layers without collision.
- [ ] Wrong-source, malformed, unsupported-version, missing-asset, duplicate, oversized, and tampered fixtures fail or warn deterministically.
- [ ] Export/import is idempotent and does not replace the active playback session.
- [ ] Package exchange works through at least Files and the system share sheet without a Spoken Margins server.
- [ ] Schemas, validators, fixture families, runtime paths, and focused tests land together.
- [ ] The product owner human-validates the end-to-end instructor and participant flows before the pilot is described as validated.

## Dependencies and related work

- Epic: #70.
- Blocked by #81 and the verified implementation state of #17.
- #18 supplies the imported-participant-layer model; #19 extends it into recursive asynchronous conversation.
- #14 defines source/content rights boundaries; #27 defines cross-edition anchors.
- Optional receipts consume #80 but do not block validating assignment and interjection exchange without telemetry.
- #22 may add signing later; a package digest does not prove participant identity.
- #26 and #68 cover synthesis and provenance-aware presentation after the one-way exchange works.

## Non-goals

- Hosted classrooms, roster provisioning, accounts, roles, invitations, or an instructor dashboard.
- Guaranteed delivery, revocation, remote deletion, or live synchronization.
- Proving that a student paid attention, understood the source, or authored an interjection.
- Recursive replies, notifications, or AI synthesis in the first package pilot.

## Audit and stopping rule

Run the same assignment across link-only public content, a changed edition, an unavailable/paywalled source, mixed read/listen evidence, two participant returns, duplicate import, and tampered packages. Compare the package-only workflow with two alternatives: ordinary manual sharing and a minimal hosted relay. Do not begin roster/backend work unless the pilot shows repeat use, source-resolution success, and materially better review than manual exchange. Stop calling the pilot privacy-preserving if participants cannot preview and minimize the return packet.

title: [Post-MVP] Record app-observed source coverage for listening and in-app reading
body:
## Outcome

Record a privacy-preserving local observation ledger from which Spoken Margins can deterministically derive how much of a specific source revision the app presented through listening or its own reading surface. The ledger may later supply an optional classroom participation receipt, but it must never be described as proof that a person paid attention, understood, or completed work.

## Current repository gap

- A session retains a latest playback position and completion percentage, not the path used to reach it.
- Seeking can move the latest position without establishing that the skipped interval was presented.
- Replays, interruption boundaries, and mixed reading/listening coverage are not modeled as durable observations.
- The native-text reading sheet is not an instrumented reading surface.
- Interjection chronology needs a real, injectable wall/monotonic clock rather than sequence-derived epoch timestamps before it can support trustworthy ordering evidence.

## Typed boundaries

Keep these layers separate:

### Source binding

- stable item ID;
- source and edition/revision identity;
- canonical coordinate space and mapping version;
- optional content digest that excludes private annotations.

### Observation event

- stable event ID and schema version;
- mode: listening or in-app reading;
- canonical start/end coordinates;
- real wall timestamp for display plus monotonic duration for interval calculation;
- device/session ID suitable for local deduplication;
- reason for opening/closing the interval, such as pause, seek, route change, interruption, background transition, viewport change, or end of item.

### Coverage projection

- normalized non-overlapping canonical intervals by mode;
- union coverage across modes;
- replay/revisit counts kept separate from first coverage;
- explicit unknown/unobserved regions;
- deterministic algorithm and version.

### Receipt/export

- assignment/source binding;
- coverage summary and optional bounded event evidence;
- creation time, schema/algorithm versions, and integrity digest;
- explicit language that the data is app-observed presentation, not attention or comprehension.

## Listening semantics

- Count only intervals for which playback progress was actually confirmed by the canonical session/player spine.
- A forward seek does not cover the skipped interval; a backward seek does not erase prior coverage.
- Playback rate changes elapsed time but not canonical source coverage.
- Commentary/interjection playback does not count as source coverage.
- Pause, interruption, route loss, failed preparation, and unconfirmed background playback close the active interval at the last confirmed position.
- Replays may contribute engagement/revisit statistics but cannot increase union coverage beyond 100 percent.

## In-app reading semantics

- Count reading evidence only from an explicit Spoken Margins reading surface with stable source-coordinate mapping.
- A document open, navigation jump, or rapid scroll to the end does not mark skipped text as covered.
- Visible-range and bounded dwell evidence means only that the app presented that range; it is not eye tracking or proof of attention.
- External reading remains `self_attested` or `unobserved`; do not silently convert it into app-observed coverage.
- Mixed read/listen sessions merge in canonical source coordinates while preserving per-mode evidence.

## Privacy and control

- Keep the detailed ledger local by default.
- Export only after an explicit, previewable user action and minimize event detail to the stated purpose.
- Never collect microphone content, private interjection audio/text, unrelated library history, or background activity merely to compute coverage.
- Let the participant inspect what will be shared, omit optional interjections, and cancel without changing their local work.
- Define retention, deletion, and re-export behavior before adding any relay or server storage.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Versioned schemas/fixtures cover source bindings, observation events, projections, receipts, migrations, and unknown fields.
- [ ] A real injectable clock supplies display timestamps and monotonic interval durations.
- [ ] Forward/backward seeks, playback-rate changes, replay, interruptions, route loss, preparation gaps, termination, and relaunch produce deterministic listening coverage.
- [ ] Open-without-reading, bounded dwell, rapid scrolling, navigation jumps, relaunch, and revision changes produce conservative reading coverage.
- [ ] Mixed reading/listening unions never exceed 100 percent and retain mode-specific intervals.
- [ ] A changed source revision cannot inherit coverage without an explicit compatible mapping.
- [ ] Duplicate/out-of-order events merge idempotently or fail explicitly.
- [ ] Receipt previews distinguish observed, self-attested, and unobserved evidence and never claim attention or comprehension.
- [ ] Local deletion removes the ledger and future exports without rewriting a package the user already shared.
- [ ] Contract validators, focused SessionKit tests, migration tests, and relevant app builds pass.
- [ ] The product owner human-validates the reading/listening disclosures and receipt preview before the flow is described as validated.

## Audit and falsification checks

Replay identical event fixtures through clean install, relaunch, and migration paths and require byte-stable normalized projections where ordering is semantically equivalent. Compare a linear listen, skip-to-end, repeated short loop, rapid scroll, long stationary viewport, mixed-mode coverage, and changed-edition import. Treat seek/scroll inflation, coverage over 100 percent, cross-edition leakage, commentary counted as source, or language implying verified attention as failure.

## Dependencies and related work

- #70 consumes optional participation receipts but does not define the observation ledger.
- #17 defines reviewed interjection packages.
- #27 defines cross-edition anchor behavior.
- #22 may later provide package signing; a digest alone is not identity or non-repudiation.

## Non-goals

- Proving attention, comprehension, authorship, or academic integrity.
- Tracking reading in arbitrary third-party apps or browsers.
- Requiring detailed telemetry sharing to listen, read, or create local interjections.
- Building instructor dashboards or a server relay in this issue.

title: [Post-MVP] Import DRM-free local audiobooks as native audio
body:
## Build 27 owner validation — September 12, 2026

DRM-free owned-audio intake and ordinary playback/resume are accepted under Add and Following / shared listening. Retry Context against a relocated local audio file remains separately open in #109; podcast-description chapter extraction is #119.

The product owner reported using **Build 27** on September 11, accepted all checklist flows except six named problems, and explicitly requested this issue reconciliation on September 12, 2026. Status here is **human_validated by owner report**, not inferred from tests. The report is aggregate acceptance; no separate device/OS matrix or exact installed commit is invented. Subsequent local repairs are not covered by that acceptance.

Evidence: `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md` and the second-edition/current owner checklists in the local workspace. No upload, external approval, or source-baseline promotion is claimed. Original issue text/checklists are preserved below as history; unchecked historical boxes are not a claim that accepted behavior is still failing.

---

## Outcome

Allow a user to import a DRM-free audiobook file from Files and listen through Spoken Margins' canonical native-audio path, preserving embedded chapters when present and retaining ordinary resume and interjection behavior.

## Product boundary

This is local media intake, not TTS:

- The imported audio remains the playback source; do not synthesize the audiobook again.
- Full-source transcription is not required for initial playback.
- DRM-protected files are explicitly out of scope and must be rejected clearly.
- Start with one audio file per imported item. Multi-file folders/disc sets can be a later issue once ordering, duplicate metadata, and shared-book progress have an explicit contract.

## Intake and ownership

- Accept common AVFoundation-readable audiobook/audio containers such as MP3, M4A, M4B, and audio-bearing MP4 when they are not protected.
- Acquire the document-picker/security-scoped URL only long enough to validate and copy the source into app-owned storage.
- Inspect playability, duration, protection state, metadata, artwork when safely available, and embedded chapter metadata before publishing a ready library item.
- Persist the owned file as a native-media representation so playback works offline and after relaunch without depending on the original Files-provider URL.
- Use stable item/media identity and collision-safe storage paths.
- An import failure must not leave a ready item, orphaned media, or a half-copied file.
- Deleting the item removes its owned audio and derived data through the existing cleanup policy.

## Chapters and playback

- Prefer embedded AVFoundation chapter metadata as canonical authored structure.
- Preserve every valid embedded chapter in order; do not impose the adaptive native-text chapter cap.
- A chapterless file remains fully playable as one item rather than requiring generated chapters.
- Use media-time anchors for resume, seeking, skip, interjections, Lock Screen state, and export references.
- Importing in the background must not replace or restart an already active session.
- Reuse the existing native-audio player, duration authority, chapter timing, and interjection context paths rather than introducing an audiobook-only transport.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A DRM-free MP3 imports, copies into app-owned storage, plays offline, and resumes after relaunch.
- [ ] DRM-free M4A/M4B fixtures with embedded chapters expose all chapter titles and navigate to the correct media times.
- [ ] A chapterless file is playable and seekable without a fabricated Listening Map.
- [ ] A protected/DRM fixture is rejected with a useful message and leaves no playable or orphaned item.
- [ ] Malformed, unsupported, zero-duration, interrupted-copy, duplicate-import, low-space, and deleted-source cases fail or recover deterministically.
- [ ] Importing while another item is playing preserves the active session.
- [ ] Interjections remain anchored to the correct audiobook media time before and after pause/resume and relaunch.
- [ ] Deleting an imported audiobook removes the app-owned file without affecting unrelated media.

## Audit / falsification checks

Exercise fixtures across supported containers, metadata encodings, embedded/no chapters, long duration, variable bit rate, protection, corrupted tails, and Files/iCloud providers. Compare app-reported duration and chapter starts against AVFoundation observations. Treat a dependency on the transient picker URL, a silent DRM failure, a lost chapter, a changed active session, an orphaned file, or a resume-time drift as a failure.

## Dependencies and related work

- #46, #55, and #66 cover direct audio URLs or native-audio defects, but not durable local-file intake.
- #72 owns global offline byte accounting and eviction policy.

## Non-goals

- DRM circumvention.
- Multi-file books or disc sets in the initial version.
- Full-source transcription as a playback prerequisite.

body:
## Build 27 scope reconciliation — September 12, 2026

The owner accepts the checklist's existing-Library upgrade and real Safari PDF import flow in Build 27. This supersedes generic pending-owner wording for that bounded route. Keep the broader authored-document/front-matter corpus requirements separate; no per-document or OS-version matrix is invented, and figure narration (#105) is unchanged.

The owner accepted the checklist except six named failures and requested GitHub reconciliation on September 12. Acceptance is owner-reported Build 27, with no inferred exact installed SHA or device-by-device matrix. Original scope is preserved below; later feature expansions and explicit research measurements are not silently marked complete. ---

## Build 26 reconciliation — 2026-09-08

Build 26 includes the post-Build-25 PDF/source-import work. Safari PDF developer proof exists and the candidate is owner-accepted; the old single-commit/default-branch status is superseded. This does not supply an individual authored-PDF corpus or iOS-version acceptance matrix. Keep the canonical chapter/front-matter and representative-document closure requirements; figure narration (#105) is still deferred.

Evidence: [scope-specific record](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/provisional-next/2026-09-04-safari-pdf-manual-proof.md), [owner acceptance](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/gate-1/2026-09-08-build-26-acceptance.md), [Build 26 handoff](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-26/build-26-testflight-upload.md).

Build identity: **0.1 (26)**, exact source `9c967793e7a0e86c26a3030390818e87d830723b`; release manifest is **verified** (425 app/adapter/UI tests plus fast checks). The owner recorded **human_validated for the candidate**, without a separate device-by-device or individual-flow matrix. Internal Margins distribution is confirmed; Build 21 remains external. #14 and later-release authorization are unchanged.

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Problem

Text-based PDF imports can expose a real chapter title in both the table of contents and at the chapter's destination. The extractor previously matched outline titles globally, so the contents-page occurrence could consume the heading and make the chapter begin at the title/author/contents pages. Separately, deterministic maps merged canonical PDF headings down to a hard maximum of 12 chapters even when the document contained more.

A representative regression is an anthology such as G. K. Chesterton's *Tremendous Trifles*: selecting “A Piece of Chalk” should start at that story, not at the book title or contents, and all later stories should remain available.

## Failure model

- **Extraction:** PDF encodings and line geometry vary; outline destinations are stronger evidence than title text alone.
- **Canonical structure:** authored PDF outline/heading boundaries must not be treated like optional listening-length suggestions.
- **Listening structure:** title, authors, summary, and contents may be useful but must not be silently folded into the first story.
- **Verification:** generated fixtures and a representative real-world corpus are needed because one PDF shape cannot falsify the heuristics.

## Required behavior

- Match an outline title only at its destination page/position rather than the first same-title occurrence in the document.
- Treat an explicit Contents/Table of Contents label, repeated off-destination outline-title matches, dot leaders, and trailing page numbers as contents evidence rather than chapter starts.
- Preserve nonempty material before the first canonical chapter as a separate `Front Matter` entry.
- Preserve every detected canonical PDF heading without a fixed 12-chapter ceiling.
- Keep ranges ordered, contiguous, and anchored to the real chapter text.
- Retain adaptive merge/split behavior for ordinary Markdown; this bug concerns canonical PDF structure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A generated PDF with title/author material, a contents page, and 20 destination-backed stories produces exactly `Front Matter` plus all 20 story chapters.
- [ ] Clicking the first story begins at its actual destination, not character zero.
- [ ] Contents entries do not appear as duplicate chapters.
- [ ] Numbered headings on an ordinary content page are not suppressed without additional contents evidence.
- [ ] Duplicate/similar titles remain associated with their own destinations.
- [ ] PDFs without usable outlines continue to use conservative visual-heading fallback.
- [ ] Scanned/image-only PDFs continue to fail clearly unless OCR has already supplied text.

## Audit / stopping rule

Evaluate a small corpus spanning publisher outlines, visual headings only, contents with and without page numbers, duplicate titles, nested outlines, multi-page contents, and malformed/no-outline PDFs. Compare chapter precision/recall and anchor-page accuracy against the prior implementation. Stop or narrow any heuristic that increases false chapter suppression on ordinary content pages. Product-owner use is required before marking the flow human-validated.

## Implementation status

Implemented on the main working tree with focused package coverage and a generated 20-story PDF regression fixture. Keep this issue open until the product owner validates the flow on a representative PDF.
