title: Onboarding: remotely configurable guided podcast and import hotlinks

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
## Product-owner expansion — 2026-09-11

Expand onboarding from a guided tutorial into an optional **setup walkthrough** that helps a new user leave onboarding with useful sources and integrations already configured. The interaction can take inspiration from Snipd's onboarding pattern without copying its UI or requiring a hosted recommendation profile.

### Select initial podcasts and blogs to follow

During onboarding, offer a browsable/selectable set of starter **podcasts and article/blog sources** and allow the user to follow several before reaching the main Library.

- The walkthrough should make following optional and reversible; no source is followed merely because it appears in onboarding.
- Reuse the canonical local subscription model from #76 rather than creating onboarding-only subscriptions.
- The source catalog may be product-owner configurable, but remote configuration may only reference validated source/feed identities and presentation metadata; it must not silently subscribe the user.
- The user should be able to search/add another source or skip the recommendations entirely.
- Podcast and blog/article sources should use the same understandable follow/unfollow vocabulary even though their entry types differ.

### Configure a read-later / Quick Import workflow

Onboarding should expose the existing **Quick Import folder** configuration rather than leaving it as an advanced discovery task.

- Let the user choose/review the folder Spoken Margins watches for quick imports.
- Explain that compatible read-later or web-clipping tools can write files into that folder.
- Use Obsidian Web Clipper as a representative validation workflow, while keeping the contract Files/folder-provider neutral.
- Provide a simple test step: save/clip one supported item and confirm that Spoken Margins can see/import it.
- Folder permissions, revoked bookmarks, unsupported files, and duplicate imports must produce recoverable states rather than silently failing.

### Surface OPML and notes-output setup

The onboarding walkthrough should link into:

- **Import OPML** for users bringing an existing podcast/blog subscription set (#76); and
- **Configure Margin output** for users who want their Margins/anchors to flow into a notes/PKM workflow (#16).

These routes must reuse the real production settings/import/export surfaces, not onboarding-only implementations.

### Added acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh user can select multiple starter podcasts/blogs, review the selections, and create canonical #76 subscriptions in one onboarding flow.
- [ ] Skipping source selection creates no subscriptions and does not reduce access to the normal Sources UI later.
- [ ] The selectable starter catalog can be updated without silently changing existing subscriptions.
- [ ] Onboarding can configure/review the Quick Import folder and verify one real file-based clipping/import round trip.
- [ ] The walkthrough provides direct production routes to OPML import and notes/PKM output configuration.
- [ ] Re-running onboarding/setup does not duplicate subscriptions, imports, or export destinations.
- [ ] Product-owner validation covers a first-run path using selected podcasts/blogs, a Quick Import folder fed by Obsidian Web Clipper, and subsequent editing/skipping of every setup choice.

---

## Outcome

Give new users two starter items:

1. the existing native-text “Welcome to Spoken Margins” item; and
2. a podcast-format guided tour that explains and links users into the ways they can add their own content.

The guided podcast must be product-owner configurable after release so its audio, metadata, and instructions can be updated without shipping a new App Store build.

## Why

The current onboarding can ask a user to add a podcast, but it does not provide an audio-first walkthrough of the available import paths. If the app’s workflows change, an onboarding tutorial bundled entirely in the binary becomes stale until the next app release.

## Experience requirements

- A fresh install/library seed contains a second starter item whose source type and playback behavior are genuinely podcast/audio, not native text rendered as speech.
- The item is clearly identified as a Spoken Margins guided tour and can be played with the normal podcast listening experience.
- The tour walks through all currently supported content-ingestion paths:
  - import/upload a PDF;
  - paste native text;
  - add a webpage through the supported browser integration/share flow;
  - paste a podcast or episode link;
  - share a podcast or episode into Spoken Margins through the share sheet.
- Actionable prompts or “hotlinks” in the tour/onboarding open the relevant in-app destination. For example, tapping the prompt to add a podcast opens the same add-item sheet available from the library “plus” button.
- Links use existing routes/actions rather than creating onboarding-only versions of import flows.
- VoiceOver labels explain the destination and do not rely on the question-mark icon alone.

## Content and delivery contract

Keep these layers separate:

- **Bundled seed definition:** establishes that the starter item exists on first launch and provides a safe fallback.
- **Remote product-owner configuration:** controls the current tutorial audio/source URL and user-facing metadata (at minimum title, description, artwork if supported, and content version).
- **App routing:** maps tutorial actions to supported import destinations.
- **User library state:** tracks whether the starter item was created, dismissed/deleted, played, and how updates affect progress.

The remote mechanism may be a small versioned manifest or an equivalent service-backed configuration, but it must:

- allow the product owner to publish a revised tutorial without an app release;
- use authenticated HTTPS and validate the response before applying it;
- define stable item identity separately from content version so refreshes do not create duplicates;
- define whether an update preserves or resets playback progress, and surface that behavior consistently;
- respect a user deletion/dismissal decision rather than silently re-adding the item on every launch;
- retain the last-known-good configuration or bundled fallback when the network or remote configuration is unavailable;
- document the product-owner publishing/rollback workflow.

Changing the remote tutorial may update onboarding content and metadata, but must not remotely introduce new executable routes or bypass the app’s supported import and security boundaries.

## Original observation

During onboarding, the question-mark prompt asks the user to add a podcast. Make that prompt tappable so it opens the same “plus” add-item sheet.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean install shows exactly the intended two starter items: the existing native-text welcome item and one guided podcast item.
- [ ] The guided item plays through the normal podcast/audio path.
- [ ] The tutorial accurately covers PDF, pasted text, browser/web sharing, pasted podcast links, and podcast share-sheet ingestion.
- [ ] Each actionable onboarding prompt opens the correct existing import UI, including the add-item sheet from the podcast prompt.
- [ ] Publishing a new tutorial content version updates the guided item on a test install without rebuilding or reinstalling the app.
- [ ] Refreshing the same version does not duplicate the starter item.
- [ ] Offline, malformed-response, removed-audio, and rollback cases use a defined last-known-good or bundled fallback.
- [ ] Deleting/dismissing the starter podcast is respected across launches and remote refreshes.
- [ ] Playback-progress behavior across a tutorial update is specified and verified.
- [ ] Routes and prompts are accessible with VoiceOver.
- [ ] The product-owner update and rollback steps are documented and exercised against a non-production test configuration.

## Verification evidence

- clean-install seed test showing the two distinct source types;
- route-level tests for every hotlink/import destination;
- configuration-version tests for first fetch, unchanged refresh, update, rollback, malformed data, and offline launch;
- persistence tests for duplicate prevention, deletion/dismissal, and playback progress;
- developer evidence that an updated remote tutorial appears without a new binary;
- product-owner validation of the actual onboarding and publishing workflow before closure.

## Stopping rules

Do not close this issue if the tutorial is still binary-only, if remote refresh can duplicate or resurrect a deleted starter item, or if automated checks are the only evidence for the user-facing onboarding flow.

## Same-release route expansion

The numbered quality-of-life release also introduces DRM-free EPUB and local audiobook import. The final tour and every route fixture must therefore cover these paths in addition to the existing PDF, pasted text, webpage/browser, and podcast paths:

- import a DRM-free EPUB through the shared Add Source flow;
- import one supported MP3, M4A, M4B, or audio-bearing MP4 audiobook file through the shared Add Source flow.

The remote manifest may select only a compiled, closed onboarding route identifier. EPUB and audiobook routes must reuse the production import UI; remote content cannot define a URL scheme, arbitrary destination, or executable navigation. This issue is not complete if the shipped tour is stale relative to either new import path.

**Not human_validated: owner retry pending.** Build 27 Timeline did not adequately distinguish publisher chapters/generated scenes from own or another person's Margins. The product owner reported using **Build 27** on September 11, accepted all checklist flows except six named problems, and explicitly requested this issue reconciliation on September 12, 2026. The report is aggregate acceptance; no separate device/OS matrix or exact installed commit is invented. Subsequent local repairs are not covered by that acceptance.

Evidence: `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md` and the second-edition/current owner checklists in the local workspace. No upload, external approval, or source-baseline promotion is claimed. Original issue text/checklists are preserved below as history; unchecked historical boxes are not a claim that accepted behavior is still failing.

---

## Feature request

Make listener interjections immediately distinguishable from ordinary source/chapter entries in the Timeline.

External tester feedback on the Welcome to Spoken Margins flow, 2026-08-22:

> “I sort of wish the interjections that are slotted into the timeline chapters would be flagged with a different color. That would help me know which ones were mine and which ones were the, um, regular ones.”

## Problem

Interjections and source structure currently appear similar enough in the Timeline that a listener has to inspect an entry to determine whether it represents:

- source/chapter structure, or
- something the listener contributed.

That makes it harder to scan where the listener reacted to the source.

## Desired behavior

- “My interjections” are visually distinct from source/chapter Timeline entries at a glance.
- A different accent/color may be part of the distinction, following the tester's suggestion.
- Do not use color as the only semantic signal; pair it with an icon, marker shape, label, typography, or another accessible cue.
- VoiceOver identifies the entry type, e.g. “My interjection” versus “Chapter” or the applicable source-entry type.
- The distinction remains understandable in Light Mode, Dark Mode, increased contrast, and common color-vision conditions.
- Existing Timeline ordering, anchoring, navigation, and tap behavior remain unchanged.

## Design boundary

Prefer a provenance-based visual vocabulary rather than a one-off hard-coded color.

The same vocabulary should be extensible later to:

1. source/chapter entries
2. My interjections
3. imported/person-specific commentary layers

The third case is tracked in #18, which already requires imported layers to remain distinct from “My interjections.”

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Timeline containing both chapters/source entries and listener interjections makes the two classes distinguishable without opening an entry.
- [ ] The distinction is not color-only.
- [ ] VoiceOver communicates whether an entry is source content or the listener's interjection.
- [ ] Light Mode, Dark Mode, and increased-contrast presentation remain legible.
- [ ] Pending, completed, and failed-transcription interjections retain the same authorship/provenance cue.
- [ ] Existing chapter jump and interjection-review behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] The styling model can accommodate imported commentary layers from #18 without conflating them with local interjections.

## Source

External tester feedback, 2026-08-22, from the Welcome to Spoken Margins guided listening session.

Related: #18.

title: [Critical regression] Native-audio interjections lose source context despite available/offline audio

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: phase: recovery-mvp
labels.description: Required before Recovery MVP human validation

body:
## Summary

There is a critical regression in the core interjection flow for native audio/podcast items: voice interjections are recorded and transcribed, but Spoken Margins fails to capture the surrounding source context and reports that the source audio is unavailable **even when the item is playable and explicitly marked Available Offline**.

This breaks the primary value of an interjection: preserving what the listener said **in relation to the source passage that prompted it**. The reporter states this failure has occurred before, later worked again, and has now regressed again.

## Impact / severity

Treat this as a release-blocking core-path regression until falsified.

Without `anchorBefore` / `anchorAfter` (or equivalent bounded source context):

- saved interjections lose the source evidence needed to interpret them later;
- AI handoff/export becomes materially less useful because listener notes are detached from the surrounding argument;
- downstream summary/discussion/share behavior cannot reliably resolve references in the listener's note;
- retrying later does not provide confidence that the context was actually captured at interjection time.

The interjection transcript alone is not an acceptable success state when source audio is available.

## Reproduction evidence

Captured on a physical iPhone on 2026-08-19.

**Item:** Former Singularity Institute President: PauseAI Is Making AI Doom WORSE  
**Apple Podcasts:** https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/doom-debates/id1751366208?i=1000784122318  
**Source URL:** https://api.substack.com/feed/podcast/211656415/fc97590468e7ecace0fbde6b2d5810c7.mp3  
**Source type:** `remote_stream`

Observed item state in the UI:

- `Ready`
- `30 chapters`
- `28 interjections`
- **Available Offline**
- listening session `in_progress`
- approximately 84% complete

The session contains 28 interjections spanning approximately **12:22 through 1:25:29**.

Opening an affected interjection shows:

> Context status  
> Unavailable — retry when audio is available

and both:

> Before — Context unavailable  
> After — Context unavailable

A **Retry Context** action is offered even though the parent item is already marked **Available Offline**.

The supplied AI Handoff contains all of the listener interjection transcripts but no surrounding source-context entries for the affected interjections.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Import/open the Apple Podcasts episode above as native audio.
2. Allow the item to become playable and download it so the detail screen shows **Available Offline**.
3. Start or continue a listening session.
4. While the podcast is playing, record a voice interjection.
5. Allow transcription to complete.
6. Open the saved interjection details.
7. Inspect **Context status**, **Before**, and **After**.
8. Export/copy the AI Handoff and inspect the source context associated with the interjection.

## Actual behavior

- Interjection recording succeeds.
- Interjection transcription succeeds.
- Source-context capture fails.
- UI reports that source audio is unavailable.
- `Before` and `After` are both unavailable.
- The failure occurs despite the item being playable and available offline.
- The handoff retains the listener notes but loses the source context that should anchor them.

## Expected behavior

For native audio, an interjection created while the source is playable must retain a durable media-time anchor and enough bounded source evidence to recover/produce the before/after context.

In particular:

- If downloaded audio exists, context extraction must use the verified local media representation.
- If local media is absent but the remote source is currently usable, context extraction may use the remote representation.
- A `remote_stream` source identity must not cause the context path to ignore an existing offline/downloaded representation.
- Temporary decoding/readiness failure must be explicit and retryable without losing the original media-time anchor.
- The app must not report “audio unavailable” while another authoritative part of the app considers the same item's audio available and playable.

## Hypotheses to falsify

These are investigation targets, not established root causes:

1. **Representation mismatch:** the context resolver keys off `sourceType == remote_stream` and looks only for the remote source instead of resolving the currently available downloaded/local representation.
2. **Split availability state:** playback/download UI and interjection-context extraction consult different media-availability stores, allowing one to say “Available Offline” while the other sees no audio.
3. **Lifecycle/race regression:** context capture is scheduled after the interjection while the source/player asset has been released or its temporary URL is no longer considered valid.
4. **Anchor persistence regression:** media time is captured but the context job cannot resolve that anchor back onto the cached asset.
5. **Download migration/cache-key mismatch:** the offline file is present under a canonical/downloaded item identity that the context extractor no longer matches to the original `remote_stream` source.

Instrumentation should distinguish these states rather than collapsing all of them into “source audio unavailable.”

## Required diagnostics

For each interjection context job, log/record at minimum:

- item/source ID and source type;
- canonical media-time anchor captured at interjection start;
- active playback representation and URL/asset identity;
- downloaded/offline asset identity and existence/readability;
- remote source availability;
- selected representation for context extraction;
- exact failure stage: resolve asset, open asset, seek, decode, transcribe, map timeline, persist context;
- retry result and whether it reused the original anchor.

Do not include private full transcripts in diagnostics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the exact episode above, a newly recorded interjection while the item is **Available Offline** receives valid bounded `Before` and `After` source context.
- [ ] The first interjection after cold launch works; this is not dependent on warming a player/transcriber path first.
- [ ] Repeated interjections throughout a long podcast do not progressively lose context.
- [ ] Context extraction works for an offline/downloaded representation whose canonical source remains `remote_stream`.
- [ ] Context extraction also works for a remote-only native-audio item when the remote media is actually available.
- [ ] If media truly is unavailable, the durable media-time anchor remains intact and **Retry Context** succeeds once the media becomes available.
- [ ] UI availability and context-resolver availability cannot disagree about the same verified local asset without emitting a diagnostic invariant failure.
- [ ] AI Handoff/export includes the expected bounded source context for successfully resolved interjections.
- [ ] Regression tests cover remote-only, downloaded/offline, app relaunch, background/foreground, and many-interjection sessions.
- [ ] A test specifically fails if an item is marked **Available Offline** while context extraction returns the generic “source audio unavailable” state for the same representation.

## Regression protection

This behavior has reportedly oscillated between broken and working states. Add an end-to-end contract test at the media-representation boundary rather than only unit-testing the context extractor in isolation. The test should create a `remote_stream` item, attach/verify an offline representation, capture an interjection at a known media time, resolve before/after context, relaunch, and repeat.

## Related

- #42 defines bounded `anchorBefore` / `anchorAfter` as the source context used to interpret interjections.
- #56 is a downstream interjection-summary failure; this issue is an upstream source-context/anchor failure and should be fixed independently.
- #46 owns podcast intake/downloaded representations and may be relevant if the regression is in remote-to-offline representation resolution.

title: Regression: native-text playback can no longer be scrubbed in-app
body:
## Summary

The in-app progress control no longer allows scrubbing while listening to a native-text item. This is a regression: native-text playback was previously seekable from within Spoken Margins.

We intentionally removed scrubbing from Apple’s Lock Screen / Now Playing controls because system scrubbing did not work reliably for native-text playback. That change appears to have also disabled the app’s own scrubber, which was not intended.

## Reproduction

1. Open a native-text item in Spoken Margins.
2. Start playback.
3. Attempt to drag the in-app progress scrubber to another position.

## Observed behavior

The in-app scrubber cannot be used to seek within the native-text item.

## Expected behavior

- Native-text playback remains scrubbable inside Spoken Margins.
- Apple Lock Screen / Now Playing scrubbing remains unavailable while the active native-text representation cannot support it reliably.
- The capabilities of the in-app transport and system remote transport are controlled independently, so disabling system scrubbing does not remove local seeking.

## Suggested investigation

- Inspect the change that removed Lock Screen / Now Playing scrubbing for native text.
- Check whether a shared seekability flag, duration publication rule, or command-registration path now gates both remote and in-app seeking.
- Separate UI-local seek capability from `MPRemoteCommandCenter` / Now Playing seek capability.
- Confirm that a local seek updates the authoritative native-text position and that playback and progress tracking continue from the selected position.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] During native-text playback, dragging the in-app scrubber seeks to the selected position.
- [ ] Playback resumes or continues from the selected position, and progress advances correctly afterward.
- [ ] Lock Screen / Control Center scrubbing is not advertised or enabled for live native-text playback where it is unsupported.
- [ ] Disabling remote/system scrubbing does not alter in-app seek availability.
- [ ] Regression coverage verifies in-app scrubbing with remote/system scrubbing disabled.
- [ ] Existing play, pause, skip-back, and skip-forward behavior remains intact.

## Related

- #62 — Lock-screen transport/state regression
- #64 — Post-MVP prepared native-text audio and Lock Screen scrubbing

title: [Post-MVP] Durable prepared native-text audio and Lock Screen scrubbing
body:
## Build 27 scope reconciliation — September 12, 2026

Current playback/preparation/reuse and remote-transport checklist flows retain Build 27 owner acceptance; #98 closes for preparation recovery. Keep this broader durable-audio issue open for its explicit termination/invalidation and physical-resource evidence matrix where not already recorded. Current-flow acceptance is not a fabricated thermal or chunk-boundary test result.

The owner accepted the checklist except six named failures and requested GitHub reconciliation on September 12. Acceptance is owner-reported Build 27, with no inferred exact installed SHA or device-by-device matrix. Original scope is preserved below; later feature expansions and explicit research measurements are not silently marked complete. Evidence: local `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md`.

---

## Build 26 reconciliation — 2026-09-08

Durable prepared audio is implemented in the internal baseline; Build 26 adds compatible-artifact reuse, playback/preparation remediation, and accepted scrubber work. The original future-tense live-only framing is historical. Keep the full persistence/invalidation/offline/Lock Screen matrix distinct from candidate acceptance and from the remaining Item Detail preparation-recovery seam in #98.

Evidence: [scope-specific record](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/reviews/2026-09-07-testflight-stabilization/implementation.md), [owner acceptance](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/gate-1/2026-09-08-build-26-acceptance.md), [Build 26 handoff](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-26/build-26-testflight-upload.md).

Build identity: **0.1 (26)**, exact source `9c967793e7a0e86c26a3030390818e87d830723b`; release manifest is **verified** (425 app/adapter/UI tests plus fast checks). The owner recorded **human_validated for the candidate**, without a separate device-by-device or individual-flow matrix. Internal Margins distribution is confirmed; Build 21 remains external. #14 and later-release authorization are unchanged.

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Summary

After MVP, make native-text narration a durable prepared-media representation so it can use the same canonical duration, media-time seeking, and Apple Now Playing scrubbing model as podcasts.

This replaces the current live-speech limitation; it is not an MVP patch for the synthetic Now Playing duration. MVP transport/state correctness remains in #62.

## Product boundary

### MVP (#62)

- Never publish an invented duration for live native text.
- Do not advertise Lock Screen scrubbing when the active representation cannot safely seek by media time.
- Keep Lock Screen / Control Center play, pause, skip-back, and skip-forward synchronized with the canonical native-text session.
- Remote transport must not change the selected voice/runtime.

### Post-MVP (this issue)

- Render native-text audio progressively and persistently.
- Promote the completed representation to `generated_tts_prerendered`.
- Publish one accurate whole-item duration and enable arbitrary Apple Now Playing scrubbing.

## Required execution model

1. On native-text import, normalize the source and create a stable chunk plan.
2. Persist an item-level render manifest keyed by:
   - item/source-text hash;
   - voice identifier and synthesis-engine/model version;
   - synthesis parameters that affect generated audio;
   - manifest/schema version.
3. Render one chunk at a time to a temporary file.
4. After a chunk succeeds, atomically commit its audio plus source-character range, duration, cumulative media-time range, and integrity metadata.
5. If the process terminates while chunk N is rendering:
   - chunks before N remain committed;
   - the incomplete temporary file for N is discarded;
   - no partial chunk is treated as playable.
6. Relaunch does **not** automatically resume every incomplete library item. When the user next opens that item, verify the manifest signature and restart the first incomplete chunk from its beginning.
7. Changing source text, voice, or synthesis version marks the old manifest stale. Playback-rate changes do not require rerendering.
8. Do not switch an already playing live-speech session to prepared media mid-session. Adopt the completed prepared representation on the next safe playback start.
9. When the manifest is complete, attach it through the existing prepared-text media path and use the canonical media player/timeline.

## Playback behavior while incomplete

- Prioritize enough initial audio for prompt playback. Further serial preparation follows #73: normally current plus bounded next-chapter demand on battery, with longer opportunistic preparation only while device conditions permit.
- Do not publish a fabricated whole-item duration.
- Do not enable arbitrary system scrubbing until the complete, verified timeline exists.
- If playback reaches the rendered boundary, expose a buffering/preparing state; do not silently switch voice/runtime.
- Deleting the item removes its manifest and owned render files.
- Cache eviction must leave the source item playable and able to render again.

## Durable-render execution constraints

This issue defines how eligible chunks are rendered and committed durably. It does not require unconditional full-item rendering. Eligibility, preparation horizon, battery/charging behavior, Low Power Mode, and jump reprioritization belong to #73.

- Run at most one resource-intensive item render job at a time and render eligible chunks sequentially.
- Reuse the warm Supertonic runtime only while another currently eligible chunk is ready to start, then unload it after completion, cancellation, or loss of eligibility.
- Check thermal state before starting each next chunk. Pause before another chunk begins under serious or critical thermal pressure; preserve every atomically committed chunk.
- Resume from the first incomplete chunk only when the device returns to an eligible thermal state and the item is still eligible.
- Expose item-level state and progress: not prepared, preparing with completed/total progress, thermally paused, stopped, failed, and ready offline.
- Provide Stop. Stopping prevents later chunks from starting, preserves completed work, and lets active playback continue through the lower-compute iOS system voice. An already-running synchronous inference call may finish, but its valid output should remain reusable.
- Automatic preparation skips an item when any listening session is substantially complete (initial threshold: 90%).
- An explicit user action such as **Prepare Audio** may override the substantially-complete skip.
- Do not sweep or resume every incomplete library item at launch. Automatic work is limited to the eligible horizon supplied by #73; “active/newly imported eligible item” does not imply rendering the entire item on battery. Explicit preparation controls any other item.
- Count every committed chunk, completed artifact, and retained Watch derivative through the unified offline-storage ledger in #72. Until that ledger exists, automatic preparation must use a conservative temporary quota that accounts for completed packages as well as chunks; it must not assume podcast download settings bound prepared audio. Lowering a limit must not make the source item unplayable.

### Scheduling and consumer boundary

This issue owns the durable render representation, resumability, foreground/on-demand preparation behavior, and promotion into canonical prepared playback.

- #74 owns opt-in `BGProcessingTask` scheduling while connected to power, durable preparation jobs, expiration handling, and best-effort overnight execution.
- #73 owns the eligible-chunk horizon, battery/charging policy, and chapter-jump reprioritization in foreground and background execution.
- #75 consumes the same completed representation and source-to-media mapping; it must not create a second Watch-specific TTS renderer.
- #72 owns total byte accounting, reservations, protection reasons, and cross-category eviction.

Completion of this issue alone must not be read as permission to sweep the library in the background, exceed a truthful global storage limit, or transfer packages to Watch.

### Thermal scheduling acceptance checks

- [ ] Instrumented tests prove maximum whole-item render concurrency is one.
- [ ] Simulated serious/critical thermal state prevents the next chunk from starting while retaining earlier committed chunks.
- [ ] Returning to an eligible thermal state resumes at the first missing chunk without rerendering valid chunks.
- [ ] Progress and state are derived from the durable manifest and survive relaunch.
- [ ] Stop prevents subsequent chunk scheduling, retains valid completed output, and continues active playback through system speech.
- [ ] Automatic preparation skips items with a session at or above 90% completion.
- [ ] Explicit **Prepare Audio** overrides the completion skip.
- [ ] Finishing or canceling a render releases the warm model runtime.
- [ ] Physical-device evidence records render duration, renderer invocation count, peak thermal state, battery impact, and time to thermal recovery for representative short and long items.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A durable manifest records the exact render signature, chunk state, source ranges, per-chunk duration, cumulative media-time ranges, and owned files.
- [ ] Terminating during each tested chunk boundary preserves all earlier committed chunks and discards/restarts only the incomplete chunk.
- [ ] Opening the same item after relaunch resumes from the first incomplete chunk without rerendering earlier valid chunks.
- [ ] Text, voice, or synthesis-version changes invalidate incompatible output; playback-speed changes do not.
- [ ] A completed item plays through the canonical prepared/native-media route with one accurate whole-item duration.
- [ ] Lock Screen and Control Center scrubbing seek to the corresponding source position and remain synchronized after foregrounding.
- [ ] Scrubbing, skipping, pausing, and resuming never change the selected voice/runtime.
- [ ] Partial manifests never expose a misleading full-duration scrubber.
- [ ] Every manifest-owned chunk and complete artifact has stable ownership/byte metadata consumable by #72; eviction, deletion, corrupt-file recovery, and low-space failure leave the source item recoverable.
- [ ] Durable rendering accepts a changing eligible-chunk horizon without corrupting, deleting, or rerendering compatible committed chunks.
- [ ] Completion of a durable whole-item representation is optional progress, not a prerequisite for bounded long-form playback.
- [ ] Tests prove execution obeys the scheduling decision supplied by #73 rather than independently scheduling every remaining chunk.
- [ ] Real-device evidence covers termination/relaunch, long-item rendering, thermal behavior, background/foreground transitions, and Lock Screen transport.

## Audit / falsification checks

- Kill the app while every representative chunk is in progress and compare the post-launch manifest and file set.
- Count renderer invocations to prove valid committed chunks are not regenerated.
- Round-trip representative source offsets through source → media time → source and require monotonic mappings.
- Compare prepared native text against the podcast/native-media route for duration, seek, pause, resume, and Now Playing behavior.
- Treat any voice switch, duplicated chunk, backward timeline movement, orphaned file, or advertised seek outside verified media as a failure.

Related: #61, #62, #72, #73, #74, and #75. Existing prepared-media and rendered-chunk infrastructure should be reused rather than introducing a new source category.

title: [Investigation] Podcast rewind / fast-forward can be temporarily unresponsive after Spotify link import
body:
## Summary

Investigate an intermittent startup/readiness issue where the podcast rewind / fast-forward controls can initially appear nonfunctional after opening an episode imported from a Spotify link, then begin working shortly afterward without any explicit recovery action.

This is intentionally an **investigation** issue rather than a confirmed deterministic bug. The reporter later suspected they may simply not have waited long enough for the episode/player to finish loading.

## User report

Captured from app feedback on 2026-08-16:

> “the reverse 15 seconds/fast forward seems to not be working for me. Was able to load in the link from Spotify to the podcast episode which is super cool”
>
> ~2 minutes later: “Interesting the buttons are working for me now”
>
> “Maybe I just wasnt waiting for it to load”

## Observed behavior

- A podcast episode imported/opened from a Spotify link loads successfully.
- Immediately afterward, rewind / fast-forward controls may appear to do nothing.
- After additional loading time, the same controls can start working normally.
- No explicit retry, reload, or recovery action was reported.

## Expected behavior

Transport controls should not silently accept taps before the underlying media is seekable.

Either:

1. rewind / fast-forward works as soon as the controls are presented as active, or
2. the controls clearly communicate that seeking is not ready yet and become enabled when it is.

## Investigation

- Reproduce from a cold/fresh launch using a Spotify episode link and a remote-stream podcast source.
- Record the state of the player when the controls are first rendered and on each ignored/accepted seek command:
  - player/item readiness
  - duration availability
  - seekable time ranges
  - buffering/loading state
  - remote vs locally cached media state
  - canonical playback coordinator/session state
- Check whether the UI enables transport before the underlying `AVPlayerItem`/media source is actually seekable.
- Check whether an early seek command is dropped while the item is preparing, then later commands succeed once readiness changes.
- Verify whether Spotify-link intake adds a timing/race difference compared with opening the same podcast through another source path.
- Confirm whether the first seek can be queued safely, rejected explicitly, or should keep the controls disabled until readiness.
- Add diagnostics that distinguish “seek command received but media not ready” from “seek executed but position did not change.”

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The team can either reproduce the temporary unresponsive state or capture enough diagnostics to classify why an early seek is ignored.
- [ ] Rewind / fast-forward never fail silently because media is still preparing.
- [ ] If seeking is not available yet, the UI exposes a clear loading/unavailable state and becomes interactive when seeking is supported.
- [ ] Once controls are enabled, the first rewind / fast-forward command changes playback position reliably.
- [ ] Focused regression coverage exercises a newly imported remote podcast before and after media readiness transitions.
- [ ] Verification includes a Spotify-link import path and at least one non-Spotify podcast-open path to determine whether the issue is import-specific or general playback readiness.

## Related

Potentially related transport/state work exists in #62, but this report is distinct: it concerns **initial podcast media readiness after link import**, not Lock Screen native-text/TTS state desynchronization.

title: Lock-screen rewind can desynchronize native-text playback, switch voice, and freeze scrubber

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
## Summary
Using Apple’s Lock Screen / Now Playing skip-back control during native-text/TTS playback can push the playback session into an inconsistent state. The observed failure included an unexpected switch to the configured Accessibility/system voice, incorrect in-app transport controls, play/pause state that disagreed with audible playback, an initially nonfunctional seek/skip action, and a progress scrubber that stopped advancing after seeking backward.

This appears related to playback-state ownership/synchronization, but is distinct from the Live Activity-specific drift tracked in #58 and #59 because this repro starts from Apple’s native Now Playing controls and affects the in-app native-text/TTS transport itself.

## Reproduction
1. Start a native-text/TTS listening session and allow audio to play normally.
2. Leave the app / use the Lock Screen Now Playing controls.
3. Tap the Apple skip-back / rewind control.
4. In the observed repro, playback effectively stopped/reconfigured and then resumed using the configured Accessibility/system voice instead of the expected voice/runtime.
5. Reopen Spoken Margins.
6. Observe that the in-app backward/forward controls have changed from the normal interval-skip controls to previous/next-style transport icons.
7. Observe that the central control shows **Play** (UI thinks playback is paused) even though audio is actively playing.
8. Tap the play/pause control once. The UI then resynchronizes with the audible playback state and playback can continue.
9. Try skip forward/backward again. The first attempt may do nothing; later attempts can begin working normally.
10. Seek/scrub backward (observed to about 31%). Audio continues from the new position, but the progress scrubber remains stuck at that value and never resumes advancing.

## Observed behavior
- Lock-screen skip-back can cause native-text playback to fall onto the configured Accessibility/system voice unexpectedly.
- In-app transport buttons can change semantics/icons from interval skip-back/skip-forward to previous/next-style controls.
- In-app play/pause can show **Play** while audio is audibly playing.
- One additional play/pause tap can resynchronize the UI and actual playback state.
- The first subsequent skip/seek command may be ignored.
- After manually scrubbing backward, audible playback can continue while the progress bar remains permanently frozen at the seeked percentage (31% in this repro).

## Expected behavior
- Lock Screen / Control Center transport commands operate on the same authoritative playback coordinator as the in-app controls.
- A remote skip/seek never changes the selected TTS voice/runtime unless the user explicitly changes it.
- In-app transport affordances retain the configured skip semantics throughout the session.
- Play/pause state always reflects actual audible playback without requiring a corrective tap.
- Every accepted remote or local seek updates the canonical playback position once; rejected commands are clean no-ops and do not partially mutate playback state.
- After seeking, the scrubber immediately reflects the new position and continues advancing from that position while audio plays.

## Suggested investigation
- Verify `MPRemoteCommandCenter` ownership and command registration for native-text/TTS sessions, especially skip-back/skip-forward versus previous/next-track handlers.
- Check whether a Lock Screen seek invalidates the prepared/current TTS runtime and accidentally falls through to a system/Accessibility voice path.
- Confirm there is exactly one source of truth for `isPlaying`, current source position, rendered-audio position, selected voice/runtime, and transport profile.
- Inspect whether remote seek handling updates one position store while the UI progress timer observes another stale store.
- Check for command-handler re-registration or target-mode changes after backgrounding/foregrounding that could explain the transport icons changing.
- Verify that a failed first skip does not leave a pending seek or stale command state that later operations inherit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Repeated Lock Screen skip-back/skip-forward commands during native-text playback do not change the selected TTS voice/runtime.
- [ ] Lock Screen, Control Center, in-app controls, and audible playback agree on play/pause state after every remote command and app foreground transition.
- [ ] The in-app transport controls retain the intended interval-skip behavior and do not silently become previous/next controls.
- [ ] The first skip/seek after returning to the app works or fails explicitly without corrupting session state.
- [ ] Scrubbing backward or forward updates the authoritative position and the progress bar continues advancing from the new position while audio plays.
- [ ] Regression coverage exercises background → remote skip/seek → foreground → local play/pause → local seek for native-text/TTS playback.
- [ ] Regression coverage verifies voice/runtime identity as well as position and `isPlaying` state.

## Evidence
A screenshot from the affected session shows the scrubber at **31%**, the central transport control rendering **Play**, and the backward/forward controls in previous/next-style form after the failure.

Related: #58, #59. Historical native-text progress/state regression: #13.

title: Support DRM-free EPUBs with canonical chapter playback and interjections
body:
## Goal
Add DRM-free EPUB ingestion so a user can listen through an entire book in Spoken Margins while preserving the EPUB's canonical chapter structure and using the existing interjection experience during playback.

## User experience
- Import/open a DRM-free `.epub` file.
- Parse the EPUB package/navigation metadata rather than flattening the book into one undifferentiated text blob.
- Present the book using its canonical reading order and chapter/section boundaries.
- Allow continuous full-book playback across chapters.
- Keep chapter identity visible during playback and make chapter navigation available.
- Allow interjections at the current reading position just as with other Spoken Margins text playback.
- After an interjection, resume at the correct location in the correct chapter without skipping or replaying unrelated text.
- Persist playback position across app launches, including chapter plus position within that chapter.

## Scope / constraints
- DRM-protected EPUBs are explicitly out of scope.
- Prefer EPUB-declared structure as the source of truth: package spine for canonical reading order, with EPUB navigation/TOC data for human-readable chapter/section labels where available.
- Handle books whose navigation hierarchy is deeper than a single chapter level without destroying the original ordering.
- Preserve enough source-location metadata to map spoken segments and interjections back to stable EPUB/chapter positions.
- Reuse the existing native-text/TTS playback and interjection pipeline where practical rather than creating a separate EPUB-only player.

## Acceptance criteria
- A valid, non-DRM EPUB can be imported and represented as a book with ordered canonical chapters/sections.
- Starting at the beginning can play continuously through the end of the EPUB without manual chapter starts.
- The currently playing canonical chapter/section is identifiable in the UI.
- The user can jump between canonical chapters/sections.
- Interjecting pauses at the current EPUB reading location and resumes at that same logical location afterward.
- Progress/restoration returns to the correct chapter and intra-chapter position after relaunch.
- Malformed/unsupported EPUBs fail gracefully with a useful error rather than corrupting the library or playback state.
- DRM-protected EPUBs are rejected clearly rather than partially imported.

## Implementation note
A useful internal model is likely `book -> ordered spine items -> canonical navigation nodes -> speakable segments`, with stable source-position identifiers carried through TTS generation/playback. The exact representation should follow the existing document/playback architecture.

## Rendering and preparation policy

Keep EPUB ingestion, canonical structure, and audio preparation as separate layers:

- Parse and persist the package, spine, navigation hierarchy, stable source locations, and normalized speakable text for the whole EPUB at import time.
- Do not require hours of synthesized audio before the book becomes playable.
- Initial playback should prepare the current canonical chapter and a bounded look-ahead that normally reaches through the next chapter.
- Chapter jumps reprioritize the selected chapter immediately and discard only obsolete uncommitted work; valid committed audio remains reusable.
- When external power, Low Power Mode, thermal state, and background execution conditions permit, preparation may extend beyond the normal look-ahead toward the remainder of the book.
- On battery or under constrained power/thermal conditions, return to the bounded demand window rather than eagerly rendering the entire EPUB.
- Scheduling policy belongs to #73; EPUB structure and interjection correctness must not depend on full-book preparation completing.

## Additional acceptance criteria

- [ ] A long EPUB becomes playable after bounded initial preparation rather than waiting for full-book synthesis.
- [ ] On-battery preparation does not run unboundedly through the entire book by default.
- [ ] The current and next chapter can be prepared without losing canonical chapter/source identities.
- [ ] Jumping to an unprepared chapter reprioritizes that chapter and resumes at the requested logical EPUB position once ready.
- [ ] Plugging in can extend preparation when Low Power Mode and thermal state allow, without changing playback position or duplicating committed audio.
- [ ] Relaunch reconstructs preparation state from durable manifests and never confuses prepared-media time with canonical EPUB source location.

Related: #64 and #73.

title: Generate deterministic listening maps for pasted-text items
body:
## Summary
Items created by pasting text do not appear to generate the deterministic Listening Map, even when the pasted content contains clear structural cues such as headings.

## Current behavior
- Create a new item via Paste.
- Paste structured text containing headings / sections.
- The item is created without the deterministic Listening Map that equivalent structured content should be able to derive.

## Desired behavior
Run the same deterministic Listening Map generation pipeline for pasted-text items whenever the input has usable structure.

The map should prefer deterministic structure already present in the text (headings, section boundaries, etc.) rather than requiring an AI-generated map when it can be derived directly.

## Suggested implementation direction
- Normalize pasted text into the same document/block representation used by other ingest paths before map generation.
- Run deterministic map extraction after normalization and before any optional AI enrichment.
- Do not key map generation solely on source type (URL/PDF/etc.); key it on whether the normalized document contains usable structure.
- Define a sensible fallback for unstructured pasted text (for example, no map or deterministic paragraph/chunk boundaries, depending on current product behavior).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pasted text with headings produces a Listening Map deterministically.
- [ ] Heading titles and ordering are preserved accurately.
- [ ] Map positions correspond to the correct locations in the generated/native audio timeline.
- [ ] Pasted text without headings continues to behave predictably and does not invent semantic section titles.
- [ ] Existing non-paste ingest paths are unaffected.

title: Playback session state bugs: AI response progress, Live Activity interject, and play/pause drift
body:
## Summary
Several playback-session state problems appear to be related and are especially visible when using AI Response / interjection during native podcast playback.

## Observed behavior
1. **AI Response progress bar can be stale / inaccurate**
   - While an AI Response is being played, the progress UI can show ~80–90% even when the response has actually completed.
   - Attached screenshot from repro shows the AI Response card at ~88% while playback had completed.

2. **Interject from Live Activity resumes at the wrong podcast position**
   - Triggering Interject from the Live Activity does not seem to insert/resume at the same logical playback position as interjecting in-app.
   - After the AI response, native podcast playback can resume noticeably *forward* from where the listener expected.
   - Rewinding did not make it easy to find the previously familiar point, suggesting the resume anchor may be wrong rather than merely a UI display issue.

3. **Live Activity play/pause state diverges from native playback state**
   - The Live Activity play/pause button can show a state that does not match the native player.
   - This has been recurrent enough that the control is currently unreliable.
   - If there is no robust way to source authoritative playback state, consider removing the Live Activity play/pause control rather than exposing a redundant control that can lie about state.
   - The essential Live Activity action is **Interject**, and that path needs to be reliable.

## Expected behavior
- AI Response progress reaches 100% / completed state when response playback completes.
- Interject from the Live Activity captures the authoritative native playback position before interruption and resumes from that same logical position afterward, without an unexplained forward jump.
- Live Activity playback state is derived from the authoritative native player/session state. If that cannot be made reliable, remove the play/pause affordance and retain Interject as the primary Live Activity control.

## Suggested investigation
- Identify a single source of truth for playback state and elapsed position across:
  - native player
  - AI Response playback
  - Live Activity / ActivityKit state
  - interjection begin/end transitions
- Confirm whether interjection currently snapshots elapsed time before pausing, after pausing, or after any seek/buffer transition.
- Verify whether AI Response completion emits the event that updates UI progress to its terminal state.
- Check whether Live Activity actions operate on stale serialized ActivityKit state rather than querying/commanding the active playback coordinator.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AI Response progress is terminally accurate at completion.
- [ ] Live Activity Interject resumes at the exact expected native-content position (within normal player timing tolerance).
- [ ] Repeated interject/resume cycles do not accumulate forward drift.
- [ ] Live Activity play/pause always matches native playback state, **or** the play/pause control is removed.
- [ ] Interject remains available and reliable from the home/lock screen.

## Evidence
Two screenshots were supplied with the report: one showing the AI Response progress discrepancy in-app and one showing the simultaneous native Now Playing + Spoken Margins Live Activity playback controls/state.

title: Live Activity play/pause state is stale and cannot resume paused playback
body:
## Summary
The Live Activity playback controls do not stay synchronized with the actual playback state. After playback is paused, the Live Activity controls also fail to restart/resume playback.

## Observed behavior
- The Live Activity play/pause button does not reliably reflect the current playback state.
- When playback is paused, tapping the playback control in the Live Activity does not restart playback.

## Expected behavior
- The Live Activity play/pause control should update whenever playback state changes, regardless of where that change originated.
- When playback is paused, tapping Play in the Live Activity should resume the current item.
- The displayed button state should immediately reflect the resulting playback state.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Live Activity shows Play while paused and Pause while actively playing.
- [ ] State remains correct when playback is changed from the app, system media controls, or the Live Activity itself.
- [ ] Tapping Play in the Live Activity while paused resumes the current playback session.
- [ ] Tapping Pause in the Live Activity while playing pauses playback.
- [ ] The Live Activity updates promptly after either action and does not remain stale.

## Notes
Likely worth checking both directions of synchronization: playback-state updates published into ActivityKit content state, and the App Intent/action path used by the Live Activity controls to operate the active player.

title: [Recovery MVP] Large Share Session export renders a blank preview

labels.name: bug

labels.description: Required before Recovery MVP human validation

labels.name: area: sharing

body:
## Summary

The **Share Session** screen generated a non-empty AI-handoff payload, but the preview panel below the **Item** button rendered as a large blank box. The user could not inspect what was about to be copied or shared.

This is a current export-preview defect, distinct from the post-MVP sharing-package design tracked in #17.

## Reproduction evidence

- Captured: 2026-08-05 during the same physical-iPhone validation session
- Item: [#247 – Anton Leicht on how middle powers avoid losing everything in a post-AI world](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/80-000-hours-podcast/id1245002988?i=1000776795600)
- Session state: `in_progress`, 96% complete, with nine interjections
- Generated Markdown handoff size: 1,054,707 bytes
- The **Share Session** button was visible and **Copy** was enabled. In the current view, both conditions require `exportPreview` to be non-empty.
- The generated handoff was successfully captured outside the preview, confirming this was a rendering/presentation failure rather than an empty export.

The handoff contains very large repeated anchor material. That likely makes payload size a useful trigger, but it is not yet a confirmed root cause.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session with enough source/interjection context to generate a large AI Handoff Markdown export (the observed payload was about 1.05 MB).
2. Open **Share Session** and select the session/options that include the listening map, interjections, and AI turns.
3. Confirm **Share Session** and **Copy** are enabled.
4. Inspect the preview panel below **Item**.

## Expected behavior

The screen visibly previews the generated content before it leaves the device. For payloads too large to render safely in full, show a bounded/virtualized preview with a clear truncation or size indicator while preserving the complete payload for Copy and Share.

## Actual behavior

The preview panel is blank even though `exportPreview` contains a large generated handoff and the sharing controls are enabled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A regression fixture at least as large as the observed 1.05 MB payload shows visible preview content or an explicit bounded-preview state.
- [ ] The screen remains responsive and the preview does not require laying out the entire payload as one unbounded SwiftUI `Text`.
- [ ] Copy and Share continue to use the complete export, even if the on-screen preview is intentionally truncated.
- [ ] Empty exports still show a clear `No export yet.` state; non-empty exports never appear as an unlabeled blank panel.
- [ ] Accessibility exposes the preview/truncation state and payload size.
- [ ] Focused UI/developer verification covers the large-payload case; product-owner validation remains separate.

## Build context

The checked-out release state matching the captured screen is version 0.1 (build 12), commit `34ac5ab6716813b117b45834ecc21afdf752fe53`. The exact installed build, iPhone model, and iOS point release were not recorded in the supplied evidence and should be confirmed during retest.

body:
## Summary

During product-owner device validation, the on-device interjection summary failed for a real podcast session containing nine saved interjections. The app displayed:

> On-device summary failed: The on-device model did not produce a safe, concise listener-note summary.

The playback screen still showed **Summarizing** when the failure banner appeared. This prevents the remaining physical-device summary acceptance in #42 from passing.

## Reproduction evidence

- Captured: 2026-08-05 on a physical iPhone with the on-device model available
- Item: [#247 – Anton Leicht on how middle powers avoid losing everything in a post-AI world](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/80-000-hours-podcast/id1245002988?i=1000776795600)
- Source: `remote_stream` from `https://media.transistor.fm/067004a2/364d2205.mp3`
- Session state: `in_progress`, 96% complete
- Interjections: nine notes at approximately 29%, 42%, 43%, 45%, 52%, 81%, 83%, 91%, and 92%
- The same session produced an AI-handoff export containing all nine note transcripts, so eligible listener-note content existed.

The supplied handoff also shows the same unusually large `anchorBefore` content repeated across the interjections. That is a possible stressor or upstream contributor, not a confirmed cause.

The private listener-note transcripts are intentionally omitted from this public issue. They can be supplied as a redacted regression fixture.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Import/open the podcast item above and play it as a remote stream.
2. Record multiple voice interjections across the session, including longer notes with filler words, repetitions, questions, and qualifications.
3. Near the end of playback, tap **Summarize**.
4. Observe the failure banner instead of a listener-note summary.

## Expected behavior

- Valid saved interjections produce concise on-device summaries that preserve the listener's intent and uncertainty, remove transcription noise, and do not quote source anchors.
- A large or repeated anchor must not cause otherwise valid listener notes to be rejected.
- If generation still fails after bounded retry/recovery, the UI should exit its busy state, provide actionable diagnostics, and allow a retry.

## Actual behavior

The entire summary operation fails with `invalidInterjectionSummary`; no usable summary is produced.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A redacted fixture matching this session shape (nine notes, long/repeated anchors, mixed note lengths) no longer ends in `invalidInterjectionSummary`.
- [ ] Generated summaries satisfy `LocalInterjectionSummaryPolicy`: no source-anchor leakage, no invented answer, and preserved listener intent/uncertainty.
- [ ] One problematic record cannot leave the whole summarization flow in an ambiguous or permanently busy state.
- [ ] After failure, the Summarize control returns to a retryable state.
- [ ] Focused automated coverage verifies the regression; product-owner device validation remains a separate required step under #42.

## Build context

The checked-out release state matching the captured UI/error text is version 0.1 (build 12), commit `34ac5ab6716813b117b45834ecc21afdf752fe53`. The exact installed build, iPhone model, and iOS point release were not recorded in the supplied evidence and should be confirmed during retest.

title: Add an “Empty Recently Deleted” action in Settings

## Feature request
Add an action in **Settings** to permanently delete all items currently in **Recently Deleted**.

## Expected behavior
- Settings includes an **Empty Recently Deleted** or **Delete All Recently Deleted Items** action.
- The action is disabled or hidden when Recently Deleted is empty.
- Selecting it shows a destructive confirmation explaining that the deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.
- Confirming permanently removes all recently deleted items and associated local data.
- Cancelling leaves all items unchanged.
- After completion, the Recently Deleted count/list updates immediately.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Delete one or more library items so they appear in Recently Deleted.
2. Open Settings and select the bulk-delete action.
3. Cancel once and verify no items are removed.
4. Confirm the action and verify all recently deleted items are permanently removed.
5. Verify the action becomes unavailable when Recently Deleted is empty.

labels.name: phase: post-mvp
labels.description: Explicitly outside the active Recovery MVP scope

labels.name: type: spike
labels.description: Bounded experiment ending in a go or no-go decision

labels.name: area: rights
labels.description: Copyright, attribution, consent, provenance, and retention

body:
## Outcome

Evaluate and, only if the evidence supports it, implement an opt-in server-hosted AI fallback for Listening Maps after the Recovery MVP. The fallback applies only when an item has no publisher-authored chapters, no existing valid Listening Map, and no adequate deterministic native-text map.

This work is explicitly outside the default tracker-free MVP release. The Recovery MVP behavior remains:

- podcasts use publisher chapters when available and otherwise remain mapless;
- native text uses existing or deterministic structure;
- no full-source podcast transcription is started for map generation;
- playback and interjection capture remain available without a map.

## Why this is separate

The on-device podcast-map spike in #42 hit its stopping rule during product-owner testing: latency was unacceptable and one run failed with “Media data outside timeline.” That path is not being repaired or shipped. A server-hosted design has different privacy, consent, retention, cost, review, and reliability constraints and therefore needs an independent decision.

## Required precedence

A server-generated map must never silently replace higher-confidence structure:

1. Existing valid Listening Map
2. Podcasting 2.0 `<podcast:chapters>` JSON
3. Podlove Simple Chapters
4. Embedded ID3/MP4 chapters
5. Timestamped episode descriptions
6. Deterministic native-text structure
7. Explicitly requested server-hosted generation

## Feasibility questions

- Compare established topic-segmentation and hierarchical summarization methods; do not roll a novel chunker without evidence.
- Determine whether a transcript provider or model API already supplies reliable long-context chunking and timestamp linkage.
- Compare bounded overlapping windows, lexical/change-point proposals, and hierarchical condensation.
- Require generated chapter candidates to reference stable source segment IDs; resolve exact text offsets and media timestamps in app-owned code.
- Measure latency, cost, retry behavior, cancellation, long-item coverage, duplicate chapters, boundary error, and failure rate.
- Define whether processing is ephemeral, what derived data is retained, and how deletion is propagated.
- Define explicit user consent and disclosure for off-device source processing without introducing advertising or unrelated tracking.

## Rights and fairness boundary

Full native-audio transcripts are internal derived data, not a user-facing replacement for the publisher's work.

The app may expose or export only:

- compact Listening Map overview, titles, and descriptions;
- timestamps and resolved map positions;
- source attribution and durable reference;
- bounded before/after anchors around a user's interjection;
- the user's own interjection audio and text.

Do not expose, browse, search, copy, share, or export the full generated transcript or large source excerpts. Ordinary exports, diagnostics, and portable packages must be tested for leakage. Product policy and qualified legal review remain required; technical controls do not themselves establish fair use.

## Acceptance evidence

- [ ] A written comparison covers at least two established segmentation/chunking approaches plus the deterministic baseline.
- [ ] Every accepted chapter resolves monotonically to an exact source segment and text/media position.
- [ ] Publisher chapters and existing valid maps are never silently replaced.
- [ ] Failure, cancellation, or timeout leaves playback, the item, and the prior map unchanged.
- [ ] Representative article and podcast evaluation records coverage, duplication, boundary error, latency, cost, and unsupported/failure rate.
- [ ] Full generated transcripts cannot appear in UI, clipboard, share sheets, exports, diagnostics, or portable packages.
- [ ] Consent, retention, deletion, provider data-use, and App Store review behavior are documented.
- [ ] The product owner judges representative maps useful before this leaves the feature flag.

## Stopping rules

Do not ship if the approach cannot maintain exact navigable positions, produces source-republishing excerpts, requires unacceptable retention or tracking, has an unsafe false-match rate, or cannot meet an agreed latency/cost envelope. Mapless playback remains the supported fallback.

## Dependencies

- #14 rights, attribution, excerpt, and sharing policy
- #46 publisher chapter and podcast intake behavior
- Recovery MVP human validation

title: [Post-MVP] Desktop browser extension for interjectable web content

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: phase: post-mvp
labels.description: Explicitly outside the active Recovery MVP scope

labels.name: type: research
labels.description: Research and decision framing without production implementation

labels.name: area: anchors
labels.description: Source, transcript, media-time, and cross-edition anchors

body:
## Outcome

A desktop browser extension lets a user make supported browser content part of a Spoken Margins session while they consume it. Initially, this should cover readable web pages and captioned YouTube-like videos: the user can start or attach a session, interject at the current source position, and have the source, session, interjections, and available transcript context captured durably in the native app.

This is explicitly **post-MVP**. The extension is a new client and capture surface, not a replacement for the Recovery MVP share-sheet intake path.

## User experience

- From a supported page, capture selected text or readable page content with title, URL, author, and publication date when available.
- From a supported video or other browser media page, start a Spoken Margins session without requiring the extension to own playback.
- While content is playing, interject with a spoken or typed note.
- Pause or coordinate playback during capture, then resume with the configured rollback/reorientation behavior.
- Anchor the interjection to source media time and, when available, the relevant timestamped transcript/caption span.
- Continue the same session in the native app, where captured content and interjections appear in the timeline and can contribute to later summary, discussion, navigation, and export.

## Actors and ownership

- **Browser extension:** detects supported content, observes page-owned playback when possible, captures metadata/transcript context, and initiates or hands off interjections.
- **Page/media player:** may retain playback ownership; the extension must not assume arbitrary media control is available.
- **Native Spoken Margins app / SessionKit:** remains the canonical persistence and sync authority and owns durable items, sessions, interjections, downstream summaries, discussions, and exports.
- **User:** explicitly grants capture/microphone permissions and can see what was captured or why capture is unavailable.

## Proposed delivery shape

### 1. Capability and architecture spike

Compare at least these topologies:

1. Observe page-owned playback and delegate recording/persistence to the native app.
2. Capture interjections in the extension and hand off a durable package to the native app.
3. Delegate playback to the native app when a source permits it.

Select the topology per content mode using reliability, browser permissions, privacy, platform/site rules, offline behavior, anchoring accuracy, and handoff complexity as decision criteria.

### 2. Browser text mode

Support selected-text and readable-page capture, source metadata, session creation/handoff, and interjection capture when the browser permits it.

### 3. Browser media mode

For an explicitly supported compatibility set, observe current source media time and playback rate, capture available captions/transcript timing, create portable anchors, and continue the session in the native app.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A documented capability matrix identifies the supported desktop browser(s), page types, media sites, capture modes, permissions, and fallbacks.
- [ ] Selected text and readable article content can be captured with source provenance.
- [ ] On a supported captioned YouTube-like video, an interjection made at 1x, 1.5x, and 1.75x is anchored to source media time rather than wall-clock elapsed time.
- [ ] Timestamped transcript/caption context is preserved when available; absence or access failure is represented clearly and never fabricated.
- [ ] Captured content, session identity, interjection audio/text, and portable anchors survive handoff and appear coherently in the native app.
- [ ] Browser storage is not the canonical durable session store.
- [ ] Page navigation, backgrounded tabs, extension/app unavailability, microphone denial, player changes, and interrupted handoff fail without corrupting or silently losing an existing session.
- [ ] Permission, privacy, retention, attribution, and relevant platform/site-policy behavior are explicit to the user and documented.
- [ ] The product owner human-validates the supported browser flows after automated traces and compatibility evidence pass.

## Fallback behavior to define

- No transcript/captions: retain a media-time anchor when reliable, or offer link-only/native handoff when it is not.
- No browser microphone access: delegate recording to the native app when available, otherwise allow non-audio capture without claiming an interjection was recorded.
- Native app unavailable: queue a bounded, recoverable handoff package or clearly report that the session was not saved.
- Unsupported or changed player integration: show an unsupported state instead of recording an unverified anchor.
- Offline or interrupted handoff: retry idempotently without duplicating the item, session, or interjection.

## Verification and stopping rules

Evidence should include:

- contract traces for browser-session handoff, duplicate retry, permission denial, unavailable transcript, tab backgrounding/navigation, and app unavailability;
- source-time versus wall-clock tests at multiple playback rates;
- compatibility tests against the declared browser/site matrix;
- persistence and sync checks showing that the native app remains authoritative;
- an omission review covering text-only pages, captioned and uncaptioned media, multiple tabs, and unsupported players.

Do not promote browser media support beyond research if a supported integration cannot obtain a stable source-time anchor, cannot hand off without silent loss/duplication, or depends on brittle page DOM assumptions without an acceptable maintenance strategy. In that case, retain text/link capture and native-app continuation as the supported fallback.

## Existing design references

- [Browser Extension Research Plan](../blob/main/docs/browser-extension-research-plan.md)
- [Product Validation Plan — Gate 5: Browser Extension for Text](../blob/main/docs/product-validation-plan.md#gate-5-browser-extension-for-text)
- [Product Validation Plan — Gate 6: Browser Extension for YouTube / Media](../blob/main/docs/product-validation-plan.md#gate-6-browser-extension-for-youtube--media)
- [SessionKit contract](../blob/main/docs/sessionkit-contract.md)

body:
## Outcome

Research advanced semantic Listening Maps only after the Recovery MVP is human validated and the basic server-hosted map feasibility decision in #51 has produced an acceptable source-position, privacy, and rights model.

This issue owns advanced semantic organization. It does not own ordinary chapter-map generation, publisher chapter ingestion, or on-device interjection summaries.

## Research scope

- Represent transcripts, annotations, optional audio features, and listening behavior in a shared or interoperable representation.
- Compare lexical topic segmentation, task-specific embeddings, general-purpose embeddings, and multimodal models.
- Detect semantic links between distant moments in one item and, only with explicit user scope, across items.
- Explore speaker, theme, concept, rhetorical-role, and mood organization.
- Support natural-language exploration such as “show related ideas” or “find where this topic returns.”
- Evaluate explainable edges that retain source positions and reveal why two moments were linked.
- Consider local indexing, rebuild cost, storage, deletion, and model-version migration.

## Guardrails

- Post-Recovery-MVP only.
- Do not expose or export full generated native-audio transcripts.
- Do not create a public corpus or an unrelated developer-operated content index.
- Cross-item analysis is opt-in and local by default; any off-device proposal inherits #51's consent and retention requirements.
- Source rights, attribution, excerpt, and retention policy must align with #14.
- A visually interesting graph is not evidence of listening usefulness.

## Required outputs

- a typed node/edge/index model distinct from the portable chapter map;
- comparison of at least two established segmentation or embedding approaches;
- a representative evaluation corpus and relevance judgments;
- explainability and provenance rules for every suggested relationship;
- latency, storage, energy, rebuild, and deletion measurements;
- privacy and rights threat model;
- a product-owner usefulness test and stopping rule.

## Dependencies

- #51 server-hosted AI Listening Map feasibility and its position/privacy model
- #14 rights, attribution, excerpt, and sharing policy
- #42 human validation of the daily-driver interjection-summary loop
- Recovery MVP human validation

title: Persist native-audio playback speed across subsequent items

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: phase: recovery-mvp
labels.description: Required before Recovery MVP human validation

milestone.title: External TestFlight 0.1
milestone.description: Blocking implementation, verification, product-owner validation, distribution, and App Store Connect work for the first external TestFlight review.

body:
## Problem
The playback speed selected for a native-audio item does not carry over when playback advances to another native-audio item.

This forces the listener to reset the speed for every item.

## Expected behavior
The selected native-audio playback speed should persist across subsequent native-audio items.

Alternatively, persistence should be configurable in Settings, for example:

- **Remember playback speed**: on/off
- optional default playback speed

## Reproduction
1. Start a native-audio item.
2. Change playback speed from the default.
3. Start or advance to another native-audio item.
4. Observe that playback speed resets.

## Acceptance criteria
- A newly loaded native-audio item uses the previously selected native-audio speed when persistence is enabled.
- The behavior is consistent for manual item selection and automatic queue advancement.
- The preference survives app relaunch if configured as a persistent setting.
- Changing speed on one item updates the remembered value for later native-audio items.
- Non-native playback sources are not unintentionally affected unless explicitly designed to share the same preference.
