body:
## Recovery MVP outcome

A user may discover a podcast in their preferred app and hand its episode link to Spoken Margins. Spoken Margins must resolve supported Spotify, Apple Podcasts, RSS, direct-audio, and equivalent public episode links into the correct native-audio item without requiring in-app podcast discovery.

This is an MVP requirement because external discovery is the primary discovery path.

## Implemented state

Merged to `main` in #50.

- Direct Apple Podcasts episode links use exact episode/feed evidence instead of title-only search.
- Spotify episode links use public metadata and score Apple/feed candidates by title, show, publisher, date, duration, and stable identity.
- High-confidence matches import automatically.
- Ambiguous results present a bounded candidate chooser rather than guessing.
- RSS enclosures, direct audio, redirects, canonical feeds, and structured publisher episode pages are supported.
- The original discovery link and canonical source provenance are retained.
- HTTP podcast enclosures are migrated through the secure download path where possible.
- Imports are idempotent and do not replace the active session/navigation unexpectedly.

## Publisher chapters

Successful podcast intake also imports publisher structure in this precedence order:

1. Podcasting 2.0 `<podcast:chapters>` JSON
2. Podlove Simple Chapters
3. Embedded ID3/MP4 chapters after download
4. Timestamped episode descriptions
5. Mapless playback

Both current and legacy Podcasting 2.0 namespace forms are accepted. Publisher timing is normalized into the existing media timeline and retained if transcript context arrives later. The default Recovery MVP does not generate an AI podcast map when publisher structure is unavailable.

## Matching model

Keep evidence types distinct:

- **Input metadata:** original provider, episode URL/ID, normalized title, show title, publisher/author, publication date, duration, artwork, and description.
- **Candidate identity:** Apple episode ID, feed URL/GUID, enclosure URL, show identity, title, date, duration, and publisher.
- **Decision evidence:** exact provider IDs when linkable, show match, title similarity, date distance, duration distance, publisher match, and canonical feed evidence.
- **Outcome:** high-confidence automatic match, bounded user selection, or unresolved with actionable alternatives.

Never select solely because a title matches. Never silently import a low-confidence candidate.

## Automated evidence

- [x] Exact Apple, RSS enclosure, and direct-audio routes avoid title-only ambiguity.
- [x] Exact/high-confidence, ambiguous, and no-match outcomes have regression coverage.
- [x] Ambiguous candidates expose distinguishing metadata.
- [x] Legacy Podcasting 2.0 namespaces and structured publisher pages have regression fixtures.
- [x] Publisher chapter URLs/collections persist to navigable media chapters.
- [x] Failed or cancelled resolution preserves the current playback/session state.
- [x] Signed iOS 18.6 app suite passes all 40 SourceLinkImportTests.
- [x] Contract validators, SessionKit 131/131, and generic iOS device build pass.

## Product-owner revalidation

Validate all of the following after #50:

- [ ] The Spotify episode reported in this issue resolves to the correct episode or correct bounded candidate.
- [ ] `https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/1891-we-need-memes/id269169796?i=1000779583526` imports the exact episode and publisher chapters when its endpoint supplies them.
- [ ] `https://www.noagendashow.net/listen/1891` imports playable audio and available publisher metadata.
- [ ] One direct RSS or direct-audio discovery link imports correctly.
- [ ] Original-link and canonical-source provenance are retained.
- [ ] Existing playback, position, and rate remain unchanged until the user starts the new item.

A publisher chapter endpoint that is unavailable may yield honest mapless playback; it must not fabricate chapters or prevent otherwise playable audio import.

## Closure rule

Do not close on one repaired URL. Close after the provider matrix above is accepted by the product owner and no fixture auto-selects a false-positive episode.

title: MVP: Complete final playback, close the session, and clamp skip-forward

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: phase: recovery-mvp
labels.description: Required before Recovery MVP human validation

milestone.title: External TestFlight 0.1
milestone.description: Blocking implementation, verification, product-owner validation, distribution, and App Store Connect work for the first external TestFlight review.

body:
## Recovery MVP outcome

End-of-media behavior must be terminal and monotonic:

- playback stops at the known duration;
- remaining time normalizes to `0:00`;
- skip-forward clamps to the duration and never seeks backward;
- when the final source/generated audio has completed and no generated turn is queued, the listening session closes automatically and the player is dismissed.

## Original failure

A `1:07:16` source displayed `−0:00` while the pause icon remained active. Pressing `+60s` at that point moved playback backward. The first fix corrected clamping but product-owner testing found that the completed session still remained open.

## Implemented state

Merged to `main` in #50.

- Native-audio skip-forward clamps to the known duration.
- Exact-end and crossing-the-end operations leave playback paused at the end.
- Lifecycle synchronization detects final completed audio.
- If no pending generated turn needs playback, the completed session is marked finished, cleared from the active player, and the app returns home.
- A queued summary/assistant turn is allowed to play before the session closes.

## Automated evidence

- [x] Exact-end skip-forward cannot seek backward.
- [x] Crossing the end clamps to duration.
- [x] Playback state becomes paused/completed.
- [x] Final audio automatically closes the completed session.
- [x] Signed iOS 18.6 app suite passes 163/163.
- [x] SessionKit suite passes 131/131.
- [x] Generic iOS device build passes.

## Product-owner evidence

- [x] Initial product-owner validation confirmed clamping worked.
- [x] Initial validation identified the remaining open-player/session defect.
- [ ] Revalidate the #50 follow-up: play the final audio to completion and confirm the session closes and the player disappears.
- [ ] At the completed position, confirm skip-forward cannot move backward and remaining time is `0:00`.

## Closure rule

Close only after the product owner accepts the final-session behavior on device. Automated checks establish `verified`, not `human_validated`.

Loading or opening a PDF pauses audio that is already playing through the native audio player.

- Check for shared app lifecycle/loading state that issues an implicit pause.
- Verify whether the behavior occurs for both local PDF import and reopening an existing PDF.

## Acceptance criteria
- Active native audio continues uninterrupted while a PDF loads.
- Loading a PDF does not reset position, rate, or play/pause state.
- Add regression coverage where practical for the playback state during document loading.

title: Synchronize AI-response playback controls and Live Activity lifecycle

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Extra attention is needed

labels.name: phase: recovery-mvp
labels.description: Required before Recovery MVP human validation

milestone.title: External TestFlight 0.1
milestone.description: Blocking implementation, verification, product-owner validation, distribution, and App Store Connect work for the first external TestFlight review.

body:
## Problem
AI-generated responses do not expose native playback controls. Playback is represented only through the Live Activity.

The Live Activity can pause playback, but the main play/pause button does not update to reflect the paused state. This leaves the UI inconsistent with the actual player state.

The Live Activity also persists after the app is quit, leaving stale playback information and controls visible after the associated playback session should have ended.

## Expected behavior
- AI-response audio exposes the same native playback controls as other playable content where supported.
- Play, pause, seek, and current-position state are driven by a single playback source of truth.
- Pausing from the Live Activity immediately changes the in-app control to a play state.
- Resuming from either surface updates all other playback surfaces.
- Lock Screen, Control Center, Live Activity, and in-app controls remain synchronized.
- The Live Activity ends when its playback session is terminated and does not remain stale after the app is quit.

## Reproduction: stale play/pause state
1. Start playback of an AI response.
2. Observe that only the Live Activity provides playback controls.
3. Pause playback from the Live Activity.
4. Return to the app.
5. Observe that playback is paused, but the in-app play/pause button still shows the previous state.

## Reproduction: Live Activity persists after quit
1. Start playback of an AI response so the Live Activity appears.
2. Quit the app.
3. Observe that the Live Activity remains visible with stale playback information or controls.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AI-response playback registers with the system media-control stack where applicable.
- [ ] All playback controls reflect the actual player state after local or external actions.
- [ ] Play/pause state updates without requiring a view refresh or navigation cycle.
- [ ] State remains correct after interruptions, route changes, backgrounding, and foregrounding.
- [ ] The Live Activity is explicitly ended when playback is terminated or the owning session is invalidated.
- [ ] App termination does not leave a stale Live Activity behind.
- [ ] Launch-time reconciliation removes any orphaned Live Activity from a prior session.
- [ ] Regression coverage verifies synchronization between Live Activity and in-app controls, plus cleanup after app termination.

title: [Recovery MVP] On-device interjection summaries and tracker-free release mode

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: phase: recovery-mvp
labels.description: Required before Recovery MVP human validation

milestone.title: External TestFlight 0.1
milestone.description: Blocking implementation, verification, product-owner validation, distribution, and App Store Connect work for the first external TestFlight review.

body:
## Recovery MVP decision

Ship the smallest private, tracker-free intelligence path:

1. On eligible devices, summarize scoped user interjections with Apple Foundation Models.
2. Disable Discuss, BYO API-key/provider settings, remote calls, retries, and restored provider jobs by default behind one reversible release flag.
3. Preserve interjection copy/export and pasted-assistant-response import so users can continue a conversation in a chatbot of their choice.
4. On devices without an available local model, hide Summarize and make no remote fallback request.
5. Keep Listening Maps deterministic or publisher-authored in this release:
   - native text keeps an existing valid map or derives one deterministically;
   - podcasts use publisher chapters when available and otherwise remain mapless.

On-device and server-hosted AI Listening Map generation are not part of the default Recovery MVP. The on-device podcast-map spike hit its stopping rule; future server-hosted feasibility is tracked in #51. Advanced semantic/cross-item exploration remains in #48.

## Interjection-summary contract

Summarize only eligible interjections for the active playback target. Bounded `anchorBefore` and `anchorAfter` may be supplied solely to resolve references.

The transformation must:

- make the listener's note more concise;
- remove fillers such as “um” and “ah,” stutters, false starts, repeated words, and obvious transcription noise;
- preserve first-person viewpoint, intent, questions, meaningful uncertainty, qualifications, preferences, and requested actions;
- never summarize or attribute source-anchor language to the listener;
- never answer the interjection;
- retain traceability to the included interjection IDs;
- become eligible again after a new interjection is added, without remaining stuck in a disabled/busy state.

## Release-flag boundary

With `SMRemoteProviderExperienceEnabled` disabled, all of the following remain unreachable:

- Discuss and follow-up UI;
- provider API-key, model, consent, and probe settings;
- compact, Watch, App Intent, shortcut, and delegated discussion commands;
- remote-provider capability publication;
- remote calls, retries, restored pending jobs, and automatic fallback.

Existing Keychain/provider data may remain local for a future re-enable. The flag must be sufficient to restore the existing remote-provider experience without reimplementing it.

## Listening Map boundary

- Existing valid maps are never silently replaced.
- Native-text structure is deterministic in the default release.
- Publisher podcast chapters take precedence in the order tracked by #46.
- Podcasts without publisher chapters remain playable without a map.
- The default release does not initiate full-source podcast transcription for map generation.
- Claims are not required.
- Full generated native-audio transcripts are not exposed, copied, shared, or exported.

## Implementation state

Merged to `main` in #50.

Automated verification includes:

- iOS 18.6 signed app suite: 163 tests passed;
- SessionKit suite: 131 tests passed;
- contract and surface-contract validators passed;
- generic iOS device build passed;
- feature-flag, summary scoping, filler rejection, anchor-copy rejection, repeat-summary eligibility, unavailable-model, and deterministic/mapless map regressions passed.

## Acceptance evidence

### Implemented and verified

- [x] Foundation Models code is guarded while the app retains its iOS 18 deployment target.
- [x] The default release flag hides Discuss and provider/API-key UI and blocks remote execution paths.
- [x] Copy/export and pasted-assistant-response import remain available.
- [x] Unsupported devices do not receive remote fallback behavior.
- [x] Summary candidates remain scoped to the active target and source-interjection IDs.
- [x] Anchors are optional source context rather than listener content.
- [x] A completed summary does not leave Summarize permanently disabled after a new interjection.

title: Bring Spoken Margins to Android
body:
## Goal
Create an Android implementation of Spoken Margins that preserves the product’s core listening and interruption workflows without forcing the iOS architecture onto Android.

## Initial product scope
- Import articles, podcasts, shared text, Markdown, and text-based PDFs.
- Support native media playback and installed Android text-to-speech voices.
- Allow interruption with a contextual note and stream the OpenAI response back into the listening session.
- Preserve session state, Listening Map behavior, and AI-handoff export semantics.
- Provide background playback, notification/media controls, audio-focus handling, and reliable resume behavior.

## Engineering work
- Decide whether Android belongs in this repository or a sibling repository; document the decision and shared-boundary rules.
- Identify which contracts, schemas, fixtures, and domain behavior can be shared verbatim.
- Define Android equivalents for AVFoundation/Now Playing, share extensions, persistence, background execution, and Live Activity behavior.
- Establish a Kotlin/Jetpack Compose application scaffold with repeatable build and test commands.
- Implement the smallest end-to-end vertical slice: import content → listen → interrupt → receive a streamed response → resume → export.
- Define parity tests against the canonical session contracts rather than visual iOS parity.

## Acceptance criteria
- The architecture decision and phased delivery plan are checked in.
- A buildable Android project exists with CI or an equivalent reproducible validation command.
- The vertical slice runs on a supported Android emulator or device.
- Shared session fixtures and contracts validate on Android.
- Platform-specific gaps and deferred features are explicitly documented.
- No regression is introduced into the existing iOS build or SessionKit tests.

title: [Post-MVP] Remove residual Kokoro/MLX code and formalize Supertonic render identity
body:
## Outcome

Remove the residual Kokoro/MLX implementation surface and formalize Supertonic as the supported local neural TTS runtime, including a stable render identity that durable prepared audio can use for invalidation and recovery.

This supersedes the original framing of Supertonic as a candidate to evaluate: the released beta already uses Supertonic. The remaining work is cleanup, migration safety, build simplification, and explicit runtime/version contracts.

## Current repository state

- Supertonic is the active local neural rendering path.
- Legacy Kokoro/MLX source, optional build configuration, documentation, tests, assets, settings, or migration values may still remain.
- #64 needs an exact engine/model/voice signature so prepared audio is reused when compatible and invalidated when synthesis output could change.

## Required work

### Residual inventory and removal

- Inventory Kokoro/MLX references across app and package source, dependencies, model assets, build settings, schemes, generated-project configuration, documentation, fixtures, tests, persisted settings, and diagnostics.
- Remove runtime adapters, models, dependencies, feature flags, dead settings, and obsolete build paths that are not deliberately retained for migration.
- Reassess the optional Kokoro/MLX device scheme and Metal-toolchain guidance; delete or rename obsolete configuration without breaking the active Supertonic device build.
- Historical documents may retain clearly labeled historical evidence, but must not imply Kokoro is an available product runtime.

### Persisted-value migration

- Identify persisted engine/voice/settings values that can refer to Kokoro/MLX.
- Map them deterministically to a supported Supertonic or installed-system-voice state, or surface an explicit recoverable selection requirement.
- Migration must be idempotent and must not silently change an active session's voice mid-playback.

### Supertonic render identity

Define one canonical signature containing every input that can change rendered samples or source-to-media mapping, including:

- engine identifier;
- model/version or bundled-asset revision;
- voice identifier and voice-asset revision;
- synthesis parameters that affect output;
- text normalization/chunking version where it affects samples or mapping;
- prepared-manifest/schema version.

Playback rate is a playback concern and must not invalidate rendered audio. The signature format must be deterministic, persistable, comparable across relaunch, and safe to include in diagnostics without private source text.

### Packaging, licensing, and diagnostics

- Document model/voice asset origin, license obligations, bundled size, supported devices/OS versions, and update strategy.
- Fail explicitly when required assets are missing, corrupt, or incompatible; retain the installed-system-voice fallback without claiming neural output.
- Diagnostics should identify the engine/model/voice revisions and fallback reason without logging source content.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No Kokoro/MLX runtime code, dependencies, bundled model assets, feature flags, or user-facing settings remain unless an explicit migration exception is documented.
- [ ] Persisted Kokoro/MLX values migrate idempotently to a supported, visible state without changing voice mid-session.
- [ ] The active Supertonic device build has one documented scheme/configuration and no obsolete Kokoro-specific prerequisites.
- [ ] One canonical render-signature implementation is used by Supertonic output and the durable manifest in #64.
- [ ] Changing any sample-affecting engine/model/voice/parameter revision invalidates incompatible prepared output.
- [ ] Playback-rate changes do not invalidate or rerender prepared audio.
- [ ] Missing/corrupt assets produce an explicit recoverable state and supported fallback.
- [ ] Licensing, asset provenance, bundled size, device/OS support, and update policy are documented.
- [ ] Contract validators, SessionKit tests, relevant migration tests, and iOS simulator/device builds pass.
- [ ] The product owner human-validates voice selection, migrated settings, Supertonic playback, and fallback behavior on supported devices.

## Audit and falsification checks

- Run a repository-wide residual-reference inventory and classify every surviving Kokoro/MLX match as removed, migration-only, or clearly historical.
- Generate signatures while changing one input at a time; require changes only for output-affecting inputs and stability across relaunch/builds with identical assets.
- Launch from representative persisted Kokoro settings repeatedly and require the same migrated result.
- Remove/corrupt representative model and voice assets and verify explicit fallback/recovery rather than a crash or falsely identified neural session.
- Treat two signature implementations, unversioned model replacement, silent voice change, or obsolete runtime code reachable from production as a failure.

## Dependencies and related work

- #64 consumes the canonical Supertonic render identity for durable prepared audio.
- #74 must use the same identity in foreground and background jobs.

## Non-goals

- Replacing the canonical playback/session spine.
- Removing installed-system voices as a supported fallback.
- Re-evaluating whether Supertonic is the chosen beta runtime without new contrary product direction.

Keep corpus generalization and full acceptance distinct from the accepted example.

Evidence: [scope-specific record](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-25/build-25-testflight-upload.md), [owner acceptance](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/gate-1/2026-09-08-build-26-acceptance.md), [Build 26 handoff](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-26/build-26-testflight-upload.md).

Build identity: **0.1 (26)**, exact source `9c967793e7a0e86c26a3030390818e87d830723b`; release manifest is **verified** (425 app/adapter/UI tests plus fast checks). The owner recorded **human_validated for the candidate**, without a separate device-by-device or individual-flow matrix. Internal Margins distribution is confirmed; Build 21 remains external. #14 and later-release authorization are unchanged.

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Source

Product research on shared and co-op interjections, 2026-07-21. Two listeners may resolve the same podcast episode through audio files that differ because of dynamic ads, silence trimming, re-encoding, corrections, or provider-specific versions.

## Question

Can Spoken Margins reliably relocate a shared interjection or Listening Map node onto the recipient's copy of the same editorial audio without redistributing the complete source and without confidently attaching commentary to the wrong passage?

This spike evaluates cross-edition resolution. It does not add a production sharing surface.

## Challenge model

Keep the evidence layers distinct:

- **Episode identity:** feed URL, item GUID, canonical episode URL, title, publisher, publication date, duration, and optional exact-edition digest.
- **Human anchor:** transcript excerpt, nearby text, chapter or Listening Map node, and sender media time.
- **Machine anchor:** versioned acoustic evidence around the source position.
- **Resolution result:** recipient-local position plus evidence class, confidence, ambiguity, and retained original evidence.

A sender timestamp is a hint, not a portable position. Dynamic insertions and deletions require a monotonic, piecewise mapping between sender and recipient timelines rather than one global offset.

## Current repository foundation

The current app already stores text, transcript, media-time, and turn anchors; playback position; nearby source context; transcript timelines; source references; and playback rate. Those are necessary inputs but do not yet prove cross-edition equivalence.

The existing playback-position `AnchorConfidence` describes how a local position was obtained. Do not overload it with cross-edition resolution status.

## Current research

### Transcript and identity baseline

Compare canonical source identity, exact-edition digest, timestamp, transcript quote, before/after context, and Listening Map nodes before adding acoustic evidence. Distinctive transcript context may solve many cases and remains inspectable by a person.

### Chromaprint baseline

Chromaprint is designed for compact fingerprints of near-identical audio, duplicate detection, and long-stream monitoring. Its raw fingerprint output and chunk/overlap support make it a plausible first benchmark, but it explicitly trades precision and robustness for search performance.

References:

- https://github.com/acoustid/chromaprint
- https://github.com/acoustid/chromaprint/blob/master/src/cmd/fpcalc.cpp
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/acoustid/chromaprint/master/LICENSE.md

Treat suitability for short speech windows and dynamic podcast editions as an empirical question. Review LGPL-related distribution obligations and the selected decoding/FFT dependencies before proposing iOS integration.

### Multi-evidence resolution

Evaluate separate acoustic windows before and after each anchor, plus distributed Listening Map nodes. Several verified nodes may act as an alignment spine that identifies where timeline offsets change. Require local evidence to agree with global episode order.

Compare at least:

1. timestamp and duration only
2. transcript quote/context matching
3. acoustic matching
4. fused transcript, acoustic, identity, and map evidence

## Resolution evidence classes

The spike should recommend a transport-neutral result vocabulary such as:

- exact edition
- acoustically verified
- transcript verified
- map interpolated
- ambiguous
- absent from recipient edition
- unresolved

Only evidence classes justified by the benchmark should be eligible for automatic inline cues. Preserve sender evidence even after a recipient-local position is resolved.

## Risks

- false confident placement beside the wrong argument
- repeated theme music, jingles, ads, or silence producing ambiguous matches
- publisher edits, time stretching, pitch changes, or replaced passages
- codec delay, resampling, window-boundary, and algorithm-version drift
- inability to decode protected or provider-owned playback
- CPU, battery, storage, and latency costs on representative devices
- licensing and App Store distribution obligations
- copyright and privacy questions for shared fingerprints and transcript excerpts
- a recipient possessing a genuinely absent edition-specific segment

## Spike outputs

- a benchmark corpus of paired episode editions with ground-truth alignment
- comparison results for all four resolution approaches
- measured placement error, false-placement rate, unresolved rate, ambiguity rate, runtime, and storage
- an omission check covering speech-only passages, dynamic pre/mid/post-roll ads, repeated material, silence edits, re-encoding, and publisher corrections
- recommended anchor evidence and resolution-result contracts
- licensing and platform feasibility note
- explicit go/no-go recommendation for Chromaprint and for automatic placement

## Decision rule

A resolver that declines difficult anchors may be acceptable. A resolver that confidently places a friend's reaction beside the wrong passage is not.

Do not advance to production until the benchmark defines an automatic-placement threshold, a runner-up/ambiguity policy, and a human-review fallback. The spike must report failures and unresolved cases rather than optimizing only average accuracy.

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Blocked by the stable minimum portable-package and durable-anchor boundary in #17.
- Findings may define a versioned optional machine-evidence extension without destabilizing the base package contract.
- Blocks full cross-edition podcast acceptance in #18; exact-edition and context-only import experiments may proceed independently.
- #21 may later supply approximate microphone-derived evidence; it does not block this spike.
- Do not add this to the active Recovery MVP.

labels.name: enhancement

body:
## Source

Product research on layered asynchronous co-op interjections, 2026-07-21.

## Outcome

After two or more people deliberately exchange commentary layers around a source, a user may request an AI-generated editorial synthesis that remains traceable to the contributing margins.

The synthesis is an attributed editorial artifact, not a participant, a consensus claim, or an invisible replacement for the original contributions.

## Product principles

- Preserve every person's original shared representation.
- Require explicit action before shared layers are included in synthesis.
- Distinguish recurring observations, independent rediscoveries, direct disagreements, unanswered questions, and novel connections.
- Link every material synthesis claim back to the specific source passage and contributing margin or margins.
- Represent uncertainty and attribution conflicts rather than resolving them silently.
- Never describe silence or omission as agreement.
- Label generated text and synthetic speech clearly.

## Proposed experience boundary

A user can choose:

- which imported and local layers participate
- whether audio transcripts, approved text, or both are used
- private local synthesis or a separately reviewed share revision
- whether names/display labels appear
- whether the result may be exported

The result must not mutate source packages, imported layers, or local interjections.

## Risks

- misattributing a statement to the wrong person
- laundering disagreement into apparent consensus
- treating semantically similar observations as identical
- exposing a private or muted contribution
- over-quoting copyrighted source material
- synthesizing from low-confidence or misresolved anchors
- losing provenance when models or prompts change
- presenting polished AI language as a participant's approved wording
- pressure to optimize engagement rather than understanding

## Research and acceptance evidence

- fixtures for agreement, rediscovery, contradiction, ambiguity, missing context, and unresolved anchors
- citation coverage from synthesis claims to source anchors and margin IDs
- tests proving excluded, muted, or private layers never enter provider context
- model/prompt/version provenance retained with the derived artifact
- review flow showing generated wording, attribution, and included sources before export
- failure behavior when anchors are unresolved or source context is insufficient
- comparison against a chronological, non-AI digest
- product-owner evaluation of whether synthesis adds understanding without erasing individual voices

## Non-goals

- automatic synthesis after every exchange
- claiming group consensus
- autonomous AI replies inserted into the conversation
- editing another participant's package
- public ranking, engagement scoring, or participant profiling

## Dependencies and sequencing

Blocked by #19 and the rights/provenance policy in #14. Cross-edition sources also require acceptable anchor-resolution evidence before source-grounded synthesis can be trusted.

body:
## Source

Product research on co-op interjections and federated sharing, 2026-07-21.

## Question

After Spoken Margins has a stable portable margin package and a validated one-way import/listen experience, does ActivityPub materially improve identity, discovery, delivery, or generic replies enough to justify operating a federated service?

ActivityPub is a possible transport topology. It must not become the canonical source-of-truth format for playback anchors or collaboration state.

## Prerequisite product model

The transport-neutral model should already define:

- source identity and source version evidence
- immutable margin package and package digest
- selected representations and redaction record
- authorship/display attribution
- imported commentary layer
- reply and package lineage
- audience and recipient-controlled reveal policy
- anchor-resolution evidence

The same model should remain transferable through Files, an encrypted link, AirDrop, or another relay.

## Current research

ActivityStreams provides standard objects and properties that could carry a readable fallback:

- `Note`
- `Audio`
- `OrderedCollection`
- `inReplyTo`
- `context`
- audience addressing

Web Annotation provides useful conceptual selectors for text quotes and media fragments.

References:

- https://www.w3.org/TR/activitypub/
- https://www.w3.org/TR/activitystreams-vocabulary/
- https://www.w3.org/TR/annotation-model/
- https://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags/

A Spoken Margins-aware client could fetch a rich margin manifest linked from an ordinary ActivityStreams object. Generic clients should only be expected to display the fallback Note, audio attachment, and link; they will not reliably implement custom anchor, reveal, or resolver semantics.

## Interoperability levels to evaluate

1. Spoken Margins to Spoken Margins: full package, anchor resolution, representations, and playback policy.
2. Spoken Margins to generic Fediverse client: readable text/audio/link fallback.
3. Generic text reply to Spoken Margins: reply associated with the originating margin where evidence permits.
4. Public comment interoperability with media-oriented servers only when the sender explicitly chooses public publication.

## Risks

- recipient addressing is not end-to-end encryption
- sender and recipient servers may access or retain private audio and metadata
- deletion, revocation, and remote-copy removal are best-effort
- custom JSON-LD terms may be ignored or transformed
- generic-client rendering and reply threading vary by implementation
- actor hosting introduces signing-key custody, delivery retries, abuse, moderation, blocking, reporting, storage, and availability responsibilities
- public audio and transcript excerpts introduce rights and consent concerns
- dedicated Spoken Margins actors may fragment identity from a user's existing account
- federation complexity may not be justified if real use remains one-to-one private exchange

## Research outputs

- transport comparison: Files/share sheet, encrypted link, CloudKit or relay, and ActivityPub
- minimal generic-client fallback object
- two-server interoperability experiment, if prerequisites are met
- privacy and server-trust threat model
- public, private-addressed, and application-encrypted delivery distinctions
- moderation and operational-responsibility inventory
- deletion/revocation behavior matrix
- recommendation: primary transport, optional adapter, or no-go

## Decision rule

ActivityPub should remain optional unless it produces value that the simpler transports cannot provide. Do not select it merely because the object vocabulary can represent Notes and Audio.

## Dependencies and sequencing

Blocked by #17 and #18. It must not block package exchange, imported commentary, or #19. Begin substantive transport selection only after the one-way experience has evidence of repeated user value.

labels.name: enhancement

body:
## Source

Product idea, 2026-07-21: a read-along or listen-along in which a recognized creator, educator, expert, or public figure shares selected interjections that can chime in beside a source.

## Product hypothesis

A curated commentary layer could be more engaging and educational than a conventional celebrity book club because the audience encounters the contributor's thinking at the exact source passages that prompted it.

The durable product concept is **creator commentary editions**, not celebrity access alone. Potential contributors include authors, teachers, researchers, journalists, subject-matter experts, reading groups, and public figures.

## Proposed experience

- A creator deliberately reviews and publishes a selected commentary layer.
- A recipient acquires or accesses the underlying source through their own lawful path.
- Spoken Margins resolves the commentary onto that source where evidence permits.
- The recipient chooses Fresh, Companion, or Guided reveal behavior.
- Every representation is attributed and clearly distinguished from the source and from AI-generated material.
- A context-only edition remains readable when the source cannot be acquired or an anchor cannot be resolved.

## Research questions

- Does inline commentary improve source completion, critical engagement, and recall compared with an interview, podcast episode, or end-of-source discussion?
- Which sources benefit from commentary and which become distracting?
- Should creators recommend a reveal mode, and how strongly should recipient control override it?
- What review and approval workflow is credible for a public contributor?
- How are creator identity, authorization, corrections, withdrawals, and representation provenance communicated?
- What business model avoids turning commentary into engagement clutter?
- How should paid, library, DRM-protected, region-limited, revised, or dynamically ad-inserted sources behave?
- Do users want commentary from one trusted person, multiple experts, or a curated sequence?

## Risks

- source, transcript, audio, publicity, or contributor rights are unclear
- a display label is mistaken for verified creator authorization
- creator commentary becomes promotional interruption rather than critical engagement
- public distribution magnifies anchor mistakes and stale editions
- the creator's raw or private recordings are exposed when only approved text/TTS was intended
- corrections and withdrawal cannot remove already downloaded copies
- recipients believe the source publisher endorsed an independent commentary edition
- accessibility and synthetic-voice disclosure are insufficient
- platform incentives drift toward celebrity ranking and engagement optimization
- commentary reduces the recipient's opportunity to form an independent interpretation

## Research outputs

- comparison with book clubs, director commentary, annotated editions, reaction media, and educational read-alongs
- one-source/one-creator prototype using the portable package path
- creator review and recipient preview scripts
- rights, attribution, and withdrawal checklist
- exact-edition, cross-edition, unavailable-source, and unresolved-anchor scenarios
- Fresh/Companion/Guided product study
- explicit evidence for whether the experience improves critical consumption rather than merely novelty

## Decision rule

Do not build creator accounts, a catalog, payment infrastructure, or public discovery until a bounded creator edition proves that recipients actually engage with both the source and the commentary.

## Dependencies

Blocked by #17 and #18. Rights/provenance policy comes from #14. Podcast editions that may differ across listeners depend on #27. #19 is optional unless the product includes participant replies or multiple commentary layers.

body:
## Source

Handwritten product note, 2026-07-21: “Abstract and register connections to DB and receive # of occurrences.”

Related concept note: a user privately reasons toward a meaningful connection, submits it only after making the leap, and receives prior-art/recurrence information plus proof of registration order. Rediscovery and novelty are both valuable.

## Outcome

From an interjection or completed listening session, a user can deliberately create a package of one or more connection claims, submit it to a registry after review, and receive:

- an immutable registration receipt
- server-observed order/time
- exact and similarity-based prior match counts
- links or identifiers for inspectable prior registrations where policy permits
- a clear distinction between “common broad connection” and “novel specific articulation”

The registry calibrates after submission; it must not autocomplete the interpretive leap beforehand.

## Native client contract

Add a transport-neutral domain boundary rather than embedding service calls in `Gate1AppModel`:

- `ConnectionClaimPackage`
  - package ID and schema version
  - source/interjection/session references
  - ordered claims from specific to abstract
  - raw user wording preserved verbatim
  - optional user-approved normalized wording
  - optional evidence references and derived-work references
  - visibility and redaction choices
  - optional device-key signature from #22
- `ConnectionRegistrationClient` protocol
  - submit
  - fetch receipt/status
  - retry idempotently
- durable local queue and receipt persistence in SessionKitPersistence
- a fake client and fixtures for deterministic tests

Keep provider/transport implementation outside core domain logic. A future remote service may live in another repository.

## Matching and epistemic requirements

- Preserve raw wording even when normalized representations are generated.
- Record match method and confidence; never collapse semantic similarity into an assertion of identity.
- Return match bands by claim level, not one flat count.
- Prevent trivial category matches from dominating results.
- Keep matching post-submission.
- Make model/version changes visible in receipts so historical results remain interpretable.
- Support user correction or withdrawal as a new append-only event; do not rewrite registration history silently.

## Privacy and abuse controls

- Default to minimal source excerpts and references rather than full source text.
- Preview exactly what is submitted.
- Use idempotency keys, strict rate limits, payload size limits, and duplicate-request protection.
- Separate public claim content from private local reasoning history.
- Do not require the full interjection audio or complete session export.
- Define retention, deletion/withdrawal, moderation, and appeal semantics before public launch.

## Acceptance evidence

- [ ] A reviewed claim package can be created from a selected interjection without mutating the source session.
- [ ] Offline submission queues once and retries idempotently without duplicate registrations.
- [ ] Receipts verify the submitted package digest and retain matcher/model versions.
- [ ] Fixtures cover exact match, close semantic match, broad-only recurrence, no match, rejected payload, rate limit, timeout, stale model, and withdrawn claim.
- [ ] UI distinguishes raw wording, normalized wording, registry result, and inference.
- [ ] No prior-art or suggestion result is fetched before the user confirms submission.
- [ ] Contract validation, SessionKit tests, persistence migration tests, privacy tests, and iOS build-for-testing pass.

## Non-goals

- No engagement feed, score farming, or novelty leaderboard.
- No claim that semantic matching establishes truth.
- No automatic publication of private conversations.
- No requirement to build the registry backend in this native repository.

## Sequencing and stopping rule

Post-Recovery-MVP. Begin with contracts, fixtures, fake transport, and a documented backend boundary. Do not add an automatic AI workflow or public social surface until the daily-driver loop is verified and human-validated.

title: [Spike] Use biometric signing as user-cost proof for sharing and connection registration

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: phase: post-mvp
labels.description: Explicitly outside the active Recovery MVP scope

labels.name: type: spike
labels.description: Bounded experiment ending in a go or no-go decision

labels.name: area: sharing
labels.description: Export, packages, import, and sharing boundaries

body:
## Source

Handwritten product note, 2026-07-21: “Authenticate an interjection using biometric proof / human connection.” Clarified intent: biometric signing is a lightweight proof-of-work or user-cost step applied when sharing interjections or registering connections.

## Corrected claim

Face ID or Touch ID does not prove a unique human identity. It can establish that a person successfully authorized a local operation with the enrolled device credential. Used deliberately, that interaction can add friction, bind a payload to a device-held key, and produce a verifiable receipt.

This is best described as **biometrically gated user-cost proof plus device-key signature**, not proof of humanity and not computational proof-of-work.

## Outcome

Before a user shares an interjection package or submits a connection claim for registration, the app may require an explicit biometric/passcode authorization. A Secure Enclave-backed key signs the canonical payload digest, producing a receipt that shows:

- the payload was finalized before authorization
- an enrolled user credential authorized use of this device key
- the signed bytes have not changed
- the operation incurred an intentional user interaction rather than occurring silently in bulk

## Intended integration points

### Sharing

- Optional or policy-required signature on the interjection package from #17.
- The share preview freezes the canonical payload before authentication.
- A successful signature is attached to the package or share receipt.
- Unsigned sharing may remain available for ordinary use; higher-trust destinations may require signing.

### Connection registration

- Optional or required signature on the connection claim package from #23.
- The registry may use a valid signature as one abuse-resistance signal and to make bulk unattended submissions harder.
- The registry must not treat one device key as one unique human.
- Server-side rate limits, duplicate detection, and moderation remain necessary.

## Proposed design

- Generate a P-256 signing key in the Secure Enclave when available.
- Protect key use with `userPresence` or an explicitly selected biometric access-control policy.
- Canonicalize and freeze the package before presenting authentication.
- Sign the package digest, not mutable UI text.
- Include public key, signature, algorithm, canonicalization version, payload digest, key ID, signing time, and authorization-policy identifier.
- Never export the private key.
- Treat biometric re-enrollment, key loss, device migration, unavailable Secure Enclave, and passcode fallback as explicit states.
- Define whether repeated submissions require fresh authorization or may use a short, visible grace interval.

## Threat model and limitations

This mechanism may help against accidental submission, invisible automation, and low-effort bulk posting from one device. It does not by itself prevent:

- many devices or many enrolled credentials
- compromised devices
- coerced authorization
- scripted workflows that still trigger user approval
- copied content signed by a legitimate device user
- false or low-quality claims

Do not market it as identity verification, Sybil resistance, truth verification, or authorship proof.

## UX requirements

- Authentication is shown only after the exact share or registration payload is reviewable.
- The prompt states the action being authorized and the payload digest or concise summary.
- Cancelled or failed authentication leaves local content unchanged.
- Verification labels say “authorized with this device key” or equivalent.
- Users can inspect whether a package or receipt is signed, unsigned, invalid, or signed by a changed/unknown key.
- Requiring biometric authorization must not block accessibility-compatible passcode fallback where policy allows.

## Acceptance evidence

- [ ] Canonicalization and signature verification are deterministic across fixtures.
- [ ] The private key cannot be exported through app code or diagnostics.
- [ ] Authentication occurs after payload freeze; editing any signed field requires a new signature.
- [ ] Cancel, lockout, unavailable biometry, changed enrollment, missing key, fallback, and unsupported-device states are tested.
- [ ] Signature verification works offline using the package public key.
- [ ] Tampering with any signed field invalidates verification.
- [ ] Automated repeated-share and repeated-registration tests prove that policy-required fresh authorization cannot be bypassed through normal app APIs.
- [ ] Threat-model documentation clearly separates interaction cost, device continuity, identity, anti-abuse value, and remaining attack paths.
- [ ] Security-sensitive key operations do not run on the UI actor.

## Non-goals

- Legal identity verification.
- Global uniqueness or “one human, one account.”
- Computational proof-of-work or cryptocurrency-style mining.
- Remote attestation that Apple or Spoken Margins endorses the content.
- Making biometrics mandatory for local capture, playback, or unsigned export unless a later policy explicitly requires it.

## Sequencing

Spike after #17 and #23 define canonical package bytes. Do not block the Recovery MVP, ordinary unsigned sharing, or local connection drafting.

title: [Spike] Anchor interjections to externally playing content with a rolling microphone buffer

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: phase: post-mvp
labels.description: Explicitly outside the active Recovery MVP scope

labels.name: type: spike
labels.description: Bounded experiment ending in a go or no-go decision

labels.description: Source, transcript, media-time, and cross-edition anchors

labels.name: area: rights
labels.description: Copyright, attribution, consent, provenance, and retention

body:
## Source

Handwritten product note, 2026-07-21: “3rd-party content listening + recording buffer → interject then transcribe.” Clarified intent: content is playing in another app or on another device while Spoken Margins records a rolling microphone buffer. When the interjection ends, the app transcribes roughly two minutes before and two minutes after the interjection to recover source context and create an approximate anchor.

## Question

Can Spoken Margins provide a useful, privacy-conscious, App-Store-safe foreground mode that anchors an interjection to externally playing content by continuously retaining only a bounded microphone buffer and transcribing a bounded context window around the interjection?

This is ambient capture, not direct access to another app’s audio session. The resulting anchor must be treated as approximate unless later matched to an acquired source or transcript.

## Intended workflow

1. The user explicitly starts an “External Listening” mode while content plays in another app or on another device.
2. Spoken Margins displays an unambiguous recording indicator and maintains a memory- or file-bounded rolling microphone buffer.
3. The user begins and records an interjection.
4. After the interjection ends, capture continues for a configurable post-roll, with an initial target of approximately two minutes.
5. The app extracts approximately two minutes of pre-roll plus two minutes of post-roll around the interjection, excluding or separately marking the user’s interjection audio.
6. Speech transcription produces surrounding content context.
7. The app stores the interjection with an approximate external-content anchor, confidence, timing metadata, and the retained context transcript.
8. If the user later supplies a URL, file, episode, or transcript, the app may attempt to resolve the approximate context to an exact source position without overwriting the original evidence.

## Product and platform constraints

- This mode requires explicit user initiation and a persistent visible recording state.
- It must not claim direct capture of another app’s protected or internal audio.
- Other-device playback and speaker playback from the same device are distinct acoustic cases and must be measured separately.
- Headphone playback may be inaudible to the microphone and therefore unsupported or degraded.
- Phone calls, private conversations, and covert background recording are outside scope.
- The user must be able to stop capture immediately and delete buffered audio.
- Rights, consent, jurisdiction, App Review, battery, thermal, and background-execution constraints require explicit review.

## Proposed domain boundary

Add an experimental external-context capture model with:

- capture session ID and explicit start/stop times
- rolling-buffer duration and retention policy
- interjection start/end monotonic timestamps
- pre-roll and post-roll durations actually retained
- device route and capture environment metadata
- raw context-audio retention state
- context transcript and transcription provenance
- approximate source label/reference supplied by the user
- anchor confidence and resolution state: `approximate`, `matched`, `ambiguous`, or `unresolved`
- optional later linkage to a canonical item/transcript anchor

Do not represent microphone-relative timing as exact media time in the external source.

## Spike outputs

- a decision record under `Contracts/docs/`
- a foreground prototype with a bounded ring buffer
- tests using content from another physical device and content from another app over speaker
- a headphone/route behavior matrix
- measured pre/post-roll accuracy, transcription quality, latency, storage, battery, and thermal impact
- separation behavior for source audio versus the spoken interjection
- privacy, consent, copyright, retention, and App Review analysis
- a recommended supported/degraded/rejected matrix
- follow-up production issues only if the spike produces an acceptable path

## Acceptance evidence

- [ ] No audio is retained before explicit mode activation.
- [ ] The rolling buffer never exceeds its documented duration or storage bound.
- [ ] Ending an interjection preserves the requested pre-roll and post-roll within measured tolerances.
- [ ] Cancel and Stop securely discard uncommitted buffered audio.
- [ ] The UI remains visibly in recording mode for the entire capture session.
- [ ] Tests distinguish same-device speaker, other-device speaker, headphones, silence, conversation contamination, and noisy environments.
- [ ] Approximate anchors are never silently presented as exact source positions.
- [ ] Later source matching preserves both the original approximate evidence and the resolved anchor.
- [ ] The spike ends with a go/no-go decision rather than production behavior hidden behind a toggle.

## Non-goals

- Bypassing DRM, platform privacy controls, or another app’s sandbox.
- Directly tapping another app’s audio stream.
- Recording calls or private conversations.
- Indefinite audio retention.
- Shipping a general-purpose recorder.

## Sequencing

Investigation only. Do not add this path to the active Recovery MVP or destabilize the existing import/share/playback spine.

## Build 26 reconciliation — 2026-09-08

The one-way foundation (#17/#18) is now integrated, internally distributed, and bounded-human-validated in Build 25, carried into Build 26. This does not implement or authorize co-op replies. Current release-lanes.md requires a later product-owner release decision for this issue; #26 synthesis is also outside the lane. Historical implementation claims must not be read as evidence of this conversation workflow.

Evidence: [scope-specific record](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/docs/release-lanes.md), [owner acceptance](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/gate-1/2026-09-08-build-26-acceptance.md), [Build 26 handoff](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-26/build-26-testflight-upload.md).

Build identity: **0.1 (26)**, exact source `9c967793e7a0e86c26a3030390818e87d830723b`; release manifest is **verified** (425 app/adapter/UI tests plus fast checks). The owner recorded **human_validated for the candidate**, without a separate device-by-device or individual-flow matrix. Internal Margins distribution is confirmed; Build 21 remains external. #14 and later-release authorization are unchanged.

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Source

Handwritten product note, 2026-07-21: “Co-op interjections: layered asynchronous conversation.”

## Outcome

Two or more people can exchange immutable commentary layers around the same source, reply to specific interjections, and listen through the resulting conversation without creating a single mutable shared transcript or requiring simultaneous playback.

## Product principle

The source remains the common spine. Each participant owns a separate layer. Replies create lineage; they do not rewrite the parent package. The receiving user decides which layers are enabled and how they influence or interrupt playback.

This collaboration model is transport-neutral. Files/share sheet should be sufficient to validate it; a cloud relay or ActivityPub adapter may deliver the same immutable packages later.

## Proposed contract additions

Extend the package/import work from #17 and #18 with:

- `conversationId` scoped to a package lineage, not a global account
- `parentPackageDigest`
- `replyToInterjectionId` or `replyToPackageScopedId`
- participant display label and optional signer key ID
- monotonic package creation time plus local receipt time
- explicit fork/merge metadata when one package replies to several prior packages
- deterministic ordering rules that do not depend on server arrival order

Imported content remains immutable. Local mute, hide, and playback policy are separate state.

## Playback and UI behavior

- Present layers as a stack with participant labels, verification state, and reply lineage.
- Let users listen chronologically by source anchor or follow a reply thread.
- Preserve each recipient's Fresh, Companion, or Guided reveal policy from #18.
- Provide explicit modes for pause-and-play commentary, commentary-only review, and source-with-selected-layers.
- Always make it clear whether audio is the source, another participant, or an AI-generated turn.
- Return to the exact source position after commentary; never cascade into duplicate resumes.

## Exchange model

Start with package exchange through Files/share sheet. Define a transport boundary so a later encrypted link, CloudKit/service relay, or ActivityPub adapter can deliver the same immutable packages. Do not make remote sync or federation a prerequisite for validating the conversation model.

## Future attributed synthesis

AI editorial synthesis is tracked separately in #26. It must cite contributing margins, preserve disagreement and uncertainty, and require explicit user action. It is not part of the minimum co-op conversation.

## Acceptance evidence

- [ ] A participant can reply to a specific imported interjection and export a child package without altering the parent.
- [ ] A recipient can import parent and child packages in either order and reconstruct the same lineage.
- [ ] Duplicate, missing-parent, forked, conflicting-label, and invalid-signature states are explicit and tested.
- [ ] Source-order and thread-order playback are deterministic.
- [ ] Muting or deleting one local layer never mutates or deletes another layer or local interjection.
- [ ] Backgrounding, route changes, and lock-screen transport preserve source ownership and resume position.
- [ ] Package fixtures, persistence migrations, SessionKit tests, UI tests, and iOS build-for-testing pass.
- [ ] Product-owner validation shows at least one conversation continuing beyond the initial one-way exchange.

## Non-goals

- No engagement feed, likes, follower graph, read receipts, typing indicators, or presence status.
- No collaborative editing of another person's words.
- No AI-generated reply inserted without a clear actor label and explicit user action.
- No dependency on ActivityPub research in #25.
- No AI synthesis dependency for the basic conversation.

## Dependencies and stopping rule

Blocked by #17 and #18. Do not implement before the Recovery MVP is human-validated and one-way imported commentary has passed bounded device checks. Blocks the attributed synthesis work in #26.

The bounded Ajeya Cotra exchange, reconstruction, and provisional-to-matched flow are human_validated in Build 25 and included in Build 26. Claims that recipient behavior exists only on local codex/sharingV1 are historical. Remaining negative-path/device matrix and #14 external gate remain open; no external release is implied.

Internal Margins distribution is confirmed; Build 21 remains external. #14 and later-release authorization are unchanged.

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Source

Handwritten product note, 2026-07-21: “Listen w/ other’s interjections.”

Additional product research identifies recipient-controlled reveal as central: even announcing that another person commented on a passage can influence what the recipient notices.

## Outcome

A user can import a trusted interjection package and hear or read those notes at their resolved source positions while retaining control over playback and influence. Imported notes remain a separate, removable layer and never overwrite local session data.

## Repository fit

Spoken Margins already has durable source/session/interjection anchors, transcript-backed media timelines, source-link intake, and a persistent playback spine. Build imported commentary as a layer over those primitives rather than flattening it into local interjections or source text.

## Proposed domain model

Add an imported commentary layer with:

- layer ID, package digest, display label, import time, and verification state
- immutable imported interjection records
- source identity and source-resolution status
- retained sender anchor evidence
- recipient-local anchor-resolution result and evidence class
- local enable/mute/delete state
- playback/reveal policy stored locally, not imposed by the imported package

Do not assign imported package IDs directly as local primary keys. Preserve package lineage and map to local IDs.

## Source and anchor resolution

- Resolve by canonical source reference and normalized episode/article identity.
- Prefer exact-edition identity or durable transcript/text evidence.
- Treat sender media time as a hint when podcast editions may differ.
- Fall back to context-only reading when the source cannot be acquired or resolution is ambiguous.
- Never silently auto-place an ambiguous margin.
- Preserve both original sender evidence and recipient-local resolution.
- Never auto-download or autoplay a newly imported package.

Cross-edition podcast research and evidence policy are tracked in #27.

## Recipient-controlled reveal modes

Names are provisional and should be product-tested:

- **Fresh:** experience the source without advance markers; reveal margins after a chapter or after finishing.
- **Companion:** receive a subtle cue and choose whether to open the margin.
- **Guided:** explicitly permit selected margins to play inline as commentary.

The recipient chooses the active mode. A sender may suggest a mode but cannot force it. The default should be selected through product evidence rather than assumed.

## Listening UX

- Show imported layers separately from “My interjections.”
- Let the user enable, mute, or remove each layer.
- Make the current speaker/layer and return-to-source behavior unambiguous.
- Imported audio must not seize Now Playing ownership from the canonical source unexpectedly.
- Return to the resolved source position exactly once after commentary.
- Offer context-only reading for unresolved or unavailable sources.

## Acceptance evidence

- [ ] A valid package from #17 imports without replacing the active item, session, screen, or playback state.
- [ ] Exact, adjusted, context-only, unresolved, invalid-digest, duplicate, absent-edition, and deleted-layer states have fixtures and tests.
- [ ] Imported notes remain distinct from local notes in persistence and export.
- [ ] Layer enable/mute/delete actions are reversible and do not delete source or session data.
- [ ] Fresh, Companion, and Guided modes are distinguishable and recipient controlled.
- [ ] Playback resumes at the correct source position after an imported note under every supported policy.
- [ ] Route changes, backgrounding, lock-screen controls, and repeated note boundaries do not create duplicate playback or wrong-source audio.
- [ ] Contract validation, SessionKit tests, iOS build-for-testing, and bounded device checks pass.
- [ ] The product owner validates at least one complete one-sender/one-recipient exchange before layered conversation work begins.

## Non-goals

- No remote synchronization or account requirement in the first implementation.
- No algorithmic recommendation of commentary layers.
- No automatic trust based only on a display name.
- No requirement to choose ActivityPub or another remote transport.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the portable reviewed package contract in #17.
- Cross-edition automatic podcast placement depends on an acceptable result from #27; exact-edition and context-only flows may proceed independently.
- Rights and provenance rules come from #14.
- Blocks #19 and #25.
- Creator commentary editions in #24 depend on this bounded one-way experience.

Original/cleaned/text representation choices must follow the current release contract, not superseded 2026-08-22 defaults.

Evidence: [scope-specific record](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-25/build-25-testflight-upload.md), [owner acceptance](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/gate-1/2026-09-08-build-26-acceptance.md), [Build 26 handoff](https://github.com/uncomposed/spoken-margins-native/blob/fdbceda0dd840a541653ac6fe84957ffd6bec704/artifacts/validation/testflight-external/build-26/build-26-testflight-upload.md).

Internal Margins distribution is confirmed; Build 21 remains external. #14 and later-release authorization are unchanged.

The original report and checklist below are preserved for scope/history. Unchecked historical boxes are not newly observed failures or fabricated individual test results; the current disposition is the reconciliation above.

---

## Source

Handwritten product note, 2026-07-21: “Sharing interjections → AI social engagement.” Clarified intent: sharing is the primary feature; the social-media idea is that an AI can more easily turn a selected interjection and its source context into a draft post.

Additional product research distinguishes the immutable private capture from a separately reviewed share revision.

## Outcome

A user can deliberately package and share one or more interjections without exposing the whole local session. The user may optionally ask their ChatBot to generate a social-ready draft from the selected interjection, source attribution, and bounded anchor context.

The app shares an inspectable package or user-approved rendered representation. It does not publish directly to a social network by default.

## Product boundary

### Private capture

The local capture may retain raw audio, raw transcription, cleaned transcription, source anchors, and other private session evidence according to local retention policy.

### Reviewed share revision

The sender selects what will represent them:

- original raw recording
- a separate re-recording
- raw transcript
- edited or approved transcript
- text-only representation
- TTS generated from approved text
- omitted/private interjection

Selecting one representation must not silently upload the others. TTS and materially AI-edited wording require visible provenance and disclosure. The private capture remains unchanged when a share revision is created.

A “Preview as recipient” step should show the selected representation, source context, attribution, reveal suggestion, and every field or attachment that will leave the device.

## Repository fit

The current app already exports a selected interjection with source anchors and supports Markdown/JSON session handoff. This issue formalizes a smaller share boundary and optional drafting step rather than introducing a feed, account system, or social backend.

## Proposed share contract

Add a canonical `spoken-margins.interjection-package.v1` containing:

- package ID, schema version, creation time, and deterministic content digest
- one or more interjections with stable local IDs and package-scoped IDs
- source identity: canonical URL/reference, title, media type, publisher/author when known
- target and durable anchor evidence sufficient for later resolution
- selected user-approved representation and provenance
- optional audio attachment only when selected
- optional AI response or summary excerpts selected explicitly
- optional author display label; no hidden device/account identifiers
- rights/copyright warning metadata and source-material inclusion flags
- redaction record showing fields omitted before export
- optional parent package digest for later reply/fork lineage
- optional sender reveal-mode suggestion that never overrides recipient policy

The lossless package is JSON. Human-readable Markdown or plain text may accompany it.

Do not freeze a cross-edition acoustic shape until #27 reports which evidence is useful. The package must remain transport-neutral; ActivityPub research is tracked separately in #25.

## Privacy and consent UX

Before export, show exactly which fields leave the device:

- interjection text/transcript
- source reference and anchor excerpt
- audio, if selected
- AI-generated content, if selected
- author label, if entered
- synthetic-voice or AI-edit provenance
- source-material and rights warnings

Default to the minimum useful package. Never include API keys, diagnostics, full source text, unrelated turns, precise private filesystem paths, or unselected raw representations.

## Acceptance evidence

- [ ] A selected interjection can be exported and re-imported byte-for-byte at the contract layer.
- [ ] Digest verification detects modification and produces a clear invalid-package state.
- [ ] Default export excludes audio, full source text, diagnostics, unrelated session data, and unselected representations.
- [ ] The preview accurately lists every included field and attachment.
- [ ] Raw, re-recorded, edited-text, text-only, and disclosed-TTS share revisions have fixtures.
- [ ] Draft fixtures cover short post, thread outline, long-form reflection, attribution, insufficient context, and copyrighted-excerpt limits.
- [ ] Share cancellation and destination failure leave the local session unchanged.
- [ ] Contract validation, export/import tests, privacy tests, AI prompt tests, and iOS build-for-testing pass.

## Non-goals

- No public timeline, follower graph, reactions, ranking, or engagement optimization.
- No direct social-network account integration in the first implementation.
- No remote mutable document.
- No claim that package authorship proves a legal identity.
- No requirement that typed interjections from #15 exist before voice/transcript sharing.

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Post-Recovery-MVP foundation.
- Rights and provenance policy comes from #14.
- Findings from #27 inform cross-edition machine evidence.
- Blocks #18 and #25.
- #15 should be representable later but does not block the initial package.
- Device signing in #22 remains optional and must not block ordinary unsigned sharing.
