body:
## Build 27 scope reconciliation — September 12, 2026

Existing session/selected-note export flows retain the owner's Build 27 checklist acceptance, except the detail Copy with Context feedback problem in #109. Keep open for the September 11 Configure Margin Output expansion, named destination profiles and its Obsidian/non-Obsidian acceptance; these new requirements were not part of the accepted candidate. Bounded sharing policy #14 is accepted.

The owner accepted the checklist except six named failures and requested GitHub reconciliation on September 12. Acceptance is owner-reported Build 27, with no inferred exact installed SHA or device-by-device matrix. Original scope is preserved below; later feature expansions and explicit research measurements are not silently marked complete. Evidence: local `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md`.

---

## Product-owner expansion — 2026-09-11: configurable notes/PKM destinations

Extend the portable export work into an explicit **Configure Margin Output** workflow so a listener can decide where their Margins and anchors should go after capture/review.

The key product requirement is not an Obsidian-only integration. Spoken Margins should preserve one canonical Markdown/JSON export contract and allow destinations to consume it.

### Destination profiles

Allow the user to configure one or more named output destinations, for example:

- a user-selected folder that may be an Obsidian vault/subfolder;
- the system share sheet for apps such as Notion and other notes/PKM tools;
- another Files-compatible notes directory;
- later, an explicitly authorized vendor adapter where a notes app requires its own API/authentication.

Each destination profile should declare:

- supported format(s): Markdown and/or JSON;
- scope: selected Margin, current item Margins, or complete session;
- destination/location identity without storing unsafe transient paths;
- naming/template policy;
- whether source anchors/context are included;
- whether cleaned/summarized text or original transcript is preferred where both exist;
- whether export is manual-only or eligible for a later explicit automation policy.

Do not make successful note capture dependent on a third-party service. Portable files remain the canonical boundary.

### Margin + anchor output

A notes export should be useful without reopening Spoken Margins. At minimum, preserve:

- Margin text/transcript/approved cleaned form;
- source title and canonical source reference;
- durable source anchor evidence (chapter/text range/media time/transcript context as applicable);
- bounded before/after context where available and permitted;
- creation time and provenance;
- optional Spoken Margins backlink/deep link;
- AI-response/derivative linkage when the Margin was made on an assistant turn rather than directly on source content.

The destination format must not flatten an AI-turn Margin onto the original source position; #112 owns that coordinate-space correctness.

### User experience

- Expose **Configure Margin Output** from Settings and from the onboarding/setup walkthrough (#69).
- Provide a test export so the user can verify that the selected destination receives a representative note before relying on it.
- Make failed/revoked destination access visible and recoverable without losing the Margin.
- Allow the user to change or disable a destination without rewriting prior exports.
- Prefer a simple portable workflow first. Direct Notion/other vendor API synchronization should be a separate adapter layer only if the file/share route cannot meet the product need.

### Added acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can configure a persistent Markdown destination in a user-selected Obsidian-compatible folder and successfully test-export a Margin with anchors.
- [ ] A user can send the same canonical Margin export through the system share sheet to another notes/PKM app such as Notion without an Obsidian-specific schema.
- [ ] Destination configuration survives relaunch without storing invalid raw security-scoped paths.
- [ ] Revoked folder access is detected and recoverable through re-selection; no Margin data is lost.
- [ ] Selected-Margin, item-scoped, and session-scoped exports can reuse the same configured destination/profile where appropriate.
- [ ] Export includes enough durable anchor/provenance data to identify where the thought occurred without exporting full copyrighted source content by default.
- [ ] AI-turn Margins retain assistant-turn identity and do not masquerade as source-relative notes.
- [ ] Onboarding (#69) can open this same production configuration surface and run a test export.
- [ ] Product-owner validation covers an Obsidian folder workflow and a non-Obsidian notes-app workflow.

---

## Source

Handwritten product note, 2026-07-21: “Interjections to PKM, e.g. Obsidian.” PKM means personal knowledge management.

## Outcome

A user can export a selected interjection, all interjections on a target, or a complete session as durable Markdown/JSON files and send them through the system share sheet or to a user-selected export folder. Obsidian should work well, but the contract must remain tool-neutral.

## Current implementation status

Build 9 contains substantial session-level export work. Keep implementation, automated verification, and product-owner validation distinct.

### Implemented and automated-test verified

- Complete sessions can be rendered as Markdown or JSON from the existing session-isolated export spine.
- A session Markdown export is prepared as a named `.md` file and can be sent through the iOS system share sheet.
- Multiple selected sessions can be saved as one Markdown file per session to a user-selected folder.
- The chosen batch-export folder is retained with a security-scoped bookmark.
- Export filenames are deterministic and filesystem-safe.
- Filename collisions do not silently overwrite existing files; the writer adds a numeric suffix.
- Batch export reports per-session successes and failures.
- Selected-interjection and target-scoped Markdown/JSON generation already exist as clipboard operations.
- Focused tests cover deterministic filenames, collision handling, and the batch session-to-folder workflow.
- The Build 9 contract validators, surface-contract validator, SessionKit test build, and release builds passed.

### Implemented but not yet product-owner validated for this issue

- Named Markdown session files through the system share sheet.
- Batch Markdown export to a remembered folder.
- Opening exported files in Obsidian and a generic text editor.
- iPhone and iPad behavior, including cancellation and revoked folder access.

### Remaining implementation

- Export a selected interjection as a named shareable file, not only clipboard text.
- Export current-target interjections as a named shareable file, not only clipboard text.
- Save selected-interjection and target-scoped exports to the chosen export folder.
- Export JSON as a named file and support lossless JSON folder export where appropriate.
- Make folder permission revocation, stale bookmarks, and re-selection explicit and recoverable.
- Complete the proposed stable front matter and provenance/rights metadata audit.
- Add stable selected, target, and full-session fixtures covering every supported anchor and provenance field.
- Add focused failure coverage for permission loss, disk failure, cancellation, and playback non-interference.
- Add bounded iPhone/iPad UI evidence for share-sheet and folder-export flows.

## Markdown and interchange shape

Use stable front matter plus readable body content:

- schema version and stable interjection/session/item IDs
- source title, canonical URL/reference, media type, and optional author/publisher
- target type and target ID
- creation time and capture provenance
- text/transcript and optional cleaned text
- before/after source anchors, chapter, transcript segment, media time, and playback rate where available
- optional AI response or summary linkage
- optional backlink/deep link into Spoken Margins
- content-rights/copyright warning metadata when relevant

Preserve raw JSON as the lossless interchange format.

## Acceptance evidence

- [ ] Exported Markdown opens cleanly in Obsidian and a generic text editor.
- [ ] JSON round-trips every supported anchor and provenance field without loss.
- [ ] Selected, target, and full-session scopes produce stable fixtures.

## Source

Handwritten product note, 2026-07-21: “Typed interjections for places users don’t want to speak.”

## Outcome

While listening to a source or generated turn, a user can pause at the current position, type an interjection, save it against the same canonical anchor used by recorded interjections, and resume exactly once from the preserved position.

## Repository fit

The existing flow in `Gate1AppModel.beginInterjection()` captures a playback anchor, pauses streaming speech, records audio, then schedules transcription. `Contracts/schemas/interjection.schema.json` currently requires an `audio` object and a transcription status, so typed capture should be modeled explicitly rather than represented as fake or discarded audio.

- `captureKind`: `voice` or `text`
- canonical user-authored `body`
- optional `audio` representation for voice capture
- optional transcript/cleaned transcript derived from audio
- preserved `anchor`, `targetType`, `targetId`, source/session IDs, and creation time

- Add a “Type” alternative beside the record control.
- Capture the anchor before presenting the editor.
- Keep playback paused while editing; Save resumes according to the pre-interjection state, Cancel restores without creating a record.
- Support source text, transcript-backed media, assistant turns, and summary turns.
- Expose the same copy/export/delete affordances as voice interjections.

body:
## Build 27 owner reconciliation — September 12, 2026

**Bounded direct-sharing policy accepted by the product owner on September 12, 2026**, following review of `docs/external-testflight-sharing-decision.md` and the walkthrough. The accepted policy covers reviewed representations and provenance, bounded inspectable excerpts, explicit voice choice, disclosed default-on acoustic matching with effective opt-out, recipient-supplied source, and complete embedded linkless text only for app-authored content or explicit sender rights confirmation. It preserves disclosure of independent map/text-derived artifacts, unsigned identity, and the inability to revoke recipient copies. The exact sender/recipient wording in that document is accepted.

This supersedes older statements that the bounded beta policy has not been accepted. It does not confer legal permission for individual material. Keep this research issue open for public/commercial/federated uses and source-specific questions outside that decision. Policy acceptance is separate from product acceptance: the two-Margin share regression remains open in #17, and exact-candidate release/internal/external requirements still apply.

The product owner reported using **Build 27** on September 11, accepted all checklist flows except six named problems, and explicitly requested this issue reconciliation on September 12, 2026. Only accepted portions above are **human_validated by owner report**; listed exceptions remain pending. The report is aggregate acceptance; no separate device/OS matrix or exact installed commit is invented. Subsequent local repairs are not covered by that acceptance.

Evidence: `artifacts/validation/internal-external-readiness/build-27-owner-validation.md` and the second-edition/current owner checklists in the local workspace. No upload, external approval, or source-baseline promotion is claimed. Original issue text/checklists are preserved below as history; unchecked historical boxes are not a claim that accepted behavior is still failing.

---

## Source

Apple Podcasts adds source attribution and the warning “This material may be protected by copyright” when a user copies a transcript excerpt.

Example observed by the product owner:

> From Odd Lots: The Creator of Claude Code on The Hottest Piece of Software in the World, Jul 20, 2026  
> https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/odd-lots/id1056200096?i=1000777521827&r=1547  
> This material may be protected by copyright.

## Question

What attribution, excerpt-limiting, warning, consent, and retention policy should apply when Spoken Margins exports or shares source context, transcript excerpts, fingerprints, recorded commentary, AI-derived text, or creator commentary editions?

This issue records policy and research. It does not assert that a warning alone creates permission or resolves copyright questions.

## Typed policy layers

Keep these distinct:

- **Source provenance:** title, author/publisher, canonical URL, episode/feed identity, publication date, and source type.
- **Included source material:** transcript quotation, before/after anchor context, full source text, audio excerpt, or acoustic fingerprint.
- **User contribution:** raw audio, transcript, edited text, re-recording, or approved TTS.
- **AI-derived material:** cleaned wording, summary, or co-op synthesis.
- **Destination and audience:** private export, direct recipient, PKM file, federated delivery, public post, or commercial creator edition.
- **Retention and revocation:** local originals, exported copies, server-hosted assets, deletion, and withdrawal expectations.

## Research questions

- What minimum source attribution should accompany each exported or shared representation?
- What bounded transcript/source context is necessary for human interpretation and anchor resolution?
- When should the app show a copyright warning or require explicit inclusion?
- Should full source text and source-audio excerpts always default to excluded?
- How should publisher-provided transcript licenses or terms be represented?
- Are compact acoustic fingerprints legally or contractually distinguishable from shared audio excerpts?
- How should synthetic voice and AI-edited wording be disclosed?
- What additional permissions are needed for public or commercial creator commentary editions?
- Which questions require qualified legal review rather than product inference?

## Risks

- implying that attribution or a warning establishes permission
- exporting more source content than needed for the user-selected purpose
- losing source provenance during package forks or AI transformation
- sharing raw voice audio when the sender selected only text or TTS
- public recipients redistributing material beyond the intended audience
- best-effort deletion being presented as guaranteed revocation
- model-generated wording obscuring who authored or approved a claim
- terms or rights differing across publishers, providers, countries, and source types

## Required outputs

- a source-attribution and excerpt policy matrix by destination
- default inclusion/exclusion rules for every representation
- warning and explicit-consent triggers
- provenance fields required in portable packages and exports
- synthetic-voice and AI-edit disclosure language
- deletion, withdrawal, and remote-copy limitations
- an escalation list for legal review
- fixtures demonstrating minimal private export, direct share, public post, and creator edition

## Dependencies

This policy informs #16, #17, #18, #21, #24, #26, and #27. Downstream issues may continue product research, but public or externally distributed behavior must not invent conflicting rights rules independently.

## Reported behavior

On the welcome/native-text item, changing voice or increasing speaking rate caused the scrubber to advance through the content without audible playback. Leaving and re-entering the listening screen did not stop the advancing position; restarting the app was the only observed recovery.

## Expected behavior

- A rate change affects active native-text speech without converting progress into a timer detached from audible output.
- Changing voice or rate never advances source position unless corresponding source audio is actually played.
- Leaving the full listening screen preserves valid playback state.
- Pause/stop/re-entry can recover without restarting the app.
- Resume begins from the last audibly supported source position.

## Relationship to prior issue

Closed #11 tracked playback speed being ignored and interjection causing native text to skip to the end. This report was filed after #11 closed, so treat it as a possible regression or incomplete closure rather than marking it duplicate without evidence.

## Triage evidence needed

- build number and commit SHA
- iPhone/iPad model and OS version
- selected voice and voice runtime
- starting and changed playback rates
- whether audio was audible before and after the change
- whether the app was foregrounded, backgrounded, or on another screen
- snapshot/diagnostic values for playback status, target, source position, audio position, and prepared-audio state
- a short screen recording if reproducible

- [ ] Reproduce or falsify on the current build using the welcome item.

- [ ] Confirm source position never outruns the last audibly confirmed position.
- [ ] Confirm changing rate while playing, paused, and starting.
- [ ] Confirm navigation away and back does not leave a phantom progress loop.

This blocks Recovery MVP human validation if reproducible. Wrong or silent playback position is a stopping-rule failure, not a cosmetic scrubber defect.

Possibly related to #10, but this issue tracks playback speed handling and interject skip-to-end behavior specifically.

title: Bug: native text playback falls back from Piper voice, stalls, then loses resume position

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
## Summary
During native text playback, audio initially starts in the selected Piper text-to-speech voice, but after some pre-rendered/cached audio appears to run out, playback pauses, falls back to the default non-Siri/non-Piper voice for an extended stretch, then eventually stops. When exiting and returning, Resume restarts from the beginning instead of the prior playback position. After reopening, playback may use the Piper voice again, but the user has to manually seek back to where playback stopped.

## Observed behavior
1. Start playback of native text using Piper text-to-speech.
2. Playback begins correctly with the Piper voice.
3. After some time, likely when the pre-rendered audio cache is exhausted, playback pauses briefly.
4. Playback resumes using the default non-Siri/non-Piper system voice instead of Piper.
5. Playback continues in that fallback voice for several minutes.
6. After roughly five minutes, playback stops.
7. Exiting and returning to the screen, then pressing Resume, restarts playback from the beginning rather than the last position.
8. After reopening, playback starts in the Piper voice again, but the user must manually navigate back to the prior position.

## Expected behavior
- Native text playback should continue fluidly in the selected Piper voice for the entire session.
- If audio generation, pre-rendering, or cache refill lags, playback should buffer or recover without silently switching to an unintended fallback voice.
- Resume should restore the last known playback position after exiting and returning.
- Playback should not stop after several minutes unless the content is complete or the user stops it.
- Native text audio playback should approach feature parity with Speech Central for continuity, resume reliability, and voice consistency.

## Impact
This makes long-form native text playback unreliable. The user has to repeatedly exit, re-enter, and manually seek to recover the Piper voice and continue playback, which is significantly less fluid than expected for native text audio playback.

## Repro notes
- Reproduced across approximately five attempts.
- The failure pattern appears tied to a boundary where cached or pre-rendered Piper audio may run out.
- Voice fallback appears to be to a default system voice rather than the configured Piper voice.

## Areas to investigate
- Piper audio pre-render/cache exhaustion behavior.
- Queue refill timing and whether playback falls through to a system TTS provider.
- Guardrails preventing unintended voice/provider switching mid-session.
- Playback state persistence and Resume position restoration.
- Stop condition after several minutes of fallback/system-voice playback.

## Acceptance criteria
- Playback remains in Piper voice across cache/pre-render boundaries.
- No unintended fallback to system voice occurs without explicit user-facing error handling.
- Playback position is persisted frequently enough that Resume restores the last meaningful position after leaving and returning.
- Long-form native text playback can continue beyond five minutes without stopping unexpectedly.
- Add regression coverage or instrumentation around provider selection, queue refill, and resume-position persistence.
